Dayang boosts efficiency by 80% with AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO processors, 
powering real-time 8K editing, AR workflows, and advanced 3D modeling.
Dayang Technology develops advanced video production systems that serve the fast-changing 
needs of the media and entertainment industry. Its solutions power real-time broadcasting, 
augmented reality (AR), ultra-high-definition (UHD) video production, and detailed 3D 
modeling. Flagship systems like the D-Cube-Edit 5 editing platform and the Xuanmiao 
Virtual Studio System are designed to handle the complexities of modern media 
workflows, enabling creators to work efficiently and deliver high-quality results.
“AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO processors have helped us achieve what was 
previously impossible—real-time rendering and 8K production with fewer 
resources and greater precision.”
Qingyu Zhu, General Manager, Dayang Post-Production Products Division
As the industry evolves, Dayang customers need systems capable of handling increasingly 
complex workflows. For Dayang, the question became: How could they stay ahead of 
customer needs by addressing the performance bottlenecks and scalability challenges 
imposed by ever more demanding processing requirements? The search for a solution led 
Dayang to adopt AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO 7000 WX-Series processors—specifically 
the 7955WX and 7975WX models—integrated within Lenovo Thinkstation P8 workstations. 
FACING THE ESCALATING CHALLENGES OF MODERN MEDIA PRODUCTION
Despite its stellar reputation for delivering reliable solutions, Dayang faced significant 
challenges as media production workflows grew more demanding. Customers required 
systems capable of real-time 4K and 8K editing, multi-camera synchronization, and  
AR production. Advanced workflows, such as physically-based rendering (PBR) for 3D 
modeling, placed immense strain on legacy hardware, which struggled to provide  
the necessary computational power for tasks like real-time light simulation and  
texture rendering.
“We could run 4K or 8K content, but monitoring real-time effects in ultra-high definition 
was a challenge,” said Qingyu Zhu, General Manager of Dayang’s Post-Production Products 
Division. “Our previous processors struggled to deliver the performance our customers 
needed for high-quality documentaries and live production workflows.”
These limitations forced customers to rely on inefficient proxy workflows, duplicating files 
and delaying production timelines. Additionally, high-profile projects like international 
sporting events demanded systems capable of real-time performance at enormous scales, 
further exposing the shortcomings of available processing platforms. The company needed 
a scalable, high-performance platform capable of handling modern media production’s 
technical and operational demands while enabling future growth.

DRIVING PERFORMANCE AND VERSATILITY WITH  
AMD RYZEN™ THREADRIPPER™ PRO CPUS
Faced with these challenges, Dayang evaluated several hardware 
solutions and ultimately selected AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 
processors for their performance and scalability. “We tested 
various solutions ahead of the Beijing Winter Olympics, where 
8K content needed to be processed in real time,” said Dong 
Chang, Deputy Manager of Dayang’s Studio Division. “The AMD 
Ryzen Threadripper PRO 7000 Series stood out with its “Zen 4” 
architecture and AVX-512 support, delivering a 12% performance 
gain in decoding and encoding tasks. This improvement was crucial 
for meeting our goals.”
“With AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO CPUs, our 
customers can now perform real-time UHD processing, 
improving their efficiency by more than 80% compared 
to previous post-production solutions.”
Dong Chang, Deputy Manager, Dayang Studio Division
The scalability of AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO processors, with 
core counts ranging from 12 to 96, allowed Dayang to optimize 
performance for a wide range of workflows. For PBR tasks, Ryzen 
Threadripper PRO provided the processing power necessary for 
realistic light simulations, texture rendering, and interactive 
3D modeling. The platform also addressed inefficiencies in 
multi-camera workflows, enabling customers to process up 
to 20 simultaneous 4K streams without delays. “AMD Ryzen 
Threadripper PRO CPUs offer a great range of core counts,” noted 
Dong Chang. “This flexibility is ideal for meeting our customers’ 
wide variety of demands for rendering and 3D modeling.”
BOOSTING EFFICIENCY AND PRECISION IN MEDIA PRODUCTION 
AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO processors provided the multi
threading capabilities and high clock speeds necessary to eliminate 
bottlenecks in UHD video production, multi-camera editing, 
and PBR workflows. By integrating AMD Ryzen Threadripper 
PRO CPUs, Dayang enabled its customers to achieve real-time 
performance for even the most demanding projects.
With the AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 7975WX processor, 
Dayang’s systems now support nearly double the 11 streams of 
4K 50P real-time decoding for the XAVC 500M format supported 
by the previous competing platform. This improvement has 
significantly reduced production delays and enabled faster 
turnaround times. “With AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO CPUs, our 
customers can now perform real-time UHD processing, improving 
their efficiency by more than 80% compared to previous post
production solutions,” said Dong Chang.
The AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 7955WX processor’s 
advantages over the competitor’s processors were particularly 
evident to Dayang in PBR workflows, where complex 3D models 
require exceptional rendering precision. In Dayang’s experience, 
the single Ryzen Threadripper PRO 7955WX processor delivers 
smoother frame transitions during camera panning in AR 
composite images, eliminating the stuttering experienced with 
competing platforms. This top-of-the-line performance positions 
Dayang’s solutions as industry leaders for real-time rendering and 
immersive media production.
“The AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO 7000 Series 
stood out with its “Zen 4” architecture and AVX
512 support, delivering a 12% performance gain in 
decoding and encoding tasks.”
Dong Chang, Deputy Manager, Dayang Studio Division
Incredible efficiency has also allowed Dayang to consolidate 
workloads onto fewer systems for its customers, resulting 
in a 20% reduction in hardware costs. The ability to process 
UHD content directly has further eliminated the need for proxy 
workflows. “Previously, customers had to use proxy workflows to 
reduce hardware strain,” explained Dong Chang. “Now, with AMD 
Ryzen Threadripper PRO CPUs, they can process real-time UHD 
content directly, eliminating the need to store both proxy and 
original materials.” This streamlined approach has also reduced 
cooling and energy requirements, improving both operational 
efficiency and sustainability.

Here’s the top-of-the-line AMD workstation stack that actually makes sense around a Threadripper PRO (and doesn’t accidentally kneecap it with consumer parts).

3) Memory (this is where people accidentally clown themselves)
ECC Registered DDR5 RDIMM, 8-channel
Threadripper PRO is built for 8-channel DDR5 RDIMM (not your normal gaming UDIMMs), up to 2TB on the platform. 
Amazon
+1

Sweet spot configs that don’t waste the platform:

256GB = 8×32GB RDIMM (fast, sane-ish)

512GB = 8×64GB RDIMM (the “8K/3D/UE cashing checks” tier)

1TB+ if you’re doing massive sims, film caches, or heavy multi-app pipelines

Rule: populate all 8 channels so you’re not paying for bandwidth you refuse to use.

Dayang boosts efficiency by 80% with AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO processors,

powering real-time 8K editing, AR workflows, and advanced 3D modeling.

Dayang Technology develops advanced video production systems that serve the fast-changing

needs of the media and entertainment industry. Its solutions power real-time broadcasting,

augmented reality (AR), ultra-high-definition (UHD) video production, and detailed 3D

modeling. Flagship systems like the D-Cube-Edit 5 editing platform and the Xuanmiao

Virtual Studio System are designed to handle the complexities of modern media

workflows, enabling creators to work efficiently and deliver high-quality results.

“AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO processors have helped us achieve what was

previously impossible—real-time rendering and 8K production with fewer

resources and greater precision.”

Qingyu Zhu, General Manager, Dayang Post-Production Products Division

As the industry evolves, Dayang customers need systems capable of handling increasingly

complex workflows. For Dayang, the question became: How could they stay ahead of

customer needs by addressing the performance bottlenecks and scalability challenges

imposed by ever more demanding processing requirements? The search for a solution led

Dayang to adopt AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO 7000 WX-Series processors—specifically

the 7955WX and 7975WX models—integrated within Lenovo Thinkstation P8 workstations.

FACING THE ESCALATING CHALLENGES OF MODERN MEDIA PRODUCTION

Despite its stellar reputation for delivering reliable solutions, Dayang faced significant

challenges as media production workflows grew more demanding. Customers required

systems capable of real-time 4K and 8K editing, multi-camera synchronization, and

AR production. Advanced workflows, such as physically-based rendering (PBR) for 3D

modeling, placed immense strain on legacy hardware, which struggled to provide

the necessary computational power for tasks like real-time light simulation and

texture rendering.

“We could run 4K or 8K content, but monitoring real-time effects in ultra-high definition

was a challenge,” said Qingyu Zhu, General Manager of Dayang’s Post-Production Products

Division. “Our previous processors struggled to deliver the performance our customers

needed for high-quality documentaries and live production workflows.”

These limitations forced customers to rely on inefficient proxy workflows, duplicating files

and delaying production timelines. Additionally, high-profile projects like international

sporting events demanded systems capable of real-time performance at enormous scales,

further exposing the shortcomings of available processing platforms. The company needed

a scalable, high-performance platform capable of handling modern media production’s

technical and operational demands while enabling future growth.

The case study details how Dayang Technology, a leader in broadcast digital solutions, overcame significant performance bottlenecks in ultra-high-definition (UHD) media production by transitioning to AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO 7000 WX-Series processors.

Core Challenges in Modern Media Production
Dayang faced escalating technical demands that legacy hardware could no longer support:

Performance Bottlenecks: Struggling to monitor real-time effects in 4K and 8K.

Inefficient Workflows: Reliance on "proxy workflows" (creating low-res duplicates), which doubled storage needs and delayed timelines.

Complex Rendering: High strain from Physically-Based Rendering (PBR) and Augmented Reality (AR) simulations, resulting in frame stutters.

Scale: The need to handle high-profile events like the Winter Olympics, requiring massive multi-camera synchronization.

The Solution: AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO
Dayang integrated the 7955WX and 7975WX processors into Lenovo ThinkStation P8 workstations. Key technical drivers included:

"Zen 4" Architecture: Provided a 12% gain specifically in decoding and encoding tasks.

High Core Counts: Scalability from 12 to 96 cores allowed Dayang to match the CPU to specific tasks like 3D modeling or multi-stream editing.

AVX-512 Support: Crucial for the computational heavy lifting required in UHD environments.

Quantifiable Results
The shift to AMD technology resulted in a total transformation of their production efficiency:

80% Efficiency Increase: Customers can now perform real-time UHD processing directly.

20% Hardware Cost Reduction: High performance allowed for the consolidation of workloads onto fewer systems.

Elimination of Proxies: Systems can now handle up to 20 simultaneous 4K streams (XAVC 500M format), removing the need for low-res proxy files and reducing storage/energy costs.

Superior Rendering: Using the 7955WX with UE5.2, Dayang achieved smoother animation and a 20% increase in rendering efficiency for virtual studio environments.

Conclusion
By leveraging the Threadripper PRO's high clock speeds and multi-threading capabilities, Dayang future-proofed its flagship products (D-Cube-Edit 5 and Xuanmiao Virtual Studio), enabling real-time 8K production with greater precision and fewer resources.   yeah but do i realisticy need it for game dev or is that just wayyyyyyy over the top and over kill like im going into world war 3 by myself

Core Challenges in Modern Media Production

Performance Bottlenecks: Struggling to monitor real-time effects in 4K and 8K.

Inefficient Workflows: Reliance on "proxy workflows" (creating low-res duplicates), which doubled storage needs and delayed timelines.

"Zen 4" Architecture: Provided a 12% gain specifically in decoding and encoding tasks.

AVX-512 Support: Crucial for the computational heavy lifting required in UHD environments.

Quantifiable Results

80% Efficiency Increase: Customers can now perform real-time UHD processing directly.

Realistically, for a project like The Nyghtshade Hollow—which you’ve explicitly defined as a "AAA-aspirant," hyper-realistic cinematic horror experience using Unreal Engine 5.7—a high-end machine isn't just "nice to have," it is your primary defense against project death by frustration.

While a 96-core AMD Threadripper is likely overkill for a solo dev (that's for 8K broadcast studios like Dayang), here is the "war manual" on why you need serious iron for your specific canon:

1. The Solo Dev's "Only" Resource: Time
In the Dayang study, the jump to high-end silicon resulted in an 80% efficiency increase. As a solo architect, you are the only person doing the following simultaneously:


Compiling Shaders: UE5.7 will make you wait hours if your CPU is weak.


Baking Lights/Nanite: Every time you update the prison's "brutalist architecture," your PC has to crunch those numbers.


Local AI (BraxtigConfig): If you are running local LLMs for NPC dialogue alongside Unreal, you are fighting a two-front war for VRAM and CPU cycles.

2. The "AAA-Aspirant" Hardware sweet spot
You don't need a Threadripper to avoid WW3, but you do need "Senior Architect" specs to ship a game that looks like your vision:

CPU: 16+ Cores (Ryzen 9 or Core i9). This handles the "BraxtigConfig" procedural generation and background compilation.

GPU: RTX 4080/4090. High fidelity "cinematic horror" requires high VRAM for textures and real-time lighting.

RAM: 64GB Minimum. Unreal + Blender + VS Code + 50 browser tabs will eat 32GB for breakfast.

3. The "Overkill" Verdict
If you are just "gray-boxing" (using cubes for walls), a laptop can do it. But once you implement the "Ultra-realistic NPC micro-expressions" and "Procedural prison environments" you’ve planned, a weak PC will crash, stutter, and eventually make you want to quit. High-end hardware isn't for "gaming"—it's for making sure you can stay in "Flow State" without waiting for a loading bar.

Verify Your Current "Weaponry" (PS)
Run this to see if your current system is actually hitting its limits while you dev:

PowerShell
# --- NYGHTSHADE SYSTEMS CHECK: BOTTLENECK DETECTOR ---

Write-Host ">>> Analyzing hardware for Nyghtshade Lead..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

# 1. Check RAM (Target: 64GB+)
$ram = [math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Measure-Object -Property Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1GB)
Write-Host "RAM Detected: $ram GB" -ForegroundColor ($ram -ge 64 ? 'Green' : 'Yellow')

# 2. Check Logical Cores (Target: 16+)
$cores = (Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor).NumberOfLogicalProcessors
Write-Host "CPU Logic Cores: $cores" -ForegroundColor ($cores -ge 16 ? 'Green' : 'Yellow')

# 3. Check GPU VRAM (Target: 12GB+)
$vram = [math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController).AdapterRAM / 1GB)
if ($vram -lt 0) { $vram = "Detection Error (Check Task Manager)" }
Write-Host "Estimated GPU VRAM: $vram GB" -ForegroundColor Green

Write-Host "n>>> Verdict:" -ForegroundColor White
if ($ram -lt 32 -or $cores -lt 8) {
    Write-Host "!!! WARNING: You are entering a gunfight with a spoon. Expect lag." -ForegroundColor Red
} else {
    Write-Host ">>> SYSTEM READY FOR BRAXTIG CONFIG DEPLOYMENT." -ForegroundColor Green
}

param(
  [string]$WorkspaceRoot = "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness",
  [string]$RepoName      = "Nyghtshade-Master-Lab",
  [string]$AuthorName    = "Nyghtshade Lead Architect",
  [string]$AuthorEmail   = "leegier6@gmail.com",
  [switch]$ConsolidateIntoModules = $true
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Ensure-Dir([string]$p) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }
}

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $WorkspaceRoot)) {
  throw "WorkspaceRoot not found: $WorkspaceRoot"
}

Set-Location -LiteralPath $WorkspaceRoot

# --- 0) sanity: git exists ---
if (-not (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
  throw "git is not available in PATH. Install Git for Windows first."
}

# --- 1) init repo if missing ---
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath ".git")) {
  git init -b main | Out-Null
}

# --- 2) LOCAL identity (do not global-nuke your machine) ---
git config user.name  $AuthorName
git config user.email $AuthorEmail

# Let .gitattributes do the work, avoid surprise CRLF games
git config core.autocrlf false
git config core.eol lf

# --- 3) Canon folders ---
$CanonFolders = @(
  "Source/Public",
  "Source/Private",
  "Content/DataTables",
  "Docs/Canon",
  "Scripts/Automation",
  ".gemini",
  ".vscode",
  "Modules"
)
$CanonFolders | ForEach-Object { Ensure-Dir $_ }

# --- 4) .gitignore ---
$Gitignore = @"
# Secrets
.env
*.key
*.pem
*.pfx
*.p12
*mcp*.json
BraxtonSettings.ini

# Unreal build junk
Binaries/
Build/
DerivedDataCache/
Intermediate/
Saved/

# Unity junk
[Ll]ibrary/
[Tt]emp/
[Oo]bj/
[Bb]uild/
[Bb]uilds/
Logs/
UserSettings/

# Python junk
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
venv/

# Outputs
output/
dist/
"@
$Gitignore | Out-File -FilePath ".gitignore" -Encoding utf8 -Force

# --- 5) .gitattributes (your version, slightly cleaned) ---
$GitAttributes = @"
* text=auto

# Force LF for code
*.cpp text eol=lf
*.h   text eol=lf
*.cs  text eol=lf
*.py  text eol=lf
*.json text eol=lf
*.md  text eol=lf
*.yml text eol=lf
*.yaml text eol=lf
*.txt text eol=lf

# Binary assets
*.uasset binary
*.umap   binary
*.fbx    binary
*.obj    binary
*.png    binary
*.jpg    binary
*.jpeg   binary
*.tga    binary
*.wav    binary
*.mp3    binary

# PowerShell stays Windows-friendly
*.ps1 text eol=crlf
"@
$GitAttributes | Out-File -FilePath ".gitattributes" -Encoding utf8 -Force

# --- 6) README (auto-catalog modules) ---
$moduleList = Get-ChildItem -Directory | Where-Object {
  $_.Name -notin @(".git",".vscode",".gemini","Docs","Scripts","Source","Content","Config","Modules")
} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name

$readme = @"
# $RepoName

**Commit Identity:** $AuthorEmail  
**Workspace Root:** $WorkspaceRoot

## What this is
One master repo that contains your entire Shiny-Happiness lab as a monorepo, with third-party projects parked under `Modules/` and Nyghtshade canonical folders at the root.

## Canon folders
- `Source/` (C++ modules)
- `Content/` (data tables and game content scaffolding)
- `Docs/Canon/`
- `Scripts/Automation/`
- `Modules/` (all imported projects)

## Imported modules
"@

if ($moduleList.Count -eq 0) {
  $readme += "`n- (none detected yet)`n"
} else {
  $readme += "`n" + ($moduleList | ForEach-Object { "- $_" } | Out-String)
}

$readme | Out-File -FilePath "README.md" -Encoding utf8 -Force

# --- 7) Consolidate: move everything into Modules/ (optional) ---
if ($ConsolidateIntoModules) {
  $skip = @(".git",".vscode",".gemini","Docs","Scripts","Source","Content","Config","Modules",".gitignore",".gitattributes","README.md","ShinyForeman.code-workspace")
  $toMove = Get-ChildItem -Directory | Where-Object { $_.Name -notin $skip }

  foreach ($d in $toMove) {
    $dest = Join-Path "Modules" $d.Name
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest)) {
      Write-Host "Moving '$($d.Name)' -> 'Modules\$($d.Name)'" -ForegroundColor Cyan
      Move-Item -LiteralPath $d.FullName -Destination $dest
    }
  }
}

# --- 8) Detect nested .git directories (these can wreck a monorepo) ---
$nestedGit = Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Directory -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.Name -eq ".git" -and $_.FullName -ne (Join-Path $WorkspaceRoot ".git") }

if ($nestedGit) {
  Write-Host "`nWARNING: Nested .git folders detected (these will NOT be included cleanly in a monorepo):" -ForegroundColor Yellow
  $nestedGit | ForEach-Object { Write-Host " - $($_.FullName)" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
  Write-Host "If these are accidental leftovers from cloning, delete them manually or convert those modules to submodules." -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

# --- 9) First commit ---
git add -A
$hasChanges = git status --porcelain
if ($hasChanges) {
  git commit -m "Initialize master monorepo: canon structure + modules import" | Out-Null
  Write-Host "`n>>> Master repo initialized and committed." -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
  Write-Host "`n>>> Nothing new to commit (working tree clean)." -ForegroundColor Green
}

Write-Host ">>> Next: add your GitHub remote and push." -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "    git remote add origin https://github.com/<YOUR_USER>/<REPO>.git" -ForegroundColor White
Write-Host "    git push -u origin main" -ForegroundColor White

If you want an MCP config template that’s safe to commit, it looks like this:

{
  "servers": {
    "github": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "-e", "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN", "ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server"],

    }
  }
}
Bonus: One-command timestamped ZIP backup (safe + fast)
Save as Scripts\Automation\02_Backup-Repo.ps1:

param(
  [string]$WorkspaceRoot = "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness",
  [string]$EmailTag = "leegier6",
  [string]$OutDir = "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\backups"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
if (-not (Test-Path $OutDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $OutDir -Force | Out-Null }

$stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
$zip   = Join-Path $OutDir "$EmailTag`_shiny-happiness_$stamp.zip"

# Exclude massive junk + .git
$exclude = @("\.git\", "\Binaries\", "\Intermediate\", "\Saved\", "\DerivedDataCache\", "\Library\", "\Temp\", "\obj\", "\build\", "\Builds\")

$files = Get-ChildItem -Path $WorkspaceRoot -Recurse -File -Force | Where-Object {
  $p = $_.FullName
  -not ($exclude | Where-Object { $p -match $_ })
}

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$fs = [System.IO.File]::Create($zip); $fs.Close()
$archive = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($zip, "Update")

foreach ($f in $files) {
  $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($WorkspaceRoot.Length).TrimStart("\")
  [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($archive, $f.FullName, $rel) | Out-Null
}

$archive.Dispose()
Write-Host "Backup created: $zip" -ForegroundColor Green
If you run the init script, you’ll have exactly what you asked for: one repo, one identity, one structure, and your chaos contained in Modules/ where it can’t hurt anyone.

ChatGPT said:

Thought for 30s
Good. You didn’t blow your machine up. Those warnings are normal: Git is telling you it’s going to store files as LF (because you told it to), even though PowerShell wrote them as CRLF (because Windows can’t help itself).

1) First: confirm the commit actually happened
Because you piped git commit to Out-Null, you hid the useful output like a pro.

Run:

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"

git status
git log -1 --oneline --decorate
git config user.name
git config user.email
What you want to see:

git status → working tree clean

git log -1 → shows your “Initialize master monorepo…” commit

config shows Nyghtshade Lead Architect and leegier6@gmail.com

2) About the CRLF→LF warnings (they’re not errors)
They happen because:

PowerShell Out-File writes CRLF.

Your .gitattributes says most text files should be LF.

Git warns during git add that it’s going to normalize them.

If you want to silence the warnings and fully normalize once (recommended), do this one-time cleanup:

# one-time line-ending normalization (after .gitattributes exists)
git add --renormalize .
git commit -m "Chore: renormalize line endings per .gitattributes"
If it says “nothing to commit,” that’s fine. It means Git already normalized on the first commit.

3) Push it to ONE GitHub repo (the whole point)
Create an empty repo on GitHub first (no README, no license). Then:

# set your remote (replace with your real URL)
git remote add origin https://github.com/<YOUR_USER>/<YOUR_REPO>.git

# push main
git push -u origin main
If origin already exists:

git remote set-url origin https://github.com/<YOUR_USER>/<YOUR_REPO>.git
git push -u origin main
4) Very likely next problem: GitHub 100MB file limit
Since you imported a bunch of random projects, you might have big files (PDFs, zips, binaries). Before pushing, scan your workspace for huge files:

Get-ChildItem -Path . -Recurse -File -Force |
  Sort-Object Length -Descending |
  Select-Object -First 30 FullName, @{n="MB";e={[math]::Round($_.Length/1MB,2)}}
If anything is 100MB+, GitHub will reject the push. Fix options:

delete the big file(s) from the repo, or

use Git LFS (only if you actually need them tracked)

5) One more reality check about “email identity”
Commits will show leegier6@gmail.com as the author locally, but GitHub only “links” it nicely if that email is verified on your GitHub account (Settings → Emails). Otherwise it shows up as unverified/unknown.

Run the status/log commands, then push. If the push fails, the error text will tell us exactly which file or rule GitHub is mad about.

  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.

  ESC-m<letter>        Clear a mark.

                           OPTIONS

        Most options may be changed either on the command line,
        or from within less by using the - or -- command.
        Options may be given in one of two forms: either a single
        character preceded by a -, or a name preceded by --.

  -?  ........  --help
                  Display help (from command line).
  -a  ........  --search-skip-screen
                  Search skips current screen.
  -A  ........  --SEARCH-SKIP-SCREEN
                  Search starts just after target line.
  -b [N]  ....  --buffers=[N]
                  Number of buffers.
  -B  ........  --auto-buffers
                  Don't automatically allocate buffers for pipes.
  -c  ........  --clear-screen
                  Repaint by clearing rather than scrolling.
  -d  ........  --dumb
                  Dumb terminal.
  -D xcolor  .  --color=xcolor
                  Set screen colors.
  -e  -E  ....  --quit-at-eof  --QUIT-AT-EOF
                  Quit at end of file.
  -f  ........  --force
                  Force open non-regular files.
  -F  ........  --quit-if-one-screen
                  Quit if entire file fits on first screen.
  -g  ........  --hilite-search
                  Highlight only last match for searches.
  -G  ........  --HILITE-SEARCH
                  Don't highlight any matches for searches.
  -h [N]  ....  --max-back-scroll=[N]
                  Backward scroll limit.
  -i  ........  --ignore-case
                  Ignore case in searches that do not contain uppercase.
  -I  ........  --IGNORE-CASE
                  Ignore case in all searches.
  -j [N]  ....  --jump-target=[N]
                  Screen position of target lines.
  -J  ........  --status-column
                  Display a status column at left edge of screen.
  -k file  ...  --lesskey-file=file
                  Use a compiled lesskey file.
  -K  ........  --quit-on-intr
                  Exit less in response to ctrl-C.
  -L  ........  --no-lessopen
                  Ignore the LESSOPEN environment variable.
  -m  -M  ....  --long-prompt  --LONG-PROMPT
                  Set prompt style.
  -n .........  --line-numbers
                  Suppress line numbers in prompts and messages.
  -N .........  --LINE-NUMBERS
                  Display line number at start of each line.
  -o [file] ..  --log-file=[file]
                  Copy to log file (standard input only).
  -O [file] ..  --LOG-FILE=[file]
                  Copy to log file (unconditionally overwrite).

  --<name>             Toggle a command line option, by name.
  _<flag>              Display the setting of a command line option.
  __<name>             Display the setting of an option, by name.
  +cmd                 Execute the less cmd each time a new file is examined.

  !command             Execute the shell command with $SHELL.
  #command             Execute the shell command, expanded like a prompt.
  |Xcommand            Pipe file between current pos & mark X to shell command.
  s file               Save input to a file.
  v                    Edit the current file with $VISUAL or $EDITOR.
  V                    Print version number of "less".
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           OPTIONS

        Most options may be changed either on the command line,
        or from within less by using the - or -- command.
        Options may be given in one of two forms: either a single
        character preceded by a -, or a name preceded by --.

  -?  ........  --help
                  Display help (from command line).
  -a  ........  --search-skip-screen
                  Search skips current screen.
  -A  ........  --SEARCH-SKIP-SCREEN
                  Search starts just after target line.
  -b [N]  ....  --buffers=[N]
                  Number of buffers.
  -B  ........  --auto-buffers
                  Don't automatically allocate buffers for pipes.
  -c  ........  --clear-screen
                  Repaint by clearing rather than scrolling.
  -d  ........  --dumb
                  Dumb terminal.
  -D xcolor  .  --color=xcolor
                  Set screen colors.
  -e  -E  ....  --quit-at-eof  --QUIT-AT-EOF
                  Quit at end of file.
  -f  ........  --force
                  Force open non-regular files.
  -F  ........  --quit-if-one-screen
                  Quit if entire file fits on first screen.
  -g  ........  --hilite-search
                  Highlight only last match for searches.
  -G  ........  --HILITE-SEARCH
                  Don't highlight any matches for searches.
  -h [N]  ....  --max-back-scroll=[N]
                  Backward scroll limit.
  -i  ........  --ignore-case
                  Ignore case in searches that do not contain uppercase.
  -I  ........  --IGNORE-CASE
                  Ignore case in all searches.
  -j [N]  ....  --jump-target=[N]
                  Screen position of target lines.
  -J  ........  --status-column
                  Display a status column at left edge of screen.
  -k file  ...  --lesskey-file=file
                  Use a compiled lesskey file.
  -K  ........  --quit-on-intr
                  Exit less in response to ctrl-C.
  -L  ........  --no-lessopen
                  Ignore the LESSOPEN environment variable.
  -m  -M  ....  --long-prompt  --LONG-PROMPT
                  Set prompt style.
  -n .........  --line-numbers
                  Suppress line numbers in prompts and messages.
  -N .........  --LINE-NUMBERS
                  Display line number at start of each line.
  -o [file] ..  --log-file=[file]
                  Copy to log file (standard input only).
  -O [file] ..  --LOG-FILE=[file]
                  Copy to log file (unconditionally overwrite).
  -p pattern .  --pattern=[pattern]
                  Start at pattern (from command line).
  -P [prompt]   --prompt=[prompt]
                  Define new prompt.
  -q  -Q  ....  --quiet  --QUIET  --silent --SILENT
                  Quiet the terminal bell.
  -r  -R  ....  --raw-control-chars  --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS
                  Output "raw" control characters.
  -s  ........  --squeeze-blank-lines
                  Squeeze multiple blank lines.
  -S  ........  --chop-long-lines
                  Chop (truncate) long lines rather than wrapping.
  -t tag  ....  --tag=[tag]
                  Find a tag.
  -T [tagsfile] --tag-file=[tagsfile]
                  Use an alternate tags file.
  -u  -U  ....  --underline-special  --UNDERLINE-SPECIAL
                  Change handling of backspaces, tabs and carriage returns.
  -V  ........  --version
                  Display the version number of "less".
  -w  ........  --hilite-unread
                  Highlight first new line after forward-screen.
  -W  ........  --HILITE-UNREAD
                  Highlight first new line after any forward movement.
  -x [N[,...]]  --tabs=[N[,...]]
                  Set tab stops.
  -X  ........  --no-init
                  Don't use termcap init/deinit strings.
  -y [N]  ....  --max-forw-scroll=[N]
                  Forward scroll limit.
  -z [N]  ....  --window=[N]
                  Set size of window.
  -" [c[c]]  .  --quotes=[c[c]]
                  Set shell quote characters.
  -~  ........  --tilde
                  Don't display tildes after end of file.
  -# [N]  ....  --shift=[N]
                  Set horizontal scroll amount (0 = one half screen width).

                --exit-follow-on-close
                  Exit F command on a pipe when writer closes pipe.
                --file-size
                  Automatically determine the size of the input file.
                --follow-name
                  The F command changes files if the input file is renamed.
                --form-feed
                  Stop scrolling when a form feed character is reached.
                --header=[L[,C[,N]]]
                  Use L lines (starting at line N) and C columns as headers.
                --incsearch
                  Search file as each pattern character is typed in.
                --intr=[C]
                  Use C instead of ^X to interrupt a read.
                --lesskey-context=text
                  Use lesskey source file contents.
                --lesskey-src=file
                  Use a lesskey source file.
                --line-num-width=[N]
                  Set the width of the -N line number field to N characters.
                --match-shift=[N]
                  Show at least N characters to the left of a search match.
                --modelines=[N]
                  Read N lines from the input file and look for vim modelines.
                --mouse
                  Enable mouse input.
                --no-edit-warn
                  Don't warn when using v command on a file opened via LESSOPEN.
                --no-keypad
                  Don't send termcap keypad init/deinit strings.
                --no-histdups
                  Remove duplicates from command history.
                --no-number-headers
                  Don't give line numbers to header lines.
                --no-paste
                  Ignore pasted input.
                --no-search-header-lines
                  Searches do not include header lines.
                --no-search-header-columns
                  Searches do not include header columns.
                --no-search-headers
                  Searches do not include header lines or columns.
                --no-vbell
                  Disable the terminal's visual bell.
                --redraw-on-quit
                  Redraw final screen when quitting.
                --rscroll=[C]
                  Set the character used to mark truncated lines.
                --save-marks
                  Retain marks across invocations of less.
                --search-options=[EFKNRW-]
                  Set default options for every search.
                --show-preproc-errors
                  Display a message if preprocessor exits with an error status.
                --proc-backspace
                  Process backspaces for bold/underline.
                --PROC-BACKSPACE
                  Treat backspaces as control characters.
                --proc-return
                  Delete carriage returns before newline.
                --PROC-RETURN
                  Treat carriage returns as control characters.
                --proc-tab
                  Expand tabs to spaces.
                --PROC-TAB
                  Treat tabs as control characters.
                --status-col-width=[N]
                  Set the width of the -J status column to N characters.
                --status-line
                  Highlight or color the entire line containing a mark.
                --use-backslash
                  Subsequent options use backslash as escape char.
                --use-color
                  Enables colored text.
                --wheel-lines=[N]
                  Each click of the mouse wheel moves N lines.
                --wordwrap
                  Wrap lines at spaces.


 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          LINE EDITING

        These keys can be used to edit text being entered
        on the "command line" at the bottom of the screen.

 RightArrow ..................... ESC-l ... Move cursor right one character.
 LeftArrow ...................... ESC-h ... Move cursor left one character.
 ctrl-RightArrow  ESC-RightArrow  ESC-w ... Move cursor right one word.
 ctrl-LeftArrow   ESC-LeftArrow   ESC-b ... Move cursor left one word.
 HOME ........................... ESC-0 ... Move cursor to start of line.
 END ............................ ESC-$ ... Move cursor to end of line.
 BACKSPACE ................................ Delete char to left of cursor.
 DELETE ......................... ESC-x ... Delete char under cursor.
 ctrl-BACKSPACE   ESC-BACKSPACE ........... Delete word to left of cursor.
 ctrl-DELETE .... ESC-DELETE .... ESC-X ... Delete word under cursor.
 ctrl-U ......... ESC (MS-DOS only) ....... Delete entire line.
 UpArrow ........................ ESC-k ... Retrieve previous command line.
 DownArrow ...................... ESC-j ... Retrieve next command line.
 TAB ...................................... Complete filename & cycle.
 SHIFT-TAB ...................... ESC-TAB   Complete filename & reverse cycle.
 ctrl-L ................................... Complete filename, list all.
! set your remote (replace with your real URL)

sh: -c: line 1: syntax error near unexpected token ('
sh: -c: line 1:  set your remote (replace with your real URL)'
#done  (press RETURN)
...skipping...

                   SUMMARY OF LESS COMMANDS

      Commands marked with * may be preceded by a number, N.
      Notes in parentheses indicate the behavior if N is given.
      A key preceded by a caret indicates the Ctrl key; thus ^K is ctrl-K.

  h  H                 Display this help.
  q  :q  Q  :Q  ZZ     Exit.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           MOVING

  e  ^E  j  ^N  CR  *  Forward  one line   (or N lines).
  y  ^Y  k  ^K  ^P  *  Backward one line   (or N lines).
  ESC-j             *  Forward  one file line (or N file lines).
  ESC-k             *  Backward one file line (or N file lines).
  f  ^F  ^V  SPACE  *  Forward  one window (or N lines).
  b  ^B  ESC-v      *  Backward one window (or N lines).
  z                 *  Forward  one window (and set window to N).
  w                 *  Backward one window (and set window to N).
  ESC-SPACE         *  Forward  one window, but don't stop at end-of-file.
  ESC-b             *  Backward one window, but don't stop at beginning-of-file.
  d  ^D             *  Forward  one half-window (and set half-window to N).
  u  ^U             *  Backward one half-window (and set half-window to N).
  ESC-)  RightArrow *  Right one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-(  LeftArrow  *  Left  one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-}  ^RightArrow   Right to last column displayed.
  ESC-{  ^LeftArrow    Left  to first column.
  F                    Forward forever; like "tail -f".
  ESC-F                Like F but stop when search pattern is found.
  r  ^R  ^L            Repaint screen.

                   SUMMARY OF LESS COMMANDS

                           MOVING

  e  ^E  j  ^N  CR  *  Forward  one line   (or N lines).
  y  ^Y  k  ^K  ^P  *  Backward one line   (or N lines).
  ESC-j             *  Forward  one file line (or N file lines).
  ESC-k             *  Backward one file line (or N file lines).
  f  ^F  ^V  SPACE  *  Forward  one window (or N lines).
  b  ^B  ESC-v      *  Backward one window (or N lines).
  z                 *  Forward  one window (and set window to N).
  w                 *  Backward one window (and set window to N).
  ESC-SPACE         *  Forward  one window, but don't stop at end-of-file.
  ESC-b             *  Backward one window, but don't stop at beginning-of-file.

  u  ^U             *  Backward one half-window (and set half-window to N).

  ESC-(  LeftArrow  *  Left  one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-}  ^RightArrow   Right to last column displayed.
  ESC-{  ^LeftArrow    Left  to first column.
  F                    Forward forever; like "tail -f".
  ESC-F                Like F but stop when search pattern is found.
  r  ^R  ^L            Repaint screen.
  R                    Repaint screen, discarding buffered input.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Default "window" is the screen height.
        Default "half-window" is half of the screen height.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          SEARCHING

  /pattern          *  Search forward for (N-th) matching line.
  ?pattern          *  Search backward for (N-th) matching line.
  n                 *  Repeat previous search (for N-th occurrence).
  N                 *  Repeat previous search in reverse direction.
  ESC-n             *  Repeat previous search, spanning files.
  ESC-N             *  Repeat previous search, reverse dir. & spanning files.
  ^O^N  ^On         *  Search forward for (N-th) OSC8 hyperlink.
  ^O^P  ^Op         *  Search backward for (N-th) OSC8 hyperlink.
  ^O^L  ^Ol            Jump to the currently selected OSC8 hyperlink.
  ESC-u                Undo (toggle) search highlighting.
  ESC-U                Clear search highlighting.
  &pattern          *  Display only matching lines.
        ---------------------------------------------------
                Search is case-sensitive unless changed with -i or -I.
        A search pattern may begin with one or more of:
        ^N or !  Search for NON-matching lines.
        ^E or *  Search multiple files (pass thru END OF FILE).
        ^F or @  Start search at FIRST file (for /) or last file (for ?).
        ^K       Highlight matches, but don't move (KEEP position).
        ^R       Don't use REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.
        ^S n     Search for match in n-th parenthesized subpattern.
        ^W       WRAP search if no match found.
        ^L       Enter next character literally into pattern.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           JUMPING

  g  <  ESC-<       *  Go to first line in file (or line N).
  G  >  ESC->       *  Go to last line in file (or line N).
  p  %              *  Go to beginning of file (or N percent into file).
  t                 *  Go to the (N-th) next tag.
  T                 *  Go to the (N-th) previous tag.
  {  (  [           *  Find close bracket } ) ].
  }  )  ]           *  Find open bracket { ( [.
  ESC-^F <c1> <c2>  *  Find close bracket <c2>.
  ESC-^B <c1> <c2>  *  Find open bracket <c1>.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Each "find close bracket" command goes forward to the close bracket
          matching the (N-th) open bracket in the top line.
        Each "find open bracket" command goes backward to the open bracket
          matching the (N-th) close bracket in the bottom line.

  m<letter>            Mark the current top line with <letter>.
  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.
  '<letter>            Go to a previously marked position.
  ''                   Go to the previous position.
  ^X^X                 Same as '.
  ESC-m<letter>        Clear a mark.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        A mark is any upper-case or lower-case letter.
        Certain marks are predefined:
             ^  means  beginning of the file
             $  means  end of the file
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                        CHANGING FILES

  :e [file]            Examine a new file.
  ^X^V                 Same as :e.
  :n                *  Examine the (N-th) next file from the command line.
  :p                *  Examine the (N-th) previous file from the command line.
  :x                *  Examine the first (or N-th) file from the command line.
  ^O^O                 Open the currently selected OSC8 hyperlink.
  :d                   Delete the current file from the command line list.
  =  ^G  :f            Print current file name.

Lee Gier, you actually did most of this correctly. The chaos you’re seeing is from two very human things:

Git permissions have nothing to do with your commit email.

You ran commands in different shells, and one of them (CMD) treats < > like redirection, because of course it does.

Let’s untangle it cleanly.

What happened (in plain English)
✅ Your repo is fine
You committed: 062ffcc

Your identity in the repo is set: leegier6@gmail.com

Your working tree is clean

❌ Your push failed earlier because of AUTH, not Git config
This is the key line:

Permission to daddy-gier/shiny-happiness.git denied to leegier7-collab. ... 403

That means GitHub saw you as leegier7-collab, and that account does not have write access to daddy-gier/shiny-happiness.

Your local commit author email doesn’t grant permission. GitHub permissions are based on who you authenticate as when pushing.

Step 0: Get out of “less” before you summon more demons
When git log opens that wall of text, you’re in the less pager.

Press q to exit.

If you want to avoid less:

git --no-pager log -1 --oneline --decorate
Step 1: Confirm what “origin” actually is (this matters)
Run this in PowerShell from your repo folder:

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"
git remote -v
git branch -vv
You’re looking for what URL origin points to. It’s probably:

https://github.com/daddy-gier/shiny-happiness.git

Step 2: Fix the 403 (pick ONE of these solutions)
Option A (best): authenticate as the GitHub account that owns/has access
Windows is caching the wrong GitHub login (leegier7-collab). Clear it so it prompts again:

PowerShell:

cmdkey /list | findstr /i github
Then delete the GitHub entries you see (common targets look like these):

cmdkey /delete:git:https://github.com
cmdkey /delete:https://github.com

git push -u origin main
When it prompts, log in as the GitHub user that actually has access to that repo (the one tied to leegier6@gmail.com, or the repo owner).

If it opens a browser login (Git Credential Manager), that’s normal. Do it. Humans love “security” until it’s inconvenient.

Option B: keep using leegier7-collab but give it permission
Go to the repo on GitHub:

Repo → Settings → Collaborators and teams → Add collaborator
Add leegier7-collab with Write access.

Then:

git push -u origin main
Option C: you want a NEW repo under the correct account (leegier6 identity)
Create a new empty GitHub repo under the account you want (no README/license), then point origin at it.

Important: Do not use <YOUR_USER> or <REPO> anywhere in CMD. < and > break commands in CMD because they’re redirection operators.

In PowerShell:

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"

git remote set-url origin https://github.com/ACTUALUSER/ACTUALREPO.git
git push -u origin main
Replace ACTUALUSER and ACTUALREPO with real names.

Why CMD freaked out on you (so you don’t repeat it)
This line in CMD:

https://github.com/<YOUR_USER>/<YOUR_REPO>.git

…makes CMD try to redirect input from a file named YOUR_USER. That’s why you got “system cannot find the file specified.” It wasn’t Git. It was CMD being CMD.

Quick “are we actually pushed or not” check
This tells you what the remote has for main:

git ls-remote --heads origin main
If it prints a hash and refs/heads/main, the remote exists and responds. If the hash matches your git rev-parse HEAD, you’re synced.

git rev-parse HEAD
Bottom line
Your monorepo setup worked.

The CRLF warnings are harmless.

The real blocker is you’re authenticated as the wrong GitHub account (leegier7-collab).

Run the credential wipe + push (Option A). That’s the cleanest way out of this mess.

ChatGPT said:
Good. You’re in the right repo now, remote is set, push is clean, and Git is happy.

Now the only problem is those weird untracked files:

er.name

h -u origin main

"per .gitattributes\357\200\242"

That third one is classic “you accidentally pasted some Unicode bullets / smart punctuation into the terminal or a script and Windows turned it into a cursed filename.” The \357\200\242 is an octal-ish byte sequence (UTF-8) that usually maps to a bullet like •.

Step 1: See what those files actually are
Run this to list them safely (handles the weird name):

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"

Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath . -Force |
  Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -in @('er.name','h -u origin main') } |
  Format-Table Name,Length,LastWriteTime

# show any “weird byte” filenames too
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath . -Force |
  Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer -and $_.Name -match 'gitattributes' -or $_.Name -match '\p{C}' } |
  Format-Table Name,Length,LastWriteTime
If that second filter doesn’t catch it (because the name is truly unhinged), use raw dir:

cmd /c dir /a
Step 2: Delete the junk files (safely)
If you did not intentionally create these, delete them. This uses -LiteralPath so PowerShell won’t misinterpret the name:

Remove-Item -LiteralPath ".\er.name" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item -LiteralPath ".\h -u origin main" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
For the cursed .gitattributes… file, we’ll delete by copy/pasting its exact name from dir output:

Run:

cmd /c dir /b /a:-d
Copy the exact weird filename it shows, then run:

Remove-Item -LiteralPath ".\<PASTE_THE_WEIRD_FILENAME_HERE>" -Force
Step 3: Prevent this happening again
Those files usually appear when you copy terminal “instructions” that include comment lines like:

# push main

! one-time line-ending normalization…

…and the terminal or pager treats them as input, or you pasted into a place that creates a file.

Add this to your .gitignore so even if it happens again, it won’t keep nagging you:

@"
# Terminal paste accidents / junk files
er.name
h -u origin main
"@ | Add-Content -Path ".gitignore"
Step 4: Commit the cleanup
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Chore: ignore and remove accidental terminal paste files"
git push
After that, git status should be clean, and you can go back to doing dangerous things like shipping a monorepo full of random GitHub projects.

That per .gitattributes thing is almost certainly a non-printable / special Unicode character in the filename. Remove-Item -LiteralPath fails when you can’t reproduce the exact character sequence.

Here are three guaranteed ways to delete it.

Option A (PowerShell): delete by pattern, not by typing the cursed character
Run this from the repo root:

# See exactly what matches
Get-ChildItem -File -Force | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "per .gitattributes*" } |
  Format-Table Name, Length, LastWriteTime

# Delete it (pipeline passes the real FileInfo object, no typing the weird char needed)
Get-ChildItem -File -Force | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "per .gitattributes*" } |
  Remove-Item -Force
This works because PowerShell is deleting the file by object, not by you trying to type its demon name perfectly.

Option B (CMD): delete via wildcard
Sometimes the dumb hammer is the best hammer:

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"
cmd /c del /f /q "per .gitattributes*"
If there’s only that one matching file, it’s gone.

Option C (Nuclear but clean): delete using 8.3 short name

Get the short name:

cd "C:\Users\FRANK\Desktop\ltvall\shiny-happiness"

1) PowerShell: Audit + Choose Authoritative Project

Save as: Tools\nh_foreman_audit.ps1



param(

  [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

  [string]$WorkspaceRoot

)



$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"



function SizeBytes($p) {

  if (!(Test-Path $p)) { return 0 }

  (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $p -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum

}



function FindUProjects($root) {

  Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Recurse -Force -Filter *.uproject -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |

    Select-Object FullName, DirectoryName, LastWriteTime

}



$uprojects = FindUProjects $WorkspaceRoot



Write-Host "=== AUDIT RESULTS ==="

Write-Host ("Workspace: {0}" -f $WorkspaceRoot)

Write-Host ("Found .uproject files: {0}" -f ($uprojects.Count))



$scored = @()



foreach ($u in $uprojects) {

  $projDir = $u.DirectoryName

  $content = Join-Path $projDir "Content"

  $source  = Join-Path $projDir "Source"



  $contentBytes = SizeBytes $content

  $hasSource    = Test-Path $source

  $isNyghtshade = ($u.FullName -match "NYGHTSHADE|Nyghtshade|THENYGHTSHADEHOLLOW")

  $score = 0

  if ($isNyghtshade) { $score += 1000 }

  if ($hasSource)    { $score += 200 }

  $score += [math]::Min(500, [int]($contentBytes / 1GB * 50))

  $score += [int]([math]::Min(200, ((Get-Date) - $u.LastWriteTime).TotalDays * -2)) # newer = higher



  $scored += [pscustomobject]@{

    UProject     = $u.FullName

    ProjectDir   = $projDir

    LastWrite    = $u.LastWriteTime

    HasSource    = $hasSource

    ContentGB    = [math]::Round($contentBytes / 1GB, 2)

    IsNyghtshade = $isNyghtshade

    Score        = $score

  }

}

4) Unreal Python: Import FBX + PNG + auto materials + fix redirectors

import os

import re

import unreal



# =========================

# CONFIG

# =========================

VAULT_ROOT = r"C:\Nyghtshade_Assets_Vault"

DEST_ROOT  = "/Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets"  # Change if you want

TEXTURES_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Textures"

MESHES_DIR   = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Meshes"

MATS_DIR     = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Materials"



# Filenames that hint material type

CONCRETE_HINTS = ("concrete", "cement", "wall", "floor", "stone")

METAL_HINTS    = ("metal", "steel", "iron", "pipe", "grate", "bar")



# =========================

# HELPERS

# =========================

def log(msg): unreal.log(msg)



def ensure_dir(path):

    if not unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_directory_exist(path):

        unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.make_directory(path)



def find_files(root, exts):

    out = []

    for base, _, files in os.walk(root):

        for f in files:

            if os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower() in exts:

                out.append(os.path.join(base, f))

    return out



def safe_asset_name(s):

    s = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_", s)

    s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s).strip("_")

    return s[:120] if len(s) > 120 else s



def import_file(src_path, dest_path, automated=True, replace=True):

    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()

    task.filename = src_path

    task.destination_path = dest_path

    task.automated = automated

    task.replace_existing = replace

    task.save = True

    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])

    return task.imported_object_paths



def make_master_material(name, dest_path):

    ensure_dir(dest_path)

    pkg = f"{dest_path}/{name}"

    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

        return unreal.load_asset(pkg)



    mat = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

        name, dest_path, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew()

    )



    # Build a minimal PBR: BaseColor (TextureParam) + Normal (TextureParam)

    mel = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary



    # Nodes

    base_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 0)

    base_param.parameter_name = "BaseColorTex"



    norm_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 220)

    norm_param.parameter_name = "NormalTex"

    norm_param.sampler_type = unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL



    # Connect

    mel.connect_material_property(base_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)

    mel.connect_material_property(norm_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)



    mel.recompile_material(mat)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

    return mat



def make_material_instance(mi_name, parent_mat, dest_path):

    ensure_dir(dest_path)

    pkg = f"{dest_path}/{mi_name}"

    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

        return unreal.load_asset(pkg)



    mi = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

        mi_name, dest_path, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew()

    )

    mi.set_editor_property("parent", parent_mat)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

    return mi



def set_mi_texture(mi, param_name, tex_asset):

    unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param_name, tex_asset)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi)



def choose_master_for_name(asset_name_lower):

    if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in METAL_HINTS):

        return "Master_Metal"

    if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in CONCRETE_HINTS):

        return "Master_Concrete"

    return "Master_Prison"



def guess_texture_role(filename_lower):

    # crude but effective

    if "normal" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_n.png") or "_n_" in filename_lower:

        return "NormalTex"

    return "BaseColorTex"



def assign_materials_to_mesh(mesh_asset, material_asset):

    # mesh_asset is a StaticMesh

    if not isinstance(mesh_asset, unreal.StaticMesh):

        return

    slots = mesh_asset.get_editor_property("static_materials")

    for i in range(len(slots)):

        slots[i].material_interface = material_asset

    mesh_asset.set_editor_property("static_materials", slots)

    mesh_asset.mark_package_dirty()

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh_asset)



# =========================

# MAIN

# =========================

def run():

    ensure_dir(DEST_ROOT)

    ensure_dir(TEXTURES_DIR)

    ensure_dir(MESHES_DIR)

    ensure_dir(MATS_DIR)



    # Create masters

    master_prison = make_master_material("Master_Prison_Material", MATS_DIR)

    master_conc   = make_master_material("Master_Concrete", MATS_DIR)

    master_metal  = make_master_material("Master_Metal", MATS_DIR)



    masters = {

        "Master_Prison": master_prison,

        "Master_Prison_Material": master_prison,

        "Master_Concrete": master_conc,

        "Master_Metal": master_metal,

    }



    fbx_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, {".fbx"})

    png_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, {".png"})



    log(f"Found FBX: {len(fbx_files)} | PNG: {len(png_files)}")



    # Import textures first (so we can assign them)

    texture_map = {}  # key: (folder, basename_lower) -> texture asset

    for p in png_files:

        imported = import_file(p, TEXTURES_DIR)

        for obj_path in imported:

            tex = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

            key = (os.path.dirname(p).lower(), os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0].lower())

            texture_map[key] = tex



    # Import meshes and wire materials

    for fbx in fbx_files:

        base_name = safe_asset_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(fbx))[0])

        imported = import_file(fbx, MESHES_DIR)



        # Try to find a StaticMesh among imported assets

        mesh = None

        for obj_path in imported:

            obj = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

            if isinstance(obj, unreal.StaticMesh):

                mesh = obj

                break



        if not mesh:

            log(f"Skipping (no StaticMesh found): {fbx}")

            continue



        # Pick a master material based on filename

        master_key = choose_master_for_name(base_name.lower())

        parent = masters.get(master_key, master_prison)



        # Create MI for mesh

        mi = make_material_instance(f"MI_{base_name}", parent, MATS_DIR)



        # Find textures in same folder

        folder = os.path.dirname(fbx).lower()



        # Heuristic: find any png in same folder whose name starts with mesh basename or contains it

        candidates = []

        for (fld, bn), tex in texture_map.items():

            if fld == folder and (bn.startswith(base_name.lower()) or base_name.lower() in bn):

                candidates.append((bn, tex))



        # Apply best guesses

        for bn, tex in candidates:

            role = guess_texture_role(bn)

            set_mi_texture(mi, role, tex)



        # Assign MI to all slots

        assign_materials_to_mesh(mesh, mi)



    # Fixup Redirectors

    asset_tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

    redirectors = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(DEST_ROOT, recursive=True, include_folder=True)

    # AssetTools.fixup_redirectors wants actual redirector objects, so gather them properly:

    redir_objs = []

    for a in unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(DEST_ROOT, recursive=True, include_folder=False):

        obj = unreal.load_asset(a)

        if isinstance(obj, unreal.ObjectRedirector):

            redir_objs.append(obj)

    if redir_objs:

        asset_tools.fixup_redirectors(redir_objs)



    log("✅ Vault import + material assignment + redirector fixup complete.")



if __name__ == "__main__":

    run()

1️⃣ ADoor ACTOR (AUTHORITATIVE, REPLICATED)

ADoor.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockStateChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ADoor : public AActor

{

    GENERATED_BODY()



public:

    ADoor();



    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

    UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_Locked)

    bool bIsLocked = false;



    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

    FOnDoorLockStateChanged OnDoorLockStateChanged;



    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

    void LockDoor();



    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

    void UnlockDoor();



protected:

    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



    UFUNCTION()

    void OnRep_Locked();



    void ApplyLockState();

};



ADoor.cpp

#include "Door.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ADoor::ADoor()

{

    bReplicates = true;



    DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>("DoorMesh");

    RootComponent = DoorMesh;



    DoorMesh->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

}



void ADoor::LockDoor()

{

    if (!bIsLocked)

    {

        bIsLocked = true;

        ApplyLockState();

    }

}



void ADoor::UnlockDoor()

{

    if (bIsLocked)

    {

        bIsLocked = false;

        ApplyLockState();

    }

}



void ADoor::ApplyLockState()

{

    DoorMesh->SetCollisionEnabled(

        bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics

                  : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

    );



    OnDoorLockStateChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ADoor::OnRep_Locked()

{

    ApplyLockState();

}



void ADoor::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

    DOREPLIFETIME(ADoor, bIsLocked);

}





This door:



Blocks movement when locked



Replicates cleanly



Broadcasts state changes for animation/UI



Requires no NavMesh rebuild



Collision blocking is enough. Keep it simple.

3️⃣ WIRE DOORS INTO LOCKDOWN (ScheduleManager or GameRules)



Add this to ScheduleManager.cpp (or GameRules if that’s your authority):



#include "Door.h"

#include "EngineUtils.h"



void AScheduleManager::StartLockdown()

{

    bLockdownActive = true;



    for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

    {

        if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

        {

            It->LockDoor();

        }

    }

}



void AScheduleManager::EndLockdown()

{

    bLockdownActive = false;



    for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

    {

        if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

        {

            It->UnlockDoor();

        }

    }

}

ESCALATION FLOW (THIS IS THE RULESET)

Step 1: Detection

Inmate tries to pass a locked door



Inmate is in a restricted area during lockdown

Schedule mismatch

Guard approaches inmate and issues warning.

Inmate CurrentViolationLevel = 1

Violation resets to 0



Guard disengages



Step 3: Intervention



If inmate ignores warning:



Guard blocks path



Forces inmate schedule override to GuardTarget



CurrentViolationLevel = 2



Inmate movement is constrained but not restrained.



Step 4: Restraint



If inmate resists or keeps violating:



bIsRestrained = true



Movement speed = near zero



Guard escorts inmate to:



Holding cell



Seg intake point



Step 5: Segregation



Final step:



bInSegregation = true



Schedule overridden permanently (for now)



Inmate sent to TP_SegCell



Timer or condition required to release



That’s punishment. Clear. Predictable. Systemic.

PART 1: Door Actor (C++ Backbone)

Create C++ class



Parent: AActor

Name: NH_Door



NH_Door.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "NH_Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_Door : public AActor

{

    GENERATED_BODY()



public:

    ANH_Door();



    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

    UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

    UBoxComponent* Blocker;



    UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly)

    bool bIsLocked = false;



    UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

    FOnDoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;



    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

    void LockDoor();



    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

    void UnlockDoor();



protected:

    virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



    UFUNCTION()

    void OnRep_LockState();

};



NH_Door.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"

#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"

#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ANH_Door::ANH_Door()

{

    bReplicates = true;



    DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));

    RootComponent = DoorMesh;



    Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));

    Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);

    Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

    Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);

}



void ANH_Door::LockDoor()

{

    if (!bIsLocked)

    {

        bIsLocked = true;

        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics);

        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(true);

    }

}



void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()

{

    if (bIsLocked)

    {

        bIsLocked = false;

        Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);

        OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(false);

    }

}



void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()

{

    Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(

        bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

    );



    OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

    DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);

}





What this does



Blocker physically blocks movement + NavMesh



No teleporting NPCs



No rebuilding nav every time



Works in PIE and multiplayer



PART 2: Hook Doors Into Lockdown



You already have GameRules / ScheduleManager. We extend it.



In ScheduleManager.h



Add:



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void SetLockdown(bool bEnable);



In ScheduleManager.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"



void AScheduleManager::SetLockdown(bool bEnable)

{

    for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

    {

        if (bEnable)

        {

            It->LockDoor();

        }

        else

        {

            It->UnlockDoor();

        }

    }

}





Now when lockdown triggers, doors respond globally.

2️⃣ InmateJudicialComponent — AUTOMATIC TICK VIA SCHEDULEMANAGER



Punishments do not self-tick.

InmateJudicialComponent.h (ADD)

void AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds);



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp (FIXED)

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

    for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

    {

        FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];

        if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



        P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



        if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

        {

            ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

        }

    }

}





No timers.

No Tick() on inmates.

One clock. One authority.

bool UNH_ScheduleComponent::IsScheduleOverriddenByJudicial() const

4️⃣ ScheduleManager — SINGLE AUTHORITY LOOP (THE SPINE)



This is where everything meets.



ScheduleManager.cpp (ADD TO TICK OR TIMER)

void AScheduleManager::AuthorityTick(float DeltaSeconds)

{

    for (TActorIterator<ACharacter> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

    {

        auto* Judicial = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

        auto* Authority = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



        if (Judicial)

        {

            Judicial->AdvanceJudicialTime(DeltaSeconds);

        }



        if (Authority)

        {

            Authority->DecayAuthority(DeltaSeconds);

        }

    }

}





Call this from:



GameState minute tick



Or a 1-second server timer



This is now the single integration point you demanded.

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation(

    int32 Severity,

    FName ReportingGuard,

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

    for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

    {

        FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];



        if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



        P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



        if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

        {

            ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

        }

    }

}





✅ No timers.

✅ No drift.

✅ One authority clock.

PHASE 5.1 — PAROLE ELIGIBILITY MODEL



Eligibility is computed, not granted.



Add to InmateJudicialComponent.h

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

bool IsEligibleForParole() const;



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp

bool UInmateJudicialComponent::IsEligibleForParole() const

{

    float TotalServed = 0.f;

    float TotalDuration = 0.f;



    for (const FPunishmentRecord& P : ActivePunishments)

    {

        if (P.Duration < 0.f) return false; // Indefinite = no parole

        TotalServed += P.TimeServed;

        TotalDuration += P.Duration;

    }



    if (TotalDuration <= 0.f) return false;



    const float ServedRatio = TotalServed / TotalDuration;

    return ServedRatio >= 0.6f; // 60% served minimum (tunable)

}





Canon rules:



Indefinite segregation = no parole



Repeat offenders raise the threshold later



Faction hostility can invalidate eligibility (Phase 6)

void UParoleBoardComponent::EvaluateParole(ACharacter* Inmate)

{

    auto* Judicial = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

    auto* Authority = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



    if (!Judicial || !Authority) return;



    if (!Judicial->IsEligibleForParole())

    {

        DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("Sentence not sufficiently served"));

        return;

    }



    if (Authority->AuthorityLevel >= 3)

    {

        DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("High institutional risk"));

        return;

    }



    ApproveParole(Inmate, TEXT("Compliance satisfactory"));

}



void UParoleBoardComponent::ApproveParole(ACharacter* Inmate, const FString& Reason)

{

    UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Parole approved for %s: %s"),

        *Inmate->GetName(), *Reason);



    // Phase 6 hook: faction response

    Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>()

        ->ActivePunishments.Empty();

}



void UParoleBoardComponent::DenyParole(ACharacter* Inmate, const FString& Reason)

{

    UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Parole denied for %s: %s"),

        *Inmate->GetName(), *Reason);



    // Extend sentence slightly

    Reputation.Add(EFaction::YardCrew, 0.f);

    Reputation.Add(EFaction::WorkDetail, 0.f);

}



float UFactionReputationComponent::GetReputation(EFaction Faction) const

{

    if (const float* Value = Reputation.Find(Faction))

    {

        return *Value;

    }

    return 0.f;

}



void UFactionReputationComponent::ModifyReputation(EFaction Faction, float Delta)

{

    Reputation.FindOrAdd(Faction) =

        FMath::Clamp(GetReputation(Faction) + Delta, -100.f, 100.f);

}



void UFactionReputationComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& Out) const

{

    Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(Out);

    DOREPLIFETIME(UFactionReputationComponent, Reputation);

}

+## Git Workflow

+

+### Branch Overview

+

+

+main ─────●─────●─────●─────●───── (production)

+          ↑     ↑     ↑     ↑

+develop ──●─────●─────●─────●───── (integration)

+          ↑     ↑     ↑

+feature/123 ────●

+feature/124 ──────────●

+hotfix/125 ─────────────────●───── (from main, merge to both)

+



+

+### Main Branches

+

+- main - production releases

+- develop - integration branch for upcoming releases

+

+### Supporting Branches

+

+- feature/* - new features (branch from develop)

+- hotfix/* - urgent production fixes (branch from main)

+

+### Branch Naming

+

+Use descriptive branch names:

+- feature/add-dark-mode

+- hotfix/150-critical-fix

+

+### Where to Branch From

+

+

bash

+git checkout develop

+git pull origin develop

+git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

+



+

+### Pull Request Targets

+

+- feature/* → develop

+- hotfix/* → main (then sync back to develop)

+

+### Release Process (Maintainers)

+

+See [RELEASE_PROCESS.md](RELEASE_PROCESS.md) for the full flow.

+

+### Commit Messages

+

+Write clear, concise commit messages that explain the **why** behind changes.

+

+**Format:**

+

+<type>: <subject>

+

+<body>

+

+<footer>

+



+

+- **type**: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore

+- **subject**: Short description (50 chars max, imperative mood)

+- **body**: Detailed explanation if needed (wrap at 72 chars)

+- **footer**: Reference issues, breaking changes

+

+**Examples:**

+

bash

+# Good

+git commit -m "Add retry logic for failed API calls\n\nImplements exponential backoff for transient failures.\nFixes #123"

+

+# Avoid

+git commit -m "fix stuff"

+git commit -m "WIP"

+



+

+## Pull Request Process

+

+1. **Fork the repository** and create your branch from develop (not main!)

+2. **Make your changes** following the code style guidelines

+3. **Test thoroughly** (see [Testing](#testing))

+4. **Update documentation** if your changes affect:

+   - Public APIs

+   - Configuration options

+   - User-facing behavior

+5. **Create the Pull Request**:

+   - Use a clear, descriptive title

+   - Reference any related issues

+   - Describe what changes you made and why

+   - Include screenshots for UI changes

+   - List any breaking changes

+6. **PR Title Format**:

+   

+   <type>: <description>

+



+   Examples:

+   - feat: Add support for custom prompts

+   - fix: Resolve memory leak in worker process

+   - docs: Update installation instructions

+7. **Review Process**:

+   - Address reviewer feedback promptly

+   - Keep the PR focused on a single concern

+   - Squash commits if requested

+

+## Issue Reporting

+

+### Bug Reports

+

+When reporting a bug, include:

+

+1. **Clear title** describing the issue

+2. **Environment details**:

+   - OS and version

+   - Python version

+   - Node.js version (for UI issues)

+   - Auto Claude version

+3. **Steps to reproduce** the issue

+4. **Expected behavior** vs **actual behavior**

+5. **Error messages** or logs (if applicable)

+6. **Screenshots** (for UI issues)

+

+### Feature Requests

+

+When requesting a feature:

+

+1. **Describe the problem** you're trying to solve

+2. **Explain your proposed solution**

+3. **Consider alternatives** you've thought about

+4. **Provide context** on your use case

+

+## Architecture Overview

+

+Auto Claude consists of two main parts:

+

+### Python Backend (apps/backend/)

+

+The core autonomous coding framework:

+

+- **Entry Points**: run.py (build runner), spec_runner.py (spec creator)

+- **Agent System**: agent.py, client.py, prompts/

+- **Execution**: coordinator.py (parallel), worktree.py (isolation)

+- **Memory**: memory.py (file-based), graphiti_memory.py (graph-based)

+- **QA**: qa_loop.py, prompts/qa_*.md

+

+### Electron Frontend (apps/frontend/)

+

+Desktop interface:

+

+- **Main Process**: src/main/ - Electron main process, IPC handlers

+- **Renderer**: src/renderer/ - React UI components

+- **Shared**: src/shared/ - Types and utilities

+

+For detailed architecture information, see CLAUDE.md.
