>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_clean_project.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_clean_project = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$ProjectDir,

>>

>>   [switch]$NukeDerivedDataCache,

>>   [switch]$AlsoGlobalDDC

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> function Zap([string]$p) {

>>   if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($p)) { return }

>>   if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p) {

>>     Write-Host "Deleting: $p" -ForegroundColor Yellow

>>     Remove-Item -LiteralPath $p -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>>   }

>> }

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir)) {

>>   throw "ProjectDir not found: $ProjectDir"

>> }

>>

>> # Kill Unreal Editor if running

>> Get-Process UnrealEditor -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>>

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Binaries")

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Intermediate")

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Saved")

>>

>> if ($NukeDerivedDataCache) {

>>   Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "DerivedDataCache")

>> }

>>

>> if ($AlsoGlobalDDC) {

>>   $globalDDC = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache"

>>   Zap $globalDDC

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host "✅ Cleanup done." -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_copy_uassets.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_copy_uassets = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$VaultPath,

>>

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$ProjectDir,

>>

>>   [string]$DestSubdir = "PrisonCore",

>>

>>   [switch]$UseRobocopy

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $VaultPath))   { throw "VaultPath not found: $VaultPath" }

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir))  { throw "ProjectDir not found: $ProjectDir" }

>>

>> $dest = Join-Path $ProjectDir "Content\$DestSubdir"

>> New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dest | Out-Null

>>

>> Write-Host "Copying .uasset/.umap from:" -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> Write-Host "  Vault: $VaultPath"

>> Write-Host "  Dest : $dest"

>>

>> # If robocopy requested and available, use it (faster + preserves structure cleanly)

>> if ($UseRobocopy -and (Get-Command robocopy.exe -EA SilentlyContinue)) {

>>   $args = @(

>>     ""$VaultPath"",

>>     ""$dest"",

>>     "*.uasset",

>>     "*.umap",

>>     "/E",

>>     "/R:1",

>>     "/W:1",

>>     "/NFL","/NDL","/NJH","/NJS","/NP"

>>   )

>>   & robocopy @args | Out-Host

>>   Write-Host "✅ Robocopy pass complete." -ForegroundColor Green

>>   exit 0

>> }

>>

>> # Pure PowerShell copy (slower but works everywhere)

>> $items = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -Force -File -EA SilentlyContinue |

>>   Where-Object { $_.Extension -in ".uasset",".umap" }

>>

>> if (!$items) {

>>   Write-Host "No .uasset/.umap files found in vault." -ForegroundColor Yellow

>>   exit 0

>> }

>>

>> foreach ($it in $items) {

>>   $rel = $it.FullName.Substring($VaultPath.Length).TrimStart('\','/')

>>   $target = Join-Path $dest $rel

>>   $targetDir = Split-Path -Parent $target

>>   if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $targetDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $targetDir | Out-Null }

>>   Copy-Item -LiteralPath $it.FullName -Destination $target -Force

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host ("✅ Copied {0} assets." -f $items.Count) -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_build_safe.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_build_safe = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$UProjectPath,

>>

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$UE57Root,

>>

>>   [ValidateSet("Win64")]

>>   [string]$Platform = "Win64",

>>

>>   [ValidateSet("Development","DebugGame","Shipping")]

>>   [string]$Config = "Development",

>>

>>   [int]$MaxParallelActions = 6,

>>

>>   [switch]$RegenerateProjectFiles

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $UProjectPath)) { throw "UProjectPath not found: $UProjectPath" }

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $UE57Root))     { throw "UE57Root not found: $UE57Root" }

>>

>> $buildBat = Join-Path $UE57Root "Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat"

>> $gpfBat   = Join-Path $UE57Root "Engine\Build\BatchFiles\GenerateProjectFiles.bat"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $buildBat)) { throw "Build.bat not found: $buildBat" }

>>

>> $projName = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($UProjectPath)

>> $target   = "${projName}Editor"

>>

>> # Kill any editor leftovers

>> Get-Process UnrealEditor -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>>

>> if ($RegenerateProjectFiles) {

>>   if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $gpfBat)) { throw "GenerateProjectFiles.bat not found: $gpfBat" }

>>   Write-Host "Regenerating project files..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

>>   & $gpfBat "-Project=$UProjectPath" -Game -Engine | Out-Host

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host "Building $target ($Platform/$Config) MaxParallelActions=$MaxParallelActions" -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> & $buildBat $target $Platform $Config "-Project=$UProjectPath" -WaitMutex "-MaxParallelActions=$MaxParallelActions" | Out-Host

>>

>> Write-Host "✅ Build finished." -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_git_init_ue.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_git_init_ue = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>>   [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>>   [string]$RepoRoot,

>>

>>   [string]$RemoteUrl = "",

>>

>>   [string]$DefaultBranch = "main"

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $RepoRoot)) { throw "RepoRoot not found: $RepoRoot" }

>>

>> function Run([string]$cmd) {

>>   Write-Host ">> $cmd" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

>>   cmd.exe /c $cmd

>>   if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Command failed: $cmd" }

>> }

>>

>> Push-Location $RepoRoot

>> try {

>>   if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $RepoRoot ".git"))) {

>>     Run "git init"

>>   }

>>

>>   # Ensure branch name

>>   Run "git checkout -B $DefaultBranch"

>>

>>   # LFS

>>   Run "git lfs install"

>>

>>   # .gitattributes for UE assets

>>   $ga = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitattributes"

>>   if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ga)) {

>>     @"

>> *.uasset filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.umap   filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.fbx    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.png    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.tga    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.wav    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> "@ | Set-Content -Path $ga -Encoding utf8

>>   }

>>

>>   # .gitignore (standard UE)

>>   $gi = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitignore"

>>   if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $gi)) {

>>     @"

>> # Unreal Engine

>> Binaries/

>> DerivedDataCache/

>> Intermediate/

>> Saved/

>> .vscode/

>> .vs/

>> *.sln

>> *.opensdf

>> *.sdf

>> *.suo

>> *.user

>> *.userprefs

>> *.VC.db

>> *.VC.VC.opendb

>> *.pdb

>> *.log

>>

>> # Build artifacts

>> Build/

>> "@ | Set-Content -Path $gi -Encoding utf8

>>   }

>>

>>   Run "git add .gitattributes .gitignore"

>>   Run "git add -A"

>>   Run "git commit -m "Initialize UE repo + LFS tracking""

>>

>>   if ($RemoteUrl -and $RemoteUrl.Trim().Length -gt 0) {

>>     $existing = (git remote) 2>$null

>>     if ($existing -notcontains "origin") {

>>       Run "git remote add origin $RemoteUrl"

>>     } else {

>>       Run "git remote set-url origin $RemoteUrl"

>>     }

>>     Run "git push -u origin $DefaultBranch"

>>   }

>>

>>   Write-Host "✅ Git init complete." -ForegroundColor Green

>> }

>> finally {

>>   Pop-Location

>> }

>> '@

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Content\Python\vault_to_unreal.py

>> # ---------------------------

>> $vault_to_unreal = @'

>> # vault_to_unreal.py

>> # Run INSIDE Unreal Editor (Python enabled) or via:

>> # UnrealEditor.exe "Path\Project.uproject" -ExecutePythonScript="...\Content\Python\vault_to_unreal.py"

>> #

>> # What it does:

>> # - Imports FBX + PNG from a vault folder into /Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets

>> # - Creates simple master materials (BaseColor + Normal)

>> # - Creates material instances per mesh and assigns best-guess textures

>> # - Assigns MI to static meshes

>> # - Fixes up redirectors

>>

>> import os

>> import re

>> import unreal

>>

>> # ------------------------

>> # CONFIG

>> # ------------------------

>> VAULT_ROOT = r"C:\Nyghtshade_Assets_Vault"

>> DEST_ROOT  = "/Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets"

>>

>> TEXTURES_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Textures"

>> MESHES_DIR   = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Meshes"

>> MATS_DIR     = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Materials"

>>

>> CONCRETE_HINTS = ("concrete", "cement", "wall", "floor", "stone")

>> METAL_HINTS    = ("metal", "steel", "iron", "pipe", "grate", "bar")

>>

>> # ------------------------

>> # HELPERS

>> # ------------------------

>> def log(msg: str):

>>     unreal.log(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def warn(msg: str):

>>     unreal.log_warning(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def err(msg: str):

>>     unreal.log_error(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def ensure_dir(path: str):

>>     if not unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_directory_exist(path):

>>         unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.make_directory(path)

>>

>> def safe_asset_name(s: str) -> str:

>>     s = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_", s)

>>     s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s).strip("_")

>>     if not s:

>>         s = "Asset"

>>     return s[:120]

>>

>> def find_files(root: str, exts: set):

>>     out = []

>>     for base, _, files in os.walk(root):

>>         for f in files:

>>             ext = os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower()

>>             if ext in exts:

>>                 out.append(os.path.join(base, f))

>>     return out

>>

>> def import_file(src_path: str, dest_path: str, automated=True, replace=True):

>>     task = unreal.AssetImportTask()

>>     task.filename = src_path

>>     task.destination_path = dest_path

>>     task.automated = automated

>>     task.replace_existing = replace

>>     task.save = True

>>

>>     unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])

>>     return list(task.imported_object_paths or [])

>>

>> def make_master_material(name: str, dest_path: str):

>>     ensure_dir(dest_path)

>>     pkg = f"{dest_path}/{name}"

>>

>>     if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

>>         return unreal.load_asset(pkg)

>>

>>     mat = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

>>         name, dest_path, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew()

>>     )

>>

>>     mel = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary

>>

>>     # BaseColor param

>>     base_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 0)

>>     base_param.parameter_name = "BaseColorTex"

>>

>>     # Normal param

>>     norm_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 220)

>>     norm_param.parameter_name = "NormalTex"

>>     norm_param.sampler_type = unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL

>>

>>     # Roughness constant (slightly rough by default)

>>     rough = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -600, 420)

>>     rough.set_editor_property("r", 0.7)

>>

>>     mel.connect_material_property(base_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)

>>     mel.connect_material_property(norm_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)

>>     mel.connect_material_property(rough, "R", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)

>>

>>     mel.recompile_material(mat)

>>     unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

>>     return mat

>>

>> def make_material_instance(mi_name: str, parent_mat, dest_path: str):

>>     ensure_dir(dest_path)

>>     pkg = f"{dest_path}/{mi_name}"

>>

>>     if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

>>         return unreal.load_asset(pkg)

>>

>>     mi = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

>>         mi_name, dest_path, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew()

>>     )

>>     mi.set_editor_property("parent", parent_mat)

>>     unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

>>     return mi

>>

>> def set_mi_texture(mi, param_name: str, tex_asset):

>>     unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param_name, tex_asset)

>>     unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi)

>>

>> def choose_master_for_name(asset_name_lower: str) -> str:

>>     if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in METAL_HINTS):

>>         return "Master_Metal"

>>     if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in CONCRETE_HINTS):

>>         return "Master_Concrete"

>>     return "Master_Prison"

>>

>> def guess_texture_role(filename_lower: str) -> str:

>>     # crude but effective heuristics

>>     if "normal" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_n") or "_n_" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_nrm"):

>>         return "NormalTex"

>>     return "BaseColorTex"

>>

>> def assign_materials_to_mesh(mesh_asset, material_asset):

>>     if not isinstance(mesh_asset, unreal.StaticMesh):

>>         return

>>     slots = list(mesh_asset.get_editor_property("static_materials") or [])

>>     if not slots:

>>         return

>>     for i in range(len(slots)):

>>         slots[i].material_interface = material_asset

>>     mesh_asset.set_editor_property("static_materials", slots)

>>     mesh_asset.mark_package_dirty()

>>     unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh_asset)

>>

>> def fixup_redirectors(root_path: str):

>>     asset_tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

>>     redirs = []

>>     for a in unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(root_path, recursive=True, include_folder=False):

>>         obj = unreal.load_asset(a)

>>         if isinstance(obj, unreal.ObjectRedirector):

>>             redirs.append(obj)

>>     if redirs:

>>         asset_tools.fixup_redirectors(redirs)

>>         log(f"Fixup redirectors: {len(redirs)}")

>>     else:

>>         log("Fixup redirectors: none")

>>

>> def run():

>>     if not os.path.isdir(VAULT_ROOT):

>>         err(f"Vault root not found: {VAULT_ROOT}")

>>         return

>>

>>     ensure_dir(DEST_ROOT)

>>     ensure_dir(TEXTURES_DIR)

>>     ensure_dir(MESHES_DIR)

>>     ensure_dir(MATS_DIR)

>>

>>     # Create masters

>>     master_prison = make_master_material("Master_Prison", MATS_DIR)

>>     master_conc   = make_master_material("Master_Concrete", MATS_DIR)

>>     master_metal  = make_master_material("Master_Metal", MATS_DIR)

>>

>>     masters = {

>>         "Master_Prison": master_prison,

>>         "Master_Concrete": master_conc,

>>         "Master_Metal": master_metal,

>>     }

>>

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force

$Root = (Get-Location).Path



function Write-File {

  param([Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$RelPath,

        [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$Content)

  $Full = Join-Path $Root $RelPath

  $Dir  = Split-Path -Parent $Full

  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Dir | Out-Null

  $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)

  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($Full, $Content, $utf8NoBom)

  Write-Host "WROTE: $RelPath" -ForegroundColor Green

}

[CmdletBinding()]

param(

  [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

  [string]$WorkspaceRoot,



  [string[]]$Roots = @(

    "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop",

    "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\Unreal Projects",

    "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\ltvall",

    "D:\",

    "C:\"

  ),



  [string]$OutCsv = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Desktop\NH_UPROJECT_AUDIT.csv"),

  [switch]$PickBest

)



Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"



if ($PWD.Path -like "C:\Windows\System32*") { throw "Don’t run this from System32. cd to your workspace first." }

if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $WorkspaceRoot)) { throw "WorkspaceRoot not found: $WorkspaceRoot" }



function Score-UProject {

  param([string]$UProjectPath)



  $dir = Split-Path -Parent $UProjectPath

  $hasSource  = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Source")

  $hasContent = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Content")

  $hasConfig  = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Config")



  $isTemplate = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Templates\*"

  $isEngine   = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Engine\*"



  $sourceCount  = 0

  $contentCount = 0

  if ($hasSource)  { $sourceCount  = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Source")  -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }

  if ($hasContent) { $contentCount = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Content") -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }



  $score = 0

  if ($hasContent) { $score += 200 }

  if ($hasConfig)  { $score += 50 }

  if ($hasSource)  { $score += 120 }



  if ($contentCount -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(400, [int]([Math]::Log10($contentCount + 1) * 200)) }

  if ($sourceCount  -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(250, [int]([Math]::Log10($sourceCount  + 1) * 150)) }



  if ($isTemplate) { $score -= 1000 }

  if ($isEngine)   { $score -= 800 }



  if ($UProjectPath.StartsWith($WorkspaceRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {

    $score += 250

  }



  [pscustomobject]@{

    Score        = $score

    UProject     = $UProjectPath

    ProjectDir   = $dir

    HasSource    = $hasSource

    HasContent   = $hasContent

    HasConfig    = $hasConfig

    SourceCount  = $sourceCount

    ContentCount = $contentCount

    IsTemplate   = $isTemplate

    IsEngine     = $isEngine

  }

}



$scanRoots = @($WorkspaceRoot) + ($Roots | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path $_) } | Select-Object -Unique)



Write-Host "=== Foreman Audit ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

Write-Host "WorkspaceRoot: $WorkspaceRoot"

Write-Host "Scan roots:"; $scanRoots | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  - $_" }



$uprojects = foreach ($r in $scanRoots) {

  Get-ChildItem -Path $r -Filter *.uproject -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

}



if (!$uprojects) { throw "No .uproject files found under scan roots." }



$report = $uprojects | ForEach-Object { Score-UProject $_.FullName } | Sort-Object Score -Descending

$report | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation -Path $OutCsv

Write-Host "Wrote CSV: $OutCsv" -ForegroundColor Green



$top = $report | Select-Object -First 10

Write-Host "`nTop candidates:" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$top | Format-Table Score,UProject,HasSource,HasContent,SourceCount,ContentCount -AutoSize



if ($PickBest) {

  $best = $report | Select-Object -First 1

  Write-Host "`nBEST (copy these):" -ForegroundColor Green

  Write-Host ('$NH_UPROJECT   = "' + $best.UProject + '"')

  Write-Host ('$NH_PROJECTDIR = "' + $best.ProjectDir + '"')

}

'@

[CmdletBinding()]

function Zap([string]$p) {

  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($p)) { return }

  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p) {

    Write-Host "Deleting: $p" -ForegroundColor Yellow

    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $p -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

  }

}



Get-Process UnrealEditor -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -EA SilentlyContinue



Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Binaries")

Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Intermediate")

Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Saved")



if ($NukeDerivedDataCache) { Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "DerivedDataCache") }



if ($AlsoGlobalDDC) {

  $globalDDC = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache"

  Zap $globalDDC

}



Write-Host "✅ Cleanup done." -ForegroundColor Green

'@

[CmdletBinding()]

param(

  [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

  [string]$ProjectDir,



  [string]$DestSubdir = "PrisonCore",

  [switch]$UseRobocopy

)



Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"



if ($PWD.Path -like "C:\Windows\System32*") { throw "Don’t run this from System32. cd to your workspace first." }

if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir)) { throw "ProjectDir not found: $ProjectDir" }

Write-Host "Copying .uasset/.umap from:" -ForegroundColor Cyan

if ($UseRobocopy -and (Get-Command robocopy.exe -EA SilentlyContinue)) {

  & robocopy $VaultPath $dest *.uasset *.umap /E /R:1 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NJH /NJS /NP | Out-Host

  Write-Host "✅ Robocopy pass complete." -ForegroundColor Green

  exit 0

}



$items = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -Force -File -EA SilentlyContinue |

  Where-Object { $_.Extension -in ".uasset",".umap" }



if (!$items) {

  Write-Host "No .uasset/.umap files found in vault." -ForegroundColor Yellow

  exit 0

}



foreach ($it in $items) {

  $rel = $it.FullName.Substring($VaultPath.Length).TrimStart('\','/')

  $target = Join-Path $dest $rel

  $targetDir = Split-Path -Parent $target

  if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $targetDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $targetDir | Out-Null }

  Copy-Item -LiteralPath $it.FullName -Destination $target -Force

}



Write-Host ("✅ Copied {0} assets." -f $items.Count) -ForegroundColor Green

'@

[CmdletBinding()]

param(

  [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

  [string]$DefaultBranch = "main"

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

function Run([string]$cmd) {

  Write-Host ">> $cmd" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

  cmd.exe /c $cmd | Out-Host

  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Command failed: $cmd" }

}



Push-Location $RepoRoot

try {

  Run "git init"

  Run "git checkout -B $DefaultBranch"

  Run "git lfs install"



  $ga = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitattributes"

  @"

*.uasset filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

*.umap   filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

*.fbx    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

*.png    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

*.tga    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

*.wav    filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

"@ | Set-Content -Path $ga -Encoding utf8



  $gi = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitignore"

  @"

# Unreal Engine

Binaries/

DerivedDataCache/

Intermediate/

Saved/

.vscode/

.vs/

*.sln

*.opensdf

*.sdf

*.suo

*.user

*.userprefs

*.VC.db

*.VC.VC.opendb

*.pdb

*.log



# Build artifacts

Build/

"@ | Set-Content -Path $gi -Encoding utf8



  Run "git add .gitattributes .gitignore"

  Run "git add -A"

  Run "git commit -m ""Initialize UE repo + LFS tracking"""



  if ($RemoteUrl -and $RemoteUrl.Trim().Length -gt 0) {

    Run "git remote remove origin 2>nul || exit /b 0"

    Run "git remote add origin $RemoteUrl"

    Run "git push -u origin $DefaultBranch"

  }



  Write-Host "✅ Git init complete." -ForegroundColor Green

}

finally {

  Pop-Location

}

'@

# vault_to_unreal.py

# Run INSIDE Unreal Editor (Python enabled) or via:

# UnrealEditor.exe "Path\Project.uproject" -ExecutePythonScript="...\Content\Python\vault_to_unreal.py"



import os

import re

import unreal



VAULT_ROOT = r"C:\Nyghtshade_Assets_Vault"

DEST_ROOT  = "/Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets"



TEXTURES_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Textures"

MESHES_DIR   = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Meshes"

MATS_DIR     = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Materials"



CONCRETE_HINTS = ("concrete", "cement", "wall", "floor", "stone", "brick")

METAL_HINTS    = ("metal", "steel", "iron", "pipe", "grate", "bar", "mesh")



def log(msg): unreal.log(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

def warn(msg): unreal.log_warning(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

def err(msg): unreal.log_error(f"[Foreman] {msg}")



def ensure_dir(path):

    if not unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_directory_exist(path):

        unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.make_directory(path)



def safe_asset_name(s: str) -> str:

    s = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_", s)

    s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s).strip("_")

    return s[:120] if len(s) > 120 else s



def find_files(root, exts):

    out = []

    for base, _, files in os.walk(root):

        for f in files:

            ext = os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower()

            if ext in exts:

                out.append(os.path.join(base, f))

    return out



def import_file(src_path, dest_path, replace=True):

    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()

    task.filename = src_path

    task.destination_path = dest_path

    task.automated = True

    task.replace_existing = replace

    task.save = True

    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])

    return list(task.imported_object_paths or [])



def choose_master_for_name(asset_name_lower: str) -> str:

    if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in METAL_HINTS):

        return "Master_Metal"

    if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in CONCRETE_HINTS):

        return "Master_Concrete"

    return "Master_Prison"



def guess_texture_role(filename_lower: str) -> str:

    if "normal" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_n") or "_n_" in filename_lower:

        return "NormalTex"

    return "BaseColorTex"



def make_master_material(name: str, dest_path: str):

    ensure_dir(dest_path)

    pkg = f"{dest_path}/{name}"

    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

        return unreal.load_asset(pkg)



    tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

    mat = tools.create_asset(name, dest_path, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())



    mel = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary

    base_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 0)

    base_param.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "BaseColorTex")



    norm_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 220)

    norm_param.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "NormalTex")

    norm_param.set_editor_property("sampler_type", unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL)



    mel.connect_material_property(base_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)

    mel.connect_material_property(norm_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)



    mel.recompile_material(mat)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

    return mat



def make_material_instance(mi_name: str, parent_mat, dest_path: str):

    ensure_dir(dest_path)

    pkg = f"{dest_path}/{mi_name}"

    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

        return unreal.load_asset(pkg)



    tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

    mi = tools.create_asset(mi_name, dest_path, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew())

    mi.set_editor_property("parent", parent_mat)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

    return mi



def set_mi_texture(mi, param_name: str, tex_asset):

    unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param_name, tex_asset)

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi)



def assign_material_to_mesh(mesh_asset, material_asset):

    if not isinstance(mesh_asset, unreal.StaticMesh):

        return

    slots = list(mesh_asset.get_editor_property("static_materials"))

    for i in range(len(slots)):

        slots[i].material_interface = material_asset

    mesh_asset.set_editor_property("static_materials", slots)

    mesh_asset.mark_package_dirty()

    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh_asset)



def run():

    if not os.path.isdir(VAULT_ROOT):

        raise RuntimeError(f"Vault path not found: {VAULT_ROOT}")



    ensure_dir(DEST_ROOT); ensure_dir(TEXTURES_DIR); ensure_dir(MESHES_DIR); ensure_dir(MATS_DIR)



    master_prison = make_master_material("Master_Prison",   MATS_DIR)

    master_conc   = make_master_material("Master_Concrete", MATS_DIR)

    master_metal  = make_master_material("Master_Metal",    MATS_DIR)



    masters = {

        "Master_Prison": master_prison,

        "Master_Concrete": master_conc,

        "Master_Metal": master_metal,

    }



    fbx_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, (".fbx",))

    tex_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, (".png", ".tga", ".jpg", ".jpeg"))



    log(f"Found FBX: {len(fbx_files)} | Textures: {len(tex_files)}")



    texture_map = {}  # (folder_lower, basename_lower) -> texture asset

    for p in tex_files:

        imported = import_file(p, TEXTURES_DIR)

        for obj_path in imported:

            tex = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

            if isinstance(tex, unreal.Texture):

                key = (os.path.dirname(p).lower(), os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0].lower())

                texture_map[key] = tex



    for fbx in fbx_files:

        base_name = safe_asset_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(fbx))[0])

        imported = import_file(fbx, MESHES_DIR)



        mesh = None

        for obj_path in imported:

            obj = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

            if isinstance(obj, unreal.StaticMesh):

                mesh = obj

                break



        if not mesh:

            warn(f"Skipping (no StaticMesh found): {fbx}")

            continue



        parent = masters.get(choose_master_for_name(base_name.lower()), master_prison)

        mi = make_material_instance(f"MI_{base_name}", parent, MATS_DIR)



        folder = os.path.dirname(fbx).lower()

        bn_lower = base_name.lower()



        for (fld, bn), tex in texture_map.items():

            if fld == folder and (bn.startswith(bn_lower) or bn_lower in bn):

                role = guess_texture_role(bn)

                set_mi_texture(mi, role, tex)



        assign_material_to_mesh(mesh, mi)



    asset_tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

    redirs = []

    for a in unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(DEST_ROOT, recursive=True, include_folder=False):

        obj = unreal.load_asset(a)

        if isinstance(obj, unreal.ObjectRedirector):

            redirs.append(obj)

    if redirs:

        asset_tools.fixup_redirectors(redirs)



    log("✅ Vault import + materials + redirector fixup complete.")



if __name__ == "__main__":

    run()

2. Analysis of the "Buddy Network" Concept

Your idea falls squarely into the domain of Distributed Computing, Grid Computing, and Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks (DePIN), but with a unique focus on peer-to-peer (P2P) resource sharing for creative work like game development.



A. Current Landscape (What Already Exists)

You are absolutely right that renting high-performance computing (HPC) power is common.



Cloud HPC (Commercial): Services like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure offer powerful GPU instances (NVIDIA A100s, H100s) ideal for AI training and rendering. This is robust but costly.



Grid/Volunteer Computing (Academic/Scientific): Projects like Folding@Home use idle CPU/GPU cycles from millions of volunteers globally for scientific simulations. The key difference: users donate cycles for a single, massive task, not for personalized, interactive development environments.



Decentralized GPU Networks (Emerging): Companies like Akash Network or Render Network (DePIN projects) are building marketplaces where hardware owners rent out their idle GPUs to others, often using blockchain technology for payment and security. This is the closest analog to your "Buddy Network."



B. The Challenge and Novelty of the "Buddy Network"

The main hurdles for your "Buddy Network" idea are Latency and Security/Isolation.



Challenge	Existing Solution/Technology	Novelty of "Buddy Assist"

Security & Privacy	Virtual Machines (VMs), Sandbox environments.	The "Firewall" concept is critical. It must guarantee zero access to personal files and processes. This requires a hypervisor or OS-level containerization visible only to the consuming process.

Latency/Transfer	High-speed Internet (fiber), Remote Desktop Protocols (RDP), streaming technology.	Game development often needs instantaneous feedback (especially for real-time rendering or compiling). A typical consumer internet connection would introduce unacceptable latency for interactive work, making it only suitable for batch jobs (like lightmap baking, video rendering, or CI/CD builds).

Fair Scheduling	Centralized schedulers (Kubernetes).	Decentralized Scheduling is the hard part. The network needs an intelligent way to assign tasks to the best available idle peer instantly and securely.

C. Technical Feasibility (Can We Make That a Thing?)

Yes, it is theoretically possible, but it is a massive undertaking.



To make the "Buddy Network" a reality for game developers, you would need to build a specialized stack:



Peer-to-Peer Discovery: A system (perhaps using a decentralized ledger or a simple P2P overlay) to let idle PCs ("Buddies") advertise their spare CPU/GPU cycles.



Secure Sandboxing: A lightweight hypervisor or container (like Docker/Podman, but simpler for consumer use) that spins up a completely isolated execution environment on the "Buddy's" hardware when they enable "Buddy Assist." This is the firewall protection you mentioned.



Image of a decentralized compute network architecture

Shutterstock

Task Streamer/Splitter: A client-side application (which could be integrated into your existing Gemini Console!) that takes a heavy task (e.g., building a complex Shader Graph, baking a NavMesh) and automatically breaks it down into small, transmissible tasks that are sent to multiple "Buddies" for parallel processing.



Low-Latency Sync (Optional): For actual interactive work (not just batch processing), you would need ultra-low latency streaming, similar to what cloud gaming services (like GeForce Now or Stadia/Luna) use, which is difficult over heterogeneous residential networks.



Your concept moves beyond simple cloud rental and introduces a powerful community resource model, specifically addressing the cost and accessibility barriers for indie game developers. It's a great vision for a potential DePIN startup focused on creative cloud computing!

Buddy Network – Architectural Blueprint & MVP Roadmap

Component	Purpose	Technologies / Notes

Discovery & Registration



Buddy Client connects to the network.



Announces idle CPU/GPU cycles and hardware capabilities.



Receives a unique node ID and public key for secure communication.



Task Submission

Job metadata: required CPU/GPU, expected memory, priority.



Task Splitting



Job is broken into micro-tasks by Task Splitter.



Each micro-task is encrypted and signed.



Task Assignment



Scheduler selects nodes based on:



Hardware specs



Current load



Latency



Past reliability



Nodes receive tasks and execute in sandbox.



Result Collection



Tasks return to Aggregator.



Results verified via checksum / redundancy (duplicate tasks on multiple nodes for reliability).



Reward Distribution



Nodes are credited for completed work.



Optional: network token, compute credits, or gamified ranking.

Phase 1 Limitations:

No host filesystem access



No host process access



Per-job sandbox



Encrypted transport



Signed job packages and signed results



Resource caps (CPU %, GPU %, VRAM, RAM, time limits)



Kill switch for the Buddy Node user

1.2 Canonical JSON rules (so signatures actually work)

Keys sorted lexicographically



No insignificant whitespace



UTF-8



Arrays preserved order



Signature is over the canonicalized JSON bytes excluding the sig field itself

4.4 Heartbeats

Node → Broker PING, Broker → Node PONG



If no heartbeat within 2 * heartbeat_sec, broker considers node offline and requeues tasks.

6) Sandbox Execution Contract (minimum viable safety)

6.1 Filesystem

Mount input bundle read-only



Provide /work ephemeral scratch



Only allow outputs inside /work/out and /work/logs



No access to host home directories, removable drives, or system folders



6.2 Network

Default: allow only Buddy Storage endpoints



Deny RFC1918 / link-local / loopback except inside sandbox



Optional: disable network for pure deterministic tasks



6.3 GPU

GPU access only if:



image is trusted + signed



GPU driver compatibility is known



limits enforced (utilization caps if possible)



7) Minimal “Task lifecycle” state machine

Node states

OFFLINE → CONNECTING → AUTHENTICATED → IDLE → RUNNING_TASK → IDLE



at any point: PAUSED_USER_ACTIVE (Buddy Assist off) → IDLE (when re-enabled)



Task states (broker-side)

QUEUED → OFFERED → ASSIGNED → RUNNING → (SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELED)



If node drops: RUNNING → REQUEUE_PENDING → QUEUED

1) C++ Door Actor (replicated, Blueprint-friendly)



Put these in your game module (or your plugin module).

If in plugin NyghtshadeHollowCore: NYGHTSHADEHOLLOWCORE_API







NH_Door.h



#pragma once







#include "CoreMinimal.h"



#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"



#include "NH_Door.generated.h"







class UStaticMeshComponent;



class UBoxComponent;







DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnNH_DoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);







UCLASS(BlueprintType)



class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOWCORE_API ANH_Door : public AActor



{



	GENERATED_BODY()







public:



	ANH_Door();







	UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Door")



	UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;







	// Physical blocker (what actually stops characters)



	UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Door")



	UBoxComponent* Blocker;







	UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Door")



	bool bStartLocked = false;







	UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly, Category="Door")



	bool bIsLocked = false;







	UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable, Category="Door")



	FOnNH_DoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;







	UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Door")



	void LockDoor();







	UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Door")



	void UnlockDoor();







	UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Door")



	void SetLocked(bool bLocked);







protected:



	virtual void BeginPlay() override;



	virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;







	UFUNCTION()



	void OnRep_LockState();







	UFUNCTION(Server, Reliable)



	void ServerSetLocked(bool bLocked);







private:



	void ApplyLockState(bool bBroadcast);



};



NH_Door.cpp



#include "NH_Door.h"







#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"



#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"







ANH_Door::ANH_Door()



{



	bReplicates = true;



	SetReplicateMovement(true);







	DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));



	RootComponent = DoorMesh;







	// Door mesh can be cosmetic or physical; we keep the "real block" separate.



	DoorMesh->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);



	DoorMesh->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(false);







	Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));



	Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);



	Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName(TEXT("BlockAll"));



	Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);







	// This helps nav when runtime generation allows it



	Blocker->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(true);



	Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);



}







void ANH_Door::BeginPlay()



{



	Super::BeginPlay();



	bIsLocked = bStartLocked;



	ApplyLockState(false);



}







void ANH_Door::LockDoor()



{



	SetLocked(true);



}







void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()



{



	SetLocked(false);



}







void ANH_Door::SetLocked(bool bLocked)



{



	// Authority decides. Clients request.



	if (HasAuthority())



	{



		if (bIsLocked != bLocked)



		{



			bIsLocked = bLocked;



			ApplyLockState(true);



		}



		return;



	}







	ServerSetLocked(bLocked);



}







void ANH_Door::ServerSetLocked_Implementation(bool bLocked)



{



	SetLocked(bLocked);



}







void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()



{



	ApplyLockState(true);



}







void ANH_Door::ApplyLockState(bool bBroadcast)



{



	Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);







	if (bBroadcast)



	{



		OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);



	}



}







void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const



{



	Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);



	DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);



}



2) Lockdown Wiring (ScheduleManager / GameRules)



You already have a “ScheduleManager/GameRules/whatever-is-authoritative” pattern in that file 



Skip to content







, so we do this the sane way: toggle lockdown, iterate doors by tag, lock/unlock.







Add to your manager header



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category="Lockdown")



void StartLockdown();

void EndLockdown();







UFUNCTION(Exec)



void Lockdown(int32 bEnable);



Add to your manager cpp



#include "NH_Door.h"



#include "EngineUtils.h"







static const FName TAG_LockdownDoor(TEXT("LockdownDoor"));







void AYourScheduleManager::StartLockdown()



{



	// bLockdownActive = true; // if you track it



	for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)



	{



		if (It->ActorHasTag(TAG_LockdownDoor))



		{



			It->LockDoor();



		}



	}



}







void AYourScheduleManager::EndLockdown()



{



	// bLockdownActive = false;



	for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)



	{



		if (It->ActorHasTag(TAG_LockdownDoor))



		{



			It->UnlockDoor();



		}



	}



}







void AYourScheduleManager::Lockdown(int32 bEnable)



{



	if (bEnable != 0) StartLockdown();



	else EndLockdown();



}

That is a deeply visionary and fascinating concept! Your idea of a "Buddy Network" for decentralized CPU and GPU sharing—especially for game developers—touches upon existing technologies but proposes a novel, secure, and community-driven application.  Before addressing your question about the "Buddy Network," let I will first finish updating the GITHUB_GUIDE.md file with the final two steps we discussed previously, as that file is currently open and incomplete.  1. Updating the GITHUB_GUIDE.md I'll add the necessary steps for Git staging and pushing the repository.  2. Analysis of the "Buddy Network" Concept Your idea falls squarely into the domain of Distributed Computing, Grid Computing, and Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks (DePIN), but with a unique focus on peer-to-peer (P2P) resource sharing for creative work like game development.  A. Current Landscape (What Already Exists) You are absolutely right that renting high-performance computing (HPC) power is common.  Cloud HPC (Commercial): Services like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure offer powerful GPU instances (NVIDIA A100s, H100s) ideal for AI training and rendering. This is robust but costly.  Grid/Volunteer Computing (Academic/Scientific): Projects like Folding@Home use idle CPU/GPU cycles from millions of volunteers globally for scientific simulations. The key difference: users donate cycles for a single, massive task, not for personalized, interactive development environments.  Decentralized GPU Networks (Emerging): Companies like Akash Network or Render Network (DePIN projects) are building marketplaces where hardware owners rent out their idle GPUs to others, often using blockchain technology for payment and security. This is the closest analog to your "Buddy Network."  B. The Challenge and Novelty of the "Buddy Network" The main hurdles for your "Buddy Network" idea are Latency and Security/Isolation.  Challenge	Existing Solution/Technology	Novelty of "Buddy Assist" Security & Privacy	Virtual Machines (VMs), Sandbox environments.	The "Firewall" concept is critical. When Buddy Assist is enabled, all tasks run inside an isolated execution sandbox that has:  No access to your filesystem  No access to user directories  No access to running applications  No access to credentials, browsers, or keystrokes  The sandbox is created fresh per job and destroyed immediately after execution. Nothing persists.  Think of it like a disposable virtual room with no doors to the rest of your house.  Q2: What technology enforces this isolation? Buddy Network uses a multi-layer isolation model, not a single line of defense:  Layer 1: OS-Level Containment Tasks execute inside containers or WASM runtimes  No host process visibility  No host syscall escalation  Layer 2: Resource Whitelisting CPU cores and GPU queues are explicitly assigned  Memory access is capped and scoped  No DMA access to host memory  Layer 3: Network Hardening Outbound traffic is restricted to the scheduler and result endpoint  No peer-to-peer lateral access  Encrypted transport only  Even if a task were malicious, it would be trapped in a box with nothing to touch.  Q3: Can a job spy on my system or other jobs? No.  Each job runs in its own isolated sandbox with:  No shared memory  No shared GPU context  No visibility into other tasks  Jobs cannot see:  Other jobs  Other nodes  The scheduler logic  Your machine state  They compute. They return results. They die.  Q4: What exactly can my hardware be used for? Only pre-approved, deterministic workloads, such as:  Shader compilation  Lightmap baking  Rendering frames  AI model training segments  Build and CI-style tasks  Buddy Network does not allow:  Arbitrary code execution  Background services  Persistent processes  Crypto mining  Network scanning  File processing outside the sandbox  If a task doesn’t fit the compute-only model, it doesn’t run.  Q5: How do I control when my machine participates? You are always in control.  Buddy Assist supports:  Manual on/off toggle  Idle-only mode  Battery-aware throttling  Plugged-in full-power mode (“Deep Sea”)  Hard CPU/GPU caps  If you move your mouse, launch a game, or unplug power, the node backs off automatically.  No fighting you for resources. No surprises.  Q6: What happens if my machine crashes mid-task? Nothing dramatic.  The task is marked incomplete  The scheduler reassigns it to another node  You are not penalized  Partial results are discarded  The system is built for unreliable nodes. That’s the whole point.  Q7: How is result integrity verified? Every task result is:  Checksummed  Signed  Optionally duplicated across nodes  If results don’t match, they are rejected and recomputed elsewhere.  Cheating the system is more expensive than participating honestly.  Q8: Is Buddy Network decentralized or centralized? Hybrid by design.  Task scheduling and verification are coordinated  Execution is fully decentralized  No single node is trusted  No single node can affect outcomes  This avoids the chaos of pure P2P while avoiding the choke points of pure cloud.  Q9: Can Buddy Network be used to attack others? No.  No raw networking  No arbitrary payloads  No peer scanning  No external target access  Buddy Network is compute, not command-and-control.  Q10: Why should I trust this over Big Cloud providers? You shouldn’t trust it blindly. No “trust us bro.”  Technical FAQ – Buddy Network Security & Architecture Q1: Does Buddy Network have access to my personal files? No. Zero. Not even by accident.  When Buddy Assist is enabled, all tasks run inside an isolated execution sandbox that has:  No access to your filesystem  No access to user directories  No access to running applications  No access to credentials, browsers, or keystrokes  The sandbox is created fresh per job and destroyed immediately after execution. Nothing persists.  Think of it like a disposable virtual room with no doors to the rest of your house.  Q2: What technology enforces this isolation? Buddy Network uses a multi-layer isolation model, not a single line of defense:  Layer 1: OS-Level Containment Tasks execute inside containers or WASM runtimes  No host process visibility  No host syscall escalation  Layer 2: Resource Whitelisting CPU cores and GPU queues are explicitly assigned  Memory access is capped and scoped  No DMA access to host memory  Layer 3: Network Hardening Outbound traffic is restricted to the scheduler and result endpoint  No peer-to-peer lateral access  Encrypted transport only  Even if a task were malicious, it would be trapped in a box with nothing to touch.  Q3: Can a job spy on my system or other jobs? No.  Each job runs in its own isolated sandbox with:  No shared memory  No shared GPU context  No visibility into other tasks  Jobs cannot see:  Other jobs  Other nodes  The scheduler logic  Your machine state  They compute. They return results. They die.  Q4: What exactly can my hardware be used for? Only pre-approved, deterministic workloads, such as:  Shader compilation  Lightmap baking  Rendering frames  AI model training segments  Build and CI-style tasks  Buddy Network does not allow:  Arbitrary code execution  Background services  Persistent processes  Crypto mining  Network scanning  File processing outside the sandbox  If a task doesn’t fit the compute-only model, it doesn’t run.  Q5: How do I control when my machine participates? You are always in control.  Buddy Assist supports:  Manual on/off toggle  Idle-only mode  Battery-aware throttling  Plugged-in full-power mode (“Deep Sea”)  Hard CPU/GPU caps  If you move your mouse, launch a game, or unplug power, the node backs off automatically.  No fighting you for resources. No surprises.  Q6: What happens if my machine crashes mid-task? Nothing dramatic.  The task is marked incomplete  The scheduler reassigns it to another node  You are not penalized  Partial results are discarded  The system is built for unreliable nodes. That’s the whole point.  Q7: How is result integrity verified? Every task result is:  Checksummed  Signed  Optionally duplicated across nodes  If results don’t match, they are rejected and recomputed elsewhere.  Cheating the system is more expensive than participating honestly.  Q8: Is Buddy Network decentralized or centralized? Hybrid by design.  Task scheduling and verification are coordinated  Execution is fully decentralized  No single node is trusted  No single node can affect outcomes  This avoids the chaos of pure P2P while avoiding the choke points of pure cloud.  Q9: Can Buddy Network be used to attack others? No.  No raw networking  No arbitrary payloads  No peer scanning  No external target access  Buddy Network is compute, not command-and-control.  Q10: Why should I trust this over Big Cloud providers? You shouldn’t trust it blindly. You should trust it because:  The sandbox is inspectable  The client is auditable  The workload types are constrained  The incentives align with transparency  You can turn it off instantly  Cloud providers sell you power. Buddy Network lets you own participation. Common Git commands
The GitLab Docs website is now available in Japanese!
Common Git commands
Git commands save you time throughout your development workflow. This reference page contains frequently used commands for common tasks such as code changes, branch management, and history review. Each command section provides the exact syntax, practical examples, and links to additional documentation.

git add
Use git add to files to the staging area.

shell
git add <file_path>
You can recursively stage changes from the current working directory with git add ., or stage all changes in the Git repository with git add --all.

For more information, see Add files to your branch.

git blame
Use git blame to report which users changed which parts of a file.

shell
git blame <file_name>
You can use git blame -L <line_start>, <line_end> to check a specific range of lines.

For more information, see Git file blame.

Example
To check which user most recently modified line five of example.txt:

shell
$ git blame -L 5, 5 example.txt
123abc (Zhang Wei 2021-07-04 12:23:04 +0000 5)
git bisect
Use git bisectto use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug.

Start by identifying a commit that is “bad” (contains the bug) and a commit that is “good” (doesn’t contain the bug).

shell
git bisect start
git bisect bad                 # Current version is bad
git bisect good v2.6.13-rc2    # v2.6.13-rc2 is known to be good
git bisect then picks a commit in between the two points and asks you identify if the commit is “good” or “bad” with git bisect goodor git bisect bad. Repeat the process until the commit is found.

git checkout
Use git checkout to switch to a specific branch.

shell
git checkout <branch_name>
To create a new branch and switch to it, use git checkout -b <branch_name>.

For more information, see Create a Git branch for your changes.

git clone
Use git clone to copy an existing Git repository.

shell
git clone <repository>
For more information, see Clone a Git repository to your local computer.

git commit
Use git commit to commits staged changes to the repository.

shell
git commit -m "<commit_message>"
If the commit message contains a blank line, the first line becomes the commit subject while the remainder becomes the commit body. Use the subject to briefly summarize a change, and the commit body to provide additional details.

For more information, see Stage, commit, and push changes.

git commit --amend
Use git commit --amend to modify the most recent commit.

shell
git commit --amend
git diff
Use git diff to view the differences between your local unstaged changes and the latest version that you cloned or pulled.

shell
git diff
You can display the difference (or diff) between your local changes and the most recent version of a branch. View a diff to understand your local changes before you commit them to the branch.

To compare your changes against a specific branch, run:

shell
git diff <branch>
In the output:

Lines with additions begin with a plus (+) and are displayed in green.
Lines with removals or changes begin with a minus (-) and are displayed in red.
git init
Use git init to initialize a directory so Git tracks it as a repository.

shell
git init
A .git file with configuration and log files is added to the directory. You shouldn’t edit the .git file directly.

The default branch is set to main. You can change the name of the default branch with git branch -m <branch_name>, or initialize with git init -b <branch_name>.

git pull
Use git pull to get all the changes made by users after the last time you cloned or pulled the project.

shell
git pull <optional_remote> <branch_name>
git push
Use git push to update remote refs.

shell
git push
For more information, see Stage, commit, and push changes.

git reflog
Use git reflog to display a list of changes to the Git reference logs.

shell
git reflog
By default, git reflog shows a list of changes to HEAD.

For more information, see Undo changes.

git remote add
Use git remote add to tell Git which remote repository in GitLab is linked to a local directory.

shell
git remote add <remote_name> <repository_url>
When you clone a repository, by default the source repository is associated with the remote name origin.

For more information on configuring additional remotes, see Forks.

git log
Use git log to display a list of commits in chronological order.

shell
git log
git show
Use git show to show information about an object in Git.

Example
To see what commit HEAD points to:

shell
$ git show HEAD
commit ab123c (HEAD -> main, origin/main, origin/HEAD)
git merge
Use git merge to combine the changes from one branch with another.

For more information on an alternative to git merge, see Rebase to address merge conflicts.

Example
To apply the changes in feature_branch to the target_branch:

shell
git checkout target_branch
git merge feature_branch
git rebase
Use git rebase to rewrite the commit history of a branch.

shell
git rebase <branch_name>
You can use git rebase to resolve merge conflicts.

In most cases, you want to rebase against the default branch.

git reset
Use git reset to undo a commit and rewind the commit history and continue on from an earlier commit.

shell
git reset
For more information, see Undo changes.

git status
Use git status to show the status of the working directory and staged files.

shell
git status
When you add, change, or delete files, Git can show you the changes.

Thought for 13s
Got it, Lee Gier. I’ll keep that Git command list “on file” so you can yank it back out later without re-pasting a whole webpage like it’s 2009.

Now, how to use those commands to your favor (aka: how to stop Git from feeling like a haunted house).

The “daily driver” flow (the one you should live in)
1) See what’s going on
git status
This is your dashboard. Run it constantly. If you don’t, you deserve the confusion you get.

2) Review what you actually changed
git diff
Before you stage anything, look at what you did. Saves you from committing garbage.

3) Stage what you want
git add <file_path>
git add .
git add --all
git add <file>: controlled, clean, professional.

git add .: fast, sometimes reckless.

git add --all: includes deletions too (good when you removed files).

4) Commit with a message that means something
git commit -m "Short, clear summary"
Make commits small and focused. One change per commit = easier fixes later.

5) Send it to the remote (GitHub/GitLab)
git push
6) Pull others’ work (or your other machine’s work)
git pull
Branch power (how you avoid breaking your main branch like an amateur)
Switch branches
git checkout <branch_name>
Create a new branch and jump to it
git checkout -b <branch_name>
Use branches for everything: features, experiments, fixes. Your main branch should be boring and stable.

“Find what changed” tools (aka: blame with purpose)
Who touched this line?
git blame <file_name>
git blame -L 5,5 <file_name>
This is how you find:

which commit introduced a change

who wrote it

when it happened

Not for drama. For debugging.

History intel (how to read the timeline like a detective)
Show the commit list
git log
Show exactly what a commit (or HEAD) is
git show HEAD
git show <commit_hash>
If you’re ever unsure “what am I about to push”, git log + git show answers that.

Merging vs rebasing (how to not create spaghetti history)
Merge (safe, keeps history)
git checkout target_branch
git merge feature_branch
Good when working with a team or when you want a clear “this got merged here” record.

Rebase (clean history, rewrites commits)
git rebase <branch_name>
Great for cleaning up your feature branch before merging, but don’t rebase shared branches unless you enjoy chaos.

Undo safety net (how you recover from “I messed up”)
Your lifeline
git reflog
This shows where HEAD has been, even after resets and rebases. It’s basically Git saying “I saw what you did.”

Reset (use carefully)
git reset
Reset is powerful, but it can also delete work depending on options. The smart move: use git reflog first if you’re uncertain.

Debugging a nightmare bug (bisect is a cheat code)
Find the commit that introduced a bug
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good <known_good_commit>
Then Git walks you through commits to find the exact offender. This is how you win when a bug “randomly appeared”.

Remotes (how you connect your local repo to GitLab/GitHub)
git remote add <remote_name> <repository_url>
Typical:

remote name: origin

URL: your GitLab/GitHub repo link

Then:

git push
The “use Git to your advantage” mindset
Commit early, commit often (small commits). It makes rollbacks painless.

Use branches so experiments don’t nuke your working code.

Use diff before add so you stage intentionally.

Use reflog when you panic. It’s your “undo button” for head movement.

Use bisect when you’re guessing. Guessing is for cavemen.

If you follow that, Git stops being a horror movie and starts being a time machine you control.

        ^E or *  Search multiple files (pass thru END OF FILE).
        ^F or @  Start search at FIRST file (for /) or last file (for ?).
        ^K       Highlight matches, but don't move (KEEP position).
        ^R       Don't use REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.
        ^W       WRAP search if no match found.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           JUMPING

  g  <  ESC-<       *  Go to first line in file (or line N).
  G  >  ESC->       *  Go to last line in file (or line N).
  p  %              *  Go to beginning of file (or N percent into file).
  t                 *  Go to the (N-th) next tag.
  T                 *  Go to the (N-th) previous tag.
  {  (  [           *  Find close bracket } ) ].
  }  )  ]           *  Find open bracket { ( [.
  ESC-^F <c1> <c2>  *  Find close bracket <c2>.
  ESC-^B <c1> <c2>  *  Find open bracket <c1>.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Each "find close bracket" command goes forward to the close bracket 
          matching the (N-th) open bracket in the top line.
        Each "find open bracket" command goes backward to the open bracket 
          matching the (N-th) close bracket in the bottom line.

  m<letter>            Mark the current top line with <letter>.
  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.
  '<letter>            Go to a previously marked position.
  ''                   Go to the previous position.
  ^X^X                 Same as '.
  ESC-M<letter>        Clear a mark.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        A mark is any upper-case or lower-case letter.
        Certain marks are predefined:
             ^  means  beginning of the file
             $  means  end of the file
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                        CHANGING FILES

  :e [file]            Examine a new file.
  ^X^V                 Same as :e.
  :n                *  Examine the (N-th) next file from the command line.
  :p                *  Examine the (N-th) previous file from the command line.
  :x                *  Examine the first (or N-th) file from the command line.
  :d                   Delete the current file from the command line list.
  =  ^G  :f            Print current file name.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                    MISCELLANEOUS COMMANDS

  -<flag>              Toggle a command line option [see OPTIONS below].
  --<name>             Toggle a command line option, by name.
  _<flag>              Display the setting of a command line option.
  __<name>             Display the setting of an option, by name.
  +cmd                 Execute the less cmd each time a new file is examined.

  !command             Execute the shell command with $SHELL.
  |Xcommand            Pipe file between current pos & mark X to shell command
.
  s file               Save input to a file.
  v                    Edit the current file with $VISUAL or $EDITOR.
  V                    Print version number of "less".
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           OPTIONS

        Most options may be changed either on the command line,
        or from within less by using the - or -- command.
        Options may be given in one of two forms: either a single
        character preceded by a -, or a name preceded by --.

  -?  ........  --help
                  Display help (from command line).
  -a  ........  --search-skip-screen
                  Search skips current screen.
  -A  ........  --SEARCH-SKIP-SCREEN
                  Search starts just after target line.
  -b [N]  ....  --buffers=[N]
                  Number of buffers.
  -B  ........  --auto-buffers
                  Don't automatically allocate buffers for pipes.
  -c  ........  --clear-screen
                  Repaint by clearing rather than scrolling.
  -d  ........  --dumb
                  Dumb terminal.
  -D xcolor  .  --color=xcolor
                  Set screen colors.
  -e  -E  ....  --quit-at-eof  --QUIT-AT-EOF
                  Quit at end of file.
  -f  ........  --force
                  Force open non-regular files.
  -F  ........  --quit-if-one-screen
                  Quit if entire file fits on first screen.
  -g  ........  --hilite-search
                  Highlight only last match for searches.
  -G  ........  --HILITE-SEARCH
                  Don't highlight any matches for searches.
  -h [N]  ....  --max-back-scroll=[N]
                  Backward scroll limit.
  -i  ........  --ignore-case
                  Ignore case in searches that do not contain uppercase.
  -I  ........  --IGNORE-CASE
                  Ignore case in all searches.
  -j [N]  ....  --jump-target=[N]
                  Screen position of target lines.
  -J  ........  --status-column
                  Display a status column at left edge of screen.
  -k [file]  .  --lesskey-file=[file]
                  Use a lesskey file.
  -K  ........  --quit-on-intr
                  Exit less in response to ctrl-C.
  -L  ........  --no-lessopen
                  Ignore the LESSOPEN environment variable.
  -m  -M  ....  --long-prompt  --LONG-PROMPT
                  Set prompt style.
  -n  -N  ....  --line-numbers  --LINE-NUMBERS
                  Don't use line numbers.
  -o [file]  .  --log-file=[file]
                  Copy to log file (standard input only).
  -O [file]  .  --LOG-FILE=[file]
                  Copy to log file (unconditionally overwrite).
  -p [pattern]  --pattern=[pattern]
                  Start at pattern (from command line).
  -P [prompt]   --prompt=[prompt]
                  Define new prompt.
  -q  -Q  ....  --quiet  --QUIET  --silent --SILENT
                  Quiet the terminal bell.
  -r  -R  ....  --raw-control-chars  --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS
                  Output "raw" control characters.
  -s  ........  --squeeze-blank-lines
                  Squeeze multiple blank lines.
  -S  ........  --chop-long-lines
                  Chop (truncate) long lines rather than wrapping.
  -t [tag]  ..  --tag=[tag]
                  Find a tag.
  -T [tagsfile] --tag-file=[tagsfile]
                  Use an alternate tags file.
  -u  -U  ....  --underline-special  --UNDERLINE-SPECIAL
                  Change handling of backspaces.
  -V  ........  --version
                  Display the version number of "less".
  -w  ........  --hilite-unread
                  Highlight first new line after forward-screen.
  -W  ........  --HILITE-UNREAD
                  Highlight first new line after any forward movement.
  -x [N[,...]]  --tabs=[N[,...]]
                  Set tab stops.
  -X  ........  --no-init
                  Don't use termcap init/deinit strings.
  -y [N]  ....  --max-forw-scroll=[N]
                  Forward scroll limit.
  -z [N]  ....  --window=[N]
                  Set size of window.
  -" [c[c]]  .  --quotes=[c[c]]
                  Set shell quote characters.
  -~  ........  --tilde
                  Don't display tildes after end of file.
  -# [N]  ....  --shift=[N]
                  Set horizontal scroll amount (0 = one half screen width).
                --file-size
                  Automatically determine the size of the input file.
                --follow-name
                  The F command changes files if the input file is renamed.
                --incsearch
                  Search file as each pattern character is typed in.
                --line-num-width=N
                  Set the width of the -N line number field to N characters.
                --mouse
                  Enable mouse input.
                --no-keypad
                  Don't send termcap keypad init/deinit strings.
                --no-histdups
                  Remove duplicates from command history.
                --rscroll=C
                  Set the character used to mark truncated lines.
                --save-marks
                  Retain marks across invocations of less.
                --status-col-width=N
                  Set the width of the -J status column to N characters.
                --use-backslash
                  Subsequent options use backslash as escape char.
                --use-color
                  Enables colored text.
                --wheel-lines=N
                  Each click of the mouse wheel moves N lines.


 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          LINE EDITING

        These keys can be used to edit text being entered 
        on the "command line" at the bottom of the screen.

 RightArrow ..................... ESC-l ... Move cursor right one character.
 LeftArrow ...................... ESC-h ... Move cursor left one character.
 ctrl-RightArrow  ESC-RightArrow  ESC-w ... Move cursor right one word.
 ctrl-LeftArrow   ESC-LeftArrow   ESC-b ... Move cursor left one word.
 HOME ........................... ESC-0 ... Move cursor to start of line.
 END ............................ ESC-$ ... Move cursor to end of line.
 BACKSPACE ................................ Delete char to left of cursor.
 DELETE ......................... ESC-x ... Delete char under cursor.
 ctrl-BACKSPACE   ESC-BACKSPACE ........... Delete word to left of cursor.
 ctrl-DELETE .... ESC-DELETE .... ESC-X ... Delete word under cursor.
 ctrl-U ......... ESC (MS-DOS only) ....... Delete entire line.
 UpArrow ........................ ESC-k ... Retrieve previous command line.
 DownArrow ...................... ESC-j ... Retrieve next command line.
 TAB ...................................... Complete filename & cycle.
 SHIFT-TAB ...................... ESC-TAB   Complete filename & reverse cycle.
 ctrl-L ................................... Complete filename, list all.

                   SUMMARY OF LESS COMMANDS

      Commands marked with * may be preceded by a number, N.
      Notes in parentheses indicate the behavior if N is given.
      A key preceded by a caret indicates the Ctrl key; thus ^K is ctrl-K.

  h  H                 Display this help.
  q  :q  Q  :Q  ZZ     Exit.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  f  ^F  ^V  SPACE  *  Forward  one window (or N lines).
  b  ^B  ESC-v      *  Backward one window (or N lines).
  z                 *  Forward  one window (and set window to N).

                           MOVING

  e  ^E  j  ^N  CR  *  Forward  one line   (or N lines).
  y  ^Y  k  ^K  ^P  *  Backward one line   (or N lines).
  f  ^F  ^V  SPACE  *  Forward  one window (or N lines).
  b  ^B  ESC-v      *  Backward one window (or N lines).
  z                 *  Forward  one window (and set window to N).
  w                 *  Backward one window (and set window to N).
  ESC-SPACE         *  Forward  one window, but don't stop at end-of-file.
  d  ^D             *  Forward  one half-window (and set half-window to N).
  u  ^U             *  Backward one half-window (and set half-window to N).
  ESC-)  RightArrow *  Right one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-(  LeftArrow  *  Left  one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-}  ^RightArrow   Right to last column displayed.
  ESC-{  ^LeftArrow    Left  to first column.
  F                    Forward forever; like "tail -f".
  ESC-F                Like F but stop when search pattern is found.
  r  ^R  ^L            Repaint screen.
  R                    Repaint screen, discarding buffered input.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Default "window" is the screen height.
        Default "half-window" is half of the screen height.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          SEARCHING

  /pattern          *  Search forward for (N-th) matching line.
  ?pattern          *  Search backward for (N-th) matching line.
  n                 *  Repeat previous search (for N-th occurrence).
  N                 *  Repeat previous search in reverse direction.
  ESC-n             *  Repeat previous search, spanning files.
  ESC-N             *  Repeat previous search, reverse dir. & spanning files.
  ESC-u                Undo (toggle) search highlighting.
  ESC-U                Clear search highlighting.
  &pattern          *  Display only matching lines.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        A search pattern may begin with one or more of:
        ^N or !  Search for NON-matching lines.
        ^E or *  Search multiple files (pass thru END OF FILE).
        ^F or @  Start search at FIRST file (for /) or last file (for ?).
        ^K       Highlight matches, but don't move (KEEP position).
        ^R       Don't use REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.
        ^W       WRAP search if no match found.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           JUMPING

  g  <  ESC-<       *  Go to first line in file (or line N).
  G  >  ESC->       *  Go to last line in file (or line N).
  p  %              *  Go to beginning of file (or N percent into file).
  t                 *  Go to the (N-th) next tag.
  T                 *  Go to the (N-th) previous tag.
  {  (  [           *  Find close bracket } ) ].
  }  )  ]           *  Find open bracket { ( [.
  ESC-^F <c1> <c2>  *  Find close bracket <c2>.
  ESC-^B <c1> <c2>  *  Find open bracket <c1>.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Each "find close bracket" command goes forward to the close bracket 
          matching the (N-th) open bracket in the top line.
        Each "find open bracket" command goes backward to the open bracket 
          matching the (N-th) close bracket in the bottom line.

  m<letter>            Mark the current top line with <letter>.
  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.
  '<letter>            Go to a previously marked position.
