ChatGPT said:
That’s a full LESS command reference—the pager utility that Git and a ton of other Unix tools rely on to view long text or logs one screen at a time. Think of it as the world’s oldest scroll wheel.
Let’s decode how to use it to your advantage—especially when you’re knee-deep in a git log, a diff, or any massive file dump.

1. Basic movement (you vs. gravity)
j / ↓ / Enter: move down one line

k / ↑: move up one line

f / space: jump down one page

b: jump up one page

g: top of the file

G: bottom of the file

Tip: Pressing numbers first (like 10j) moves multiple lines at once. Because apparently, typing two keys is faster than one.

2. Searching (find what you need without your soul leaving your body)
/word – search forward for “word”

?word – search backward

n – jump to next match

N – jump to previous match

&pattern – show only matching lines

That last one’s killer. Try &ERROR inside a massive log file—you’ll only see lines with “ERROR”.

3. Jumping (your teleportation keys)
g or 1G – first line

G – last line

p or % – go to N% through the file

m<letter> – mark your spot

'<letter> – jump back to that mark

Example: mark your current place with ma, scroll around, and go back with 'a.

4. Exiting (the one thing everyone forgets)
q or :q or ZZ – any of these will quit.
No ritual incantations required.

5. Tricks that make you look like a wizard
F – follow the file like tail -f (great for live logs).

R – reload the file if new data came in.

| – pipe the viewed text to another command (|grep, etc.).

v – open the file in your default editor ($EDITOR like vim or nano).

-N – show line numbers (toggle anytime).

6. Why this matters for Git
You’re using less constantly without realizing it:

git log pages results through less

git diff does the same

Pressing /, n, or G works inside Git output too

That means you can, say:

run git diff, press /NPC to jump to every NPC-related change

or git log, then /2026-01-04 to find today’s commits fast

If you use less right, you’ll never scroll like a mortal again. It’s your microscope, telescope, and escape hatch all in one terminal window.

You said:
        ^F or @  Start search at FIRST file (for /) or last file (for ?).
        ^K       Highlight matches, but don't move (KEEP position).
        ^R       Don't use REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.
        ^W       WRAP search if no match found.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           JUMPING

  g  <  ESC-<       *  Go to first line in file (or line N).
  G  >  ESC->       *  Go to last line in file (or line N).
  p  %              *  Go to beginning of file (or N percent into file).
  t                 *  Go to the (N-th) next tag.
  T                 *  Go to the (N-th) previous tag.
  {  (  [           *  Find close bracket } ) ].
  }  )  ]           *  Find open bracket { ( [.
  ESC-^F <c1> <c2>  *  Find close bracket <c2>.
  ESC-^B <c1> <c2>  *  Find open bracket <c1>.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Each "find close bracket" command goes forward to the close bracket 
          matching the (N-th) open bracket in the top line.
        Each "find open bracket" command goes backward to the open bracket 
          matching the (N-th) close bracket in the bottom line.

  m<letter>            Mark the current top line with <letter>.
  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.
  '<letter>            Go to a previously marked position.
  ''                   Go to the previous position.
  ^X^X                 Same as '.
  ESC-M<letter>        Clear a mark.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        A mark is any upper-case or lower-case letter.
        Certain marks are predefined:
             ^  means  beginning of the file
             $  means  end of the file
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                        CHANGING FILES

  :e [file]            Examine a new file.
  ^X^V                 Same as :e.
  :n                *  Examine the (N-th) next file from the command line.
  :p                *  Examine the (N-th) previous file from the command line.
  :x                *  Examine the first (or N-th) file from the command line.
  :d                   Delete the current file from the command line list.
  =  ^G  :f            Print current file name.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                    MISCELLANEOUS COMMANDS

  -<flag>              Toggle a command line option [see OPTIONS below].
  --<name>             Toggle a command line option, by name.
  _<flag>              Display the setting of a command line option.
  __<name>             Display the setting of an option, by name.
  +cmd                 Execute the less cmd each time a new file is examined.

  !command             Execute the shell command with $SHELL.
  |Xcommand            Pipe file between current pos & mark X to shell command
.
  s file               Save input to a file.
  v                    Edit the current file with $VISUAL or $EDITOR.
  V                    Print version number of "less".
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           OPTIONS

        Most options may be changed either on the command line,
        or from within less by using the - or -- command.
        Options may be given in one of two forms: either a single
        character preceded by a -, or a name preceded by --.

  -?  ........  --help
                  Display help (from command line).
  -a  ........  --search-skip-screen
                  Search skips current screen.
  -A  ........  --SEARCH-SKIP-SCREEN
                  Search starts just after target line.
  -b [N]  ....  --buffers=[N]
                  Number of buffers.
  -B  ........  --auto-buffers
                  Don't automatically allocate buffers for pipes.
  -c  ........  --clear-screen
                  Repaint by clearing rather than scrolling.
  -d  ........  --dumb
                  Dumb terminal.
  -D xcolor  .  --color=xcolor
                  Set screen colors.
  -e  -E  ....  --quit-at-eof  --QUIT-AT-EOF
                  Quit at end of file.
  -f  ........  --force
                  Force open non-regular files.
  -F  ........  --quit-if-one-screen
                  Quit if entire file fits on first screen.
  -g  ........  --hilite-search
                  Highlight only last match for searches.
  -G  ........  --HILITE-SEARCH
                  Don't highlight any matches for searches.
  -h [N]  ....  --max-back-scroll=[N]
                  Backward scroll limit.
  -i  ........  --ignore-case
                  Ignore case in searches that do not contain uppercase.
  -I  ........  --IGNORE-CASE
                  Ignore case in all searches.
  -j [N]  ....  --jump-target=[N]
                  Screen position of target lines.
  -J  ........  --status-column
                  Display a status column at left edge of screen.
  -k [file]  .  --lesskey-file=[file]
                  Use a lesskey file.
  -K  ........  --quit-on-intr
                  Exit less in response to ctrl-C.
  -L  ........  --no-lessopen
                  Ignore the LESSOPEN environment variable.
  -m  -M  ....  --long-prompt  --LONG-PROMPT
                  Set prompt style.
  -n  -N  ....  --line-numbers  --LINE-NUMBERS
                  Don't use line numbers.
  -o [file]  .  --log-file=[file]
                  Copy to log file (standard input only).
  -O [file]  .  --LOG-FILE=[file]
                  Copy to log file (unconditionally overwrite).
  -p [pattern]  --pattern=[pattern]
                  Start at pattern (from command line).
  -P [prompt]   --prompt=[prompt]
                  Define new prompt.
  -q  -Q  ....  --quiet  --QUIET  --silent --SILENT
                  Quiet the terminal bell.
  -r  -R  ....  --raw-control-chars  --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS
                  Output "raw" control characters.
  -s  ........  --squeeze-blank-lines
                  Squeeze multiple blank lines.
  -S  ........  --chop-long-lines
                  Chop (truncate) long lines rather than wrapping.
  -t [tag]  ..  --tag=[tag]
                  Find a tag.
  -T [tagsfile] --tag-file=[tagsfile]
                  Use an alternate tags file.
  -u  -U  ....  --underline-special  --UNDERLINE-SPECIAL
                  Change handling of backspaces.
  -V  ........  --version
                  Display the version number of "less".
  -w  ........  --hilite-unread
                  Highlight first new line after forward-screen.
  -W  ........  --HILITE-UNREAD
                  Highlight first new line after any forward movement.
  -x [N[,...]]  --tabs=[N[,...]]
                  Set tab stops.
  -X  ........  --no-init
                  Don't use termcap init/deinit strings.
  -y [N]  ....  --max-forw-scroll=[N]
                  Forward scroll limit.
  -z [N]  ....  --window=[N]
                  Set size of window.
  -" [c[c]]  .  --quotes=[c[c]]
                  Set shell quote characters.
  -~  ........  --tilde
                  Don't display tildes after end of file.
  -# [N]  ....  --shift=[N]
                  Set horizontal scroll amount (0 = one half screen width).
                --file-size
                  Automatically determine the size of the input file.
                --follow-name
                  The F command changes files if the input file is renamed.
                --incsearch
                  Search file as each pattern character is typed in.
                --line-num-width=N
                  Set the width of the -N line number field to N characters.
                --mouse
                  Enable mouse input.
                --no-keypad
                  Don't send termcap keypad init/deinit strings.
                --no-histdups
                  Remove duplicates from command history.
                --rscroll=C
                  Set the character used to mark truncated lines.
                --save-marks
                  Retain marks across invocations of less.
                --status-col-width=N
                  Set the width of the -J status column to N characters.
                --use-backslash
                  Subsequent options use backslash as escape char.
                --use-color
                  Enables colored text.
                --wheel-lines=N
                  Each click of the mouse wheel moves N lines.


 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          LINE EDITING

        These keys can be used to edit text being entered 
        on the "command line" at the bottom of the screen.

 RightArrow ..................... ESC-l ... Move cursor right one character.
 LeftArrow ...................... ESC-h ... Move cursor left one character.
 ctrl-RightArrow  ESC-RightArrow  ESC-w ... Move cursor right one word.
 ctrl-LeftArrow   ESC-LeftArrow   ESC-b ... Move cursor left one word.
 HOME ........................... ESC-0 ... Move cursor to start of line.
 END ............................ ESC-$ ... Move cursor to end of line.
 BACKSPACE ................................ Delete char to left of cursor.
 DELETE ......................... ESC-x ... Delete char under cursor.
 ctrl-BACKSPACE   ESC-BACKSPACE ........... Delete word to left of cursor.
 ctrl-DELETE .... ESC-DELETE .... ESC-X ... Delete word under cursor.
 ctrl-U ......... ESC (MS-DOS only) ....... Delete entire line.
 UpArrow ........................ ESC-k ... Retrieve previous command line.
 DownArrow ...................... ESC-j ... Retrieve next command line.
 TAB ...................................... Complete filename & cycle.
 SHIFT-TAB ...................... ESC-TAB   Complete filename & reverse cycle.
 ctrl-L ................................... Complete filename, list all.

                   SUMMARY OF LESS COMMANDS

      Commands marked with * may be preceded by a number, N.
      Notes in parentheses indicate the behavior if N is given.
      A key preceded by a caret indicates the Ctrl key; thus ^K is ctrl-K.

  ESC-(  LeftArrow  *  Left  one half screen width (or N positions).
  ESC-}  ^RightArrow   Right to last column displayed.
  ESC-{  ^LeftArrow    Left  to first column.
  F                    Forward forever; like "tail -f".
  ESC-F                Like F but stop when search pattern is found.
  r  ^R  ^L            Repaint screen.
  R                    Repaint screen, discarding buffered input.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Default "window" is the screen height.
        Default "half-window" is half of the screen height.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          SEARCHING

  /pattern          *  Search forward for (N-th) matching line.
  ?pattern          *  Search backward for (N-th) matching line.
  n                 *  Repeat previous search (for N-th occurrence).
  N                 *  Repeat previous search in reverse direction.
  ESC-n             *  Repeat previous search, spanning files.
  ESC-N             *  Repeat previous search, reverse dir. & spanning files.
  ESC-u                Undo (toggle) search highlighting.
  ESC-U                Clear search highlighting.
  &pattern          *  Display only matching lines.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        A search pattern may begin with one or more of:
        ^N or !  Search for NON-matching lines.
        ^E or *  Search multiple files (pass thru END OF FILE).
        ^F or @  Start search at FIRST file (for /) or last file (for ?).
        ^K       Highlight matches, but don't move (KEEP position).
        ^R       Don't use REGULAR EXPRESSIONS.
        ^W       WRAP search if no match found.
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                           JUMPING

  g  <  ESC-<       *  Go to first line in file (or line N).
  G  >  ESC->       *  Go to last line in file (or line N).
  p  %              *  Go to beginning of file (or N percent into file).
  t                 *  Go to the (N-th) next tag.
  T                 *  Go to the (N-th) previous tag.
  {  (  [           *  Find close bracket } ) ].
  }  )  ]           *  Find open bracket { ( [.
  ESC-^F <c1> <c2>  *  Find close bracket <c2>.
  ESC-^B <c1> <c2>  *  Find open bracket <c1>.
        ---------------------------------------------------
        Each "find close bracket" command goes forward to the close bracket 
          matching the (N-th) open bracket in the top line.
        Each "find open bracket" command goes backward to the open bracket 
          matching the (N-th) close bracket in the bottom line.

  m<letter>            Mark the current top line with <letter>.
  M<letter>            Mark the current bottom line with <letter>.
  '<letter>            Go to a previously marked position.

Thought for 33s
You’re staring at less help text because Git dumps you into less whenever output is long. Congrats: you’ve met the ancient terminal gremlin that controls your scrolling.

Here’s what that specific chunk means, and how to weaponize it instead of getting trapped in it.

Those “weird” search modifiers (the ones you pasted)
In less, search is normally:

/pattern forward

?pattern backward

n next match

N previous match

Now the “prefixes” you pasted are special control keys you press right after you type / (or ?) and before the pattern:

^W = Wrap search
If it doesn’t find it below, it jumps back to the top and keeps looking.
Practical: stop missing matches just because you started in the middle.

^R = Literal search (no regex)
Less uses regex by default. This makes it treat your pattern like plain text.
Practical: search for stuff like *.uproject, a+b, [submodule without regex headaches.

^K = Highlight matches but don’t move
It lights up matches on screen without jumping you away.
Practical: scan the current view for hits without losing your place.

^E / * = Search across multiple files (only matters if you opened less with multiple files)
Practical: rare unless you did less file1 file2 file3 or Git invoked a multi-file pager.

^F / @ = Start at FIRST/LAST file (again, multi-file mode)

Reality check: most of the time you’ll mainly use /, n, N, and occasionally ^R and ^W.

Jumping + Marks (this is the “I don’t get lost” kit)
These are legit power moves:

g = top, G = bottom

123g = jump to line 123

50% = jump halfway through the file

ma = mark the current position as a

'a = jump back to mark a

'' = jump back to your previous position (like “back button”)

Use case in Git output:
Open git show, hit ma at the top, search around, then 'a to snap back.

Why your terminal blew up with “syntax error near unexpected token newline”
This part of your paste tells me what happened:

/bin/bash: -c: line 1: `lessecho ... -- itory_url>'
bash: syntax error near unexpected token `newline'
Two things likely happened (both are extremely human):

1) You typed a command with angle brackets literally
Example: you typed this exactly:

git remote add <remote_name> <repository_url>
In bash, < and > are redirection operators, not “placeholders.” So bash freaks out.

Do it like this instead:

git remote add origin https://github.com/daddy-gier/shiny-happiness.git
2) You accidentally triggered less’s pipe command
In less, | means “pipe text to a shell command”. If you hit | and then mashed keys or pasted, less can spawn weird internal quoting like lessecho ... and your shell prints errors.

Fix: ignore it. It’s not “your repo broke.” It’s just a terminal tantrum.

What your Git output actually shows (and how to use it)
Your git show output is about submodules:

.gitmodules got created listing submodule names + URLs

you also added gitlink entries (the new file mode 160000 lines) which point to specific commits in each submodule

Submodule survival commands (the ones that keep you sane)
Clone with submodules:

git clone --recurse-submodules <repo_url>
If you already cloned:

git submodule update --init --recursive
Pull main repo + update submodules:

git pull
git submodule update --init --recursive
Make Git stop dumping you into less (optional, but saves time)
If you just want raw output:

git --no-pager show
git --no-pager log
git --no-pager diff
Or permanently:

git config --global core.pager "cat"
(You can undo later; this is “no pager ever again.”)

If you memorize only 8 keys in less, make it these:
q quit, / search, n next, N prev, g top, G bottom, ma mark, 'a return.
That’s enough to stop getting bullied by your own terminal.

Thought for 1m 2s
Lee Gier, your current tuning is basically “redline it and pray.” A Min Frequency of 2470 MHz on a 7700 XT is unnecessarily aggressive and a classic way to get random driver resets, Unity editor hiccups, and “why did my GPU just disappear” moments.

Here’s a high-performance, stability-first setup for an XFX RX 7700 XT that plays nice with Unity 6 (and your Ryzen 7 1700X, which is going to bottleneck some editor stuff no matter what you do).

The settings you should use (safe performance profile)
GPU Tuning (Advanced Control)
Min Frequency (MHz): 2200
Max Frequency (MHz): 2700
Voltage (mV): 1080 (if it crashes, bump to 1100)

Why this works:

A high min forces the card to stay pegged and can destabilize boost behavior.

A max around 2700 is a realistic “good silicon” target without turning it into a lottery ticket.

1080 mV is a common undervolt zone for stability + efficiency. Less heat, fewer spikes, fewer crashes.

What you have now (2470–2600 @ 1150 mV) is weirdly tight and hot-headed:

tight range = less room for boost control

1150 mV = more heat for no meaningful Unity gain

Fan Tuning (stop doing 100% at idle like a maniac)
You have Fan Advanced Control enabled, and your curve looks pinned near 100% which is… loud and pointless.

Set something like this:

Zero RPM: Enabled (optional, but fine)
If you want stability under long loads, you can disable Zero RPM. For Unity, either is fine.

Fan Curve (PWM / Temp):

30% @ 50°C

40% @ 65°C

55% @ 75°C

70% @ 85°C

85% @ 92°C

Targets:

Keep GPU under ~80–85°C

Keep Hotspot under ~95°C (AMD hotspot runs higher, that’s normal)

If hotspot hits 100°C+ regularly, increase the 85°C and 92°C fan points a bit.

SmartAccess Memory
You’ve got it Enabled in Adrenalin. Good.
Just make sure it’s actually supported/enabled in BIOS too (Resizable BAR / Above 4G Decoding). If not, Adrenalin can “say” it’s on while reality says otherwise.

The “don’t crash Unity” method (the part humans skip)
Do this in order, because stability comes from small steps, not vibes:

Apply the profile above (2200 / 2700 / 1080mV)

Run something consistent:

Adrenalin Stress Test, or

3DMark Time Spy Stress Test, or

A demanding game benchmark loop for 10–15 minutes

If stable and temps are good:

Try Max Frequency 2750

If still stable:

Try Voltage 1060 mV

The second you get a crash/black screen/driver reset:

Add +20 mV back (example: 1060 → 1080)

That’s how you find your card’s sweet spot without turning your project into a crash test dummy.

One blunt truth (CPU bottleneck reality)
Your Ryzen 7 1700X will cap performance in Unity editor workloads (script compilation, light baking, scene processing). Overclocking the GPU to the moon won’t fix CPU-bound moments. The best win here is:

stable GPU clocks

cooler temps

fewer driver spikes

consistent frame pacing

That’s exactly what undervolt + sane min/max clocks gives you.

TL;DR “Set it like this”
Min: 2200 MHz

Max: 2700 MHz

Voltage: 1080 mV (1100 if unstable)

Fan curve: 30%@50C, 40%@65C, 55%@75C, 70%@85C, 85%@92C

SAM: keep enabled

This gets you near-peak performance without living on the edge of a driver timeout.

ChatGPT said:
Sure, Lee Gier. If you want your PC to sound like it’s trying to achieve flight, you can absolutely run 100% fans 24/7. It’ll keep temps down. It’ll also wear the fans faster and annoy every living thing in the room. But it’s your kingdom.

Here’s how to do it cleanly in AMD Adrenalin:

Set fans to 100% all the time (Adrenalin)
Performance → Tuning

Turn Fan Tuning to Enabled

Turn Advanced Control to Enabled

Disable “Zero RPM” (this matters, otherwise it will still stop at idle)

On the fan curve graph, set every point to 100%:

Drag each node up to 100%

Add extra nodes if it lets you and keep them at 100%

Click Apply Changes

Quick sanity check
After applying:

It should show Fan Speed climbing immediately.

If it still says 0 RPM at idle, you didn’t disable Zero RPM, or the GPU is obeying a hardware “fan stop” rule until a threshold. Disabling Zero RPM usually fixes it.

Even better way (more reliable): set a fixed fan speed
Some Adrenalin versions let you set a fixed fan speed instead of a curve. If you see “Fan Speed” with a manual slider option, set it to 100% and apply. That’s the most “always-on” method.

One important reality check
At 22°C GPU / 28°C hotspot (like your screenshot), running 100% fan is not “cooling,” it’s “punishing bearings for fun.” Your GPU is already chilling.

If your real goal is no crashes, fan speed is only part of it. The stability comes from sane clocks and voltage. You can run 100% fan and still crash if the undervolt/clock range is too spicy.

If you’re doing 100% fans anyway, keep the tuning stable:

Min 2200

Max 2700

Voltage 1080–1100 mV

That combo gives you cool temps and fewer driver resets.

Thought for 17s
Lee Gier, VRAM tuning is where people chase 1–5% gains and accidentally buy themselves “random black screen” DLC. Unity 6 won’t magically transform because your memory clock is higher, but you can squeeze some extra bandwidth safely.

From your screenshot:

Memory Timing: Fast Timing (more risky)

Max Frequency: 2400 MHz (already an OC)

Here’s the sane way to set it.

Best “fast but stable” VRAM settings (RX 7700 XT)
Option A (recommended for stability)
Memory Timing: Default (NOT Fast Timing)

Max Frequency: 2300–2350 MHz

This is the “Unity won’t randomly explode” setup. You still get a small bump, with way fewer surprises.

Option B (if you insist on Fast Timing)
Memory Timing: Fast Timing

Max Frequency: 2250–2300 MHz to start

Fast Timing tightens timings. That means you usually need less MHz to stay stable. Running Fast Timing + 2400 is exactly how people end up staring at a driver timeout like it’s a personality trait.

Option C (your current 2400 MHz)
Keep 2400 MHz only if:

Memory Timing is Default, and

You can pass stress tests without artifacts or resets

How to know if VRAM is unstable (the real signs)
VRAM instability usually looks like:

sparkles/artifacts

weird texture corruption

sudden driver reset / black screen

“device removed” type errors (Unity can throw these)

If any of that happens:

switch Fast Timing → Default

drop Max Frequency by 50 MHz

repeat until stable

Power limit matters (and helps stability)
If you’re pushing GPU clocks too, set:

Power Limit: +10% (or +15% if you’re already stable and temps are low)

Power limit doesn’t “overvolt” your card by itself. It just stops it from choking when it needs headroom, which reduces clock dips and some instability.

My exact recommendation for you (with your goals)
Since you want “most out of my card without crashing,” do this:

Memory Timing: Default

VRAM Max Frequency: 2350 MHz

Power Limit: +10%

(Keep your core tuning from earlier: Min 2200 / Max 2700 / 1080–1100 mV)

That’s the sweet spot: extra bandwidth, minimal drama.

And yes, you can crank VRAM harder, but the performance-per-headache ratio gets stupid fast.

You said:
Give me a PowerShell script to move everything from the C drive to the D drive that doesn't come factory on a C drive.And give it connecting files as well, like make all the files transfer with their connections to show the new location of where the files went, like copy path.
ChatGPT said:

Thought for 14s
Lee Gier, what you’re asking for is basically: “move everything that matters off C: without bricking Windows, and keep all the old paths working.” Humans love doing this right before something explodes.

Blunt truth: there is no safe, universal “move everything that didn’t come factory” script. Windows doesn’t tag files as “factory” vs “yours,” and moving Windows\, Program Files\, ProgramData\, AppData\ randomly will break apps or the OS.
What is sane: move user data (Desktop/Documents/Downloads/etc.) to D:, then create junctions so anything still pointing at the old path keeps working.

Below is a PowerShell script that:

Moves common user folders from C:\Users\...\ to D:\UsersData\...\

Writes a CSV “path map” (old → new) so you can see exactly where everything went

Creates junctions (fake folders) at the old locations pointing to the new locations, so “connections” keep working

Has a DRY RUN mode by default (does not touch anything until you tell it to)

<#
Move-UserDataToD.ps1

SAFELY moves user data from C: to D: and keeps old paths working using junctions.
- DOES NOT touch Windows, Program Files, ProgramData, or system folders.
- Default mode is DRY RUN. Use -Execute to actually move.

Example:
  .\Move-UserDataToD.ps1
  .\Move-UserDataToD.ps1 -Execute
  .\Move-UserDataToD.ps1 -Execute -DestinationRoot "D:\MigratedUsers"

#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Execute,
    [string]$DestinationRoot = "D:\UsersData",
    [string[]]$IncludeUsers = @(),          # empty = all non-system user profiles
    [switch]$IncludeOneDrive,               # optional: moves OneDrive folder (if present) - risky if OneDrive is active
    [switch]$NoJunctions                    # optional: do NOT create junctions
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Test-Admin {
    $currentUser = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $principal   = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($currentUser)
    return $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Ensure-Dir($Path) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
        if ($Execute) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null }
        else { Write-Host "[DRY] Would create directory: $Path" }
    }
}

function Safe-RoboMove {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Source,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$Dest,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$LogFile
    )

    # Robocopy flags:
    # /MOVE moves files+dirs (deletes from source after copy)
    # /E includes subdirs incl empty
    # /COPY:DATSOU preserves data, attrs, timestamps, security, owner, auditing
    # /R /W retry/wait
    # /XJ excludes junctions (avoid loops)
    $args = @(
        "`"$Source`"",
        "`"$Dest`"",
        "/E","/MOVE",
        "/COPY:DATSOU",
        "/R:2","/W:2",
        "/XJ","/MT:8",
        "/LOG+:`"$LogFile`""
    )

    if (-not $Execute) {
        Write-Host "[DRY] robocopy $($args -join ' ')"
        return 0
    }

    $p = Start-Process -FilePath "robocopy.exe" -ArgumentList $args -Wait -PassThru
    return $p.ExitCode
}

function New-Junction {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$LinkPath,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string]$TargetPath
    )

    if ($NoJunctions) { return }

    # If something still exists at LinkPath, don't overwrite.
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LinkPath) {
        return
    }

    if (-not $Execute) {
        Write-Host "[DRY] Would create junction: $LinkPath -> $TargetPath"
        return
    }

    # Use cmd mklink for junctions (works without needing Developer Mode).
    cmd /c "mklink /J `"$LinkPath`" `"$TargetPath`"" | Out-Null
}

# ---- Main ----

$timestamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
$RunRoot   = Join-Path $DestinationRoot ("_MigrationRun_$timestamp")
$LogDir    = Join-Path $RunRoot "_logs"
$CsvMap    = Join-Path $LogDir "PathMap.csv"
$RoboLog   = Join-Path $LogDir "robocopy.log"
$Transcript= Join-Path $LogDir "transcript.txt"

if ($Execute -and -not (Test-Admin)) {
    Write-Warning "Not running as Administrator. Some moves/junctions may fail due to permissions."
    Write-Warning "If you hit Access Denied, re-run PowerShell as Admin."
}

Ensure-Dir $DestinationRoot
Ensure-Dir $RunRoot
Ensure-Dir $LogDir

if ($Execute) { Start-Transcript -Path $Transcript -Force | Out-Null }
else { Write-Host "[DRY] Transcript would be saved to: $Transcript" }

# Build user list (exclude system profiles)
$systemProfiles = @("Default", "Default User", "All Users", "Public", "Administrator", "WDAGUtilityAccount")
$profiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath "C:\Users" -Directory |
    Where-Object { $systemProfiles -notcontains $_.Name }

if ($IncludeUsers.Count -gt 0) {
    $profiles = $profiles | Where-Object { $IncludeUsers -contains $_.Name }
}

if (-not $profiles) {
    throw "No user profiles found to process."
}

# Folders to migrate per user
$KnownFolders = @(
    "Desktop",
    "Documents",
    "Downloads",
    "Pictures",
    "Videos",
    "Music",
    "Favorites"
)

if ($IncludeOneDrive) {
    $KnownFolders += "OneDrive"
}

# Start PathMap CSV
$pathMap = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

foreach ($prof in $profiles) {
    $userName  = $prof.Name
    $srcUser   = $prof.FullName
    $dstUser   = Join-Path $RunRoot $userName
    Ensure-Dir $dstUser

    Write-Host "=== User: $userName ==="
    foreach ($folder in $KnownFolders) {
        $src = Join-Path $srcUser $folder
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $src)) {
            continue
        }

        $dst = Join-Path $dstUser $folder
        Ensure-Dir $dst

        # Record mapping
        $pathMap.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            User     = $userName
            OldPath  = $src
            NewPath  = $dst
            Action   = "MOVE+JUNCTION"
            RunId    = $timestamp
        })

        Write-Host "-> $folder"
        $code = Safe-RoboMove -Source $src -Dest $dst -LogFile $RoboLog

        # Robocopy exit codes: 0-7 are OK-ish (7 includes some mismatches). 8+ indicates failures.
        if ($Execute -and $code -ge 8) {
            Write-Warning "Robocopy reported failure exit code $code for $src"
            Write-Warning "Check log: $RoboLog"
        }

        # Create junction at old location so paths keep working
        New-Junction -LinkPath $src -TargetPath $dst
    }
}

# Save mapping CSV
if ($Execute) {
    $pathMap | Export-Csv -Path $CsvMap -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
    Write-Host "Path map saved to: $CsvMap"
    Write-Host "Robocopy log saved to: $RoboLog"
    Stop-Transcript | Out-Null
} else {
    Write-Host "[DRY] Would export PathMap CSV to: $CsvMap"
    Write-Host "[DRY] Would log robocopy to: $RoboLog"
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "DONE. Migration root: $RunRoot"
Write-Host "Mode: " -NoNewline
if ($Execute) { Write-Host "EXECUTE (changes were made)" } else { Write-Host "DRY RUN (no changes)" }

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "IMPORTANT:"
Write-Host " - This moves user DATA folders only. It does NOT move Windows or installed programs."
Write-Host " - Junctions keep old paths working (apps still see C:\Users\...\Documents etc)."
Write-Host " - If you want the *default* save locations to change, do that in Windows Storage settings after this."
What this gives you (your “connections”)
Junctions at the old folder paths (example: C:\Users\Lee\Documents) that point to the new location (example: D:\UsersData\_MigrationRun_...\Lee\Documents)

A CSV map listing every moved folder with OldPath → NewPath so you have a clean record.

How to run it
Save as: Move-UserDataToD.ps1

Open PowerShell as Administrator

Dry run first:

.\Move-UserDataToD.ps1
If the output looks right, execute:

.\Move-UserDataToD.ps1 -Execute
What this script deliberately does NOT do (because I’m not helping you nuke your OS)
It does not move:

C:\Windows

C:\Program Files

C:\Program Files (x86)

C:\ProgramData

random app folders that “feel non-factory”

If you want installed apps on D:, the correct approach is:

reinstall apps to D: (WinGet/installer)

or move some apps that support it (rare)

or relocate Steam/Epic libraries (they have built-in options)

If you want, I can also give you a second script that moves your Steam/Epic/Unity/Unreal project directories (safe targets) and updates common config paths where possible, but the “move everything” fantasy ends in tears.

ChatGPT said:

Thought for 27s
Lee Gier, you want an “extremely detailed list of everything in the entire PC.” Reasonable human request, totally not how forensic tools are born.

Here’s a PowerShell inventory script that dumps a full hardware + OS + drivers + apps + services + tasks + network + storage + security report into a timestamped folder on your D: (or wherever you tell it). It also generates an HTML report so you can read it without living in CSV hell.

It does not dump passwords, Wi-Fi keys, or other “oops I leaked my life” stuff. It will also not attempt to list every file on every drive unless you explicitly enable it, because that’s how you create a 40GB text file and regret.

<#
PC_DeepInventory.ps1
Creates a deep inventory of this PC (hardware, OS, drivers, apps, storage, network, security, tasks, services).
Outputs: JSON/CSV/TXT + a readable HTML report.

USAGE:
  # Dry run style (safe): just run it
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1

  # Put output somewhere else
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -OutRoot "D:\PC_Audit"

  # Add a light file/folder size index (recommended if you want "what's eating my drive")
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -IncludeFileIndex

  # WARNING: Deep file path index (can be huge/slow)
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -DeepFileIndex

NOTES:
- Best run as Administrator for the most complete output.
- Does NOT extract secrets or passwords.
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$OutRoot = "D:\PC_Audit",
  [switch]$IncludeFileIndex,
  [switch]$DeepFileIndex
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Test-Admin {
  $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
  $p  = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
  return $p.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Write-Step([string]$Msg) {
  $ts = (Get-Date).ToString("HH:mm:ss")
  Write-Host "[$ts] $Msg"
}

function Save-Json($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Csv($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $Path -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Txt([string]$Text, [string]$Path) {
  $Text | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Try-Capture([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Block) {
  try {
    Write-Step "Collecting: $Name"
    & $Block
  } catch {
    $err = $_ | Out-String
    Write-Warning "Failed: $Name"
    return [pscustomobject]@{
      Name = $Name
      Error = $err.Trim()
    }
  }
  return $null
}

function Run-External([string]$Name, [string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args, [string]$OutFile) {
  Write-Step "Running: $Name"
  try {
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Exe -ArgumentList $Args -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru `
      -RedirectStandardOutput $OutFile -RedirectStandardError ($OutFile + ".err.txt")
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; OutFile=$OutFile }
  } catch {
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; Error=($_ | Out-String).Trim(); OutFile=$OutFile }
  }
}

# -------------------- Setup output --------------------
$stamp   = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
$outDir  = Join-Path $OutRoot "PC_Inventory_$stamp"
$rawDir  = Join-Path $outDir "_raw"
$csvDir  = Join-Path $outDir "csv"
$jsonDir = Join-Path $outDir "json"
$txtDir  = Join-Path $outDir "txt"

Ensure-Dir $outDir
Ensure-Dir $rawDir
Ensure-Dir $csvDir
Ensure-Dir $jsonDir
Ensure-Dir $txtDir

$transcript = Join-Path $txtDir "transcript.txt"
Start-Transcript -Path $transcript -Force | Out-Null

$IsAdmin = Test-Admin
Write-Step "Admin: $IsAdmin"
Write-Step "Output folder: $outDir"

# Collect errors without killing the whole run
$errors = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

# -------------------- System basics --------------------
$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Get-ComputerInfo" {
  $ci = Get-ComputerInfo
  Save-Json $ci (Join-Path $jsonDir "ComputerInfo.json")
})) | Out-Null

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "systeminfo" {
  $path = Join-Path $txtDir "systeminfo.txt"
  Run-External -Name "systeminfo" -Exe "cmd.exe" -Args @("/c","systeminfo") -OutFile $path | Out-Null
})) | Out-Null

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "msinfo32 report" {
  $path = Join-Path $txtDir "msinfo32_report.txt"
  # msinfo32 /report can take a bit, but it's one of the best built-in inventories.
  Run-External -Name "msinfo32 /report" -Exe "msinfo32.exe" -Args @("/report","`"$path`"") -OutFile (Join-Path $rawDir "msinfo32_stdout.txt") | Out-Null
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Hardware (CIM / Win32_*) --------------------
$hwClasses = @(

function Get-InstalledPrograms {
  $paths = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
  )
  $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
      Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
  }
  $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
}

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Installed programs (registry uninstall keys)" {
  $apps = Get-InstalledPrograms
  Save-Csv $apps (Join-Path $csvDir "InstalledPrograms.csv")
  Save-Json $apps (Join-Path $jsonDir "InstalledPrograms.json")
})) | Out-Null

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "UWP / Microsoft Store apps" {
  $appx = Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Name, PackageFullName, Publisher, InstallLocation, Status
  if ($appx) {
    Save-Csv $appx (Join-Path $csvDir "AppxPackages_AllUsers.csv")
    Save-Json $appx (Join-Path $jsonDir "AppxPackages_AllUsers.json")
  }
})) | Out-Null

    [pscustomobject]@{

      TaskPath = $_.TaskPath
      State    = $_.State
      Author   = $_.Author
      Description = $_.Description
      LastRunTime = $info.LastRunTime
      NextRunTime = $info.NextRunTime
      LastTaskResult = $info.LastTaskResult
    }
  }
  Save-Csv $tasks (Join-Path $csvDir "ScheduledTasks.csv")
  Save-Json $tasks (Join-Path $jsonDir "ScheduledTasks.json")
})) | Out-Null

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Startup locations" {
  $startup = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  $runKeys = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
  )
  foreach ($rk in $runKeys) {
    $vals = Get-ItemProperty -Path $rk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($vals) {
      $vals.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^PS" } | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$rk; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.Value })
      }
    }
  }

  $startupFolders = @(
    "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup",
    "$env:AppData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
  )
  foreach ($sf in $startupFolders) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sf) {
      Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sf -Force | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$sf; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.FullName })
      }
    }
  }

  Save-Csv $startup (Join-Path $csvDir "StartupItems.csv")
  Save-Json $startup (Join-Path $jsonDir "StartupItems.json")
})) | Out-Null

  Save-Json $routes   (Join-Path $jsonDir "NetRoutes.json")

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Open TCP connections (snapshot)" {
  $tcp = Get-NetTCPConnection -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object State, LocalAddress, LocalPort, RemoteAddress, RemotePort, OwningProcess
  Save-Csv $tcp (Join-Path $csvDir "NetTCPConnections.csv")
  Save-Json $tcp (Join-Path $jsonDir "NetTCPConnections.json")
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Security (safe, non-secret) --------------------
$errors.Add((Try-Capture "BitLocker status" {
  $bl = Get-Command Get-BitLockerVolume -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if ($bl) {
    $b = Get-BitLockerVolume
    Save-Csv $b (Join-Path $csvDir "BitLocker.csv")
    Save-Json $b (Join-Path $jsonDir "BitLocker.json")

  if ($lu) {
    $users = Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled, LastLogon, PasswordLastSet, Description
    Save-Csv $users (Join-Path $csvDir "LocalUsers.csv")
    Save-Json $users (Join-Path $jsonDir "LocalUsers.json")

    Save-Csv $admins (Join-Path $csvDir "LocalAdminsGroup.csv")
    Save-Json $admins (Join-Path $jsonDir "LocalAdminsGroup.json")
  }

  if ($hf) {

    Save-Json $hf (Join-Path $jsonDir "HotFixes.json")
  }

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Event logs: last 200 errors (System + Application)" {
  $events = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  foreach ($log in @("System","Application")) {
    $e = Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName=$log; Level=2 } -MaxEvents 200 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, LevelDisplayName, ProviderName, Message
    foreach ($x in $e) {
      $events.Add([pscustomobject]@{
        Log=$log
        TimeCreated=$x.TimeCreated
        Id=$x.Id
        Provider=$x.ProviderName
        Message=$x.Message
      })
    }
  }
  Save-Csv $events (Join-Path $csvDir "RecentErrors_System_Application.csv")
  Save-Json $events (Join-Path $jsonDir "RecentErrors_System_Application.json")
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Optional: file/folder index --------------------
function Get-FolderSizeBytes([string]$Path) {
  try {
    $sum = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum
    if ($null -eq $sum) { return 0 }
    return [int64]$sum
  } catch {
    return -1
  }
}

if ($IncludeFileIndex -or $DeepFileIndex) {
  $errors.Add((Try-Capture "File index (WARNING: can be slow)" {
    $drives = Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Where-Object { Test-Path $_.Root }
    $index = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

    foreach ($d in $drives) {
      $root = $d.Root
      Write-Step "Indexing drive root: $root"
      $top = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

      foreach ($item in $top) {
        if ($item.PSIsContainer) {
          $bytes = Get-FolderSizeBytes $item.FullName
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "Directory"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $bytes
          })
        } else {
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "File"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $item.Length
          })
        }
      }

      if ($DeepFileIndex) {
        # This can become MASSIVE.
        $deepPath = Join-Path $csvDir ("DeepFileIndex_" + ($root.TrimEnd("\").Replace(":","")) + ".csv")
        Write-Step "Deep indexing ALL paths under: $root (this can take ages and create huge files)"
        Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
          Select-Object FullName, Length, LastWriteTime, Attributes |
          Export-Csv -LiteralPath $deepPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
      }
    }

    Save-Csv $index (Join-Path $csvDir "DriveRootIndex.csv")
    Save-Json $index (Join-Path $jsonDir "DriveRootIndex.json")
  })) | Out-Null
}

# -------------------- Error log --------------------
$errorsClean = $errors | Where-Object { $_ -ne $null }
if ($errorsClean.Count -gt 0) {
  Save-Csv $errorsClean (Join-Path $csvDir "CollectionErrors.csv")
  Save-Json $errorsClean (Join-Path $jsonDir "CollectionErrors.json")
}

Thought for 36s
Lee Gier, what you want is basically a traffic cop for your Downloads folder: let everything download to C:\Users\FRANK\Downloads like normal, then the script benchmarks D/G/H, checks which one is fastest and least full, and moves completed downloads there. And you want it to print the full decision report right in the PowerShell window because staring at silent scripts is a human pastime.

PowerShell script: Auto-route Downloads from C: to best of D/G/H (fast + free), and print report
Save as: AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1

<#
AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1

Goal:
- Leave browser/app download location alone (C:\Users\<you>\Downloads).
- Automatically move completed downloads to the "best" drive among D/G/H,
  based on a quick speed test + how full the drive is.
- Print a detailed report in the PowerShell window.

Usage:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1 -Candidates D,G,H -MinFreeGB 30
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1 -ReportOnly

Stop:
  Ctrl + C

Notes:
- Does NOT change Windows settings, browser settings, or registry.
- It watches your Downloads folder and moves files *after* they are stable/unlocked.
- Some downloads create temp extensions (.crdownload, .part, .tmp). Those are ignored until final file appears.

#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string[]]$Candidates = @("D","G","H"),
  [int]$MinFreeGB = 20,
  [int]$SpeedTestMB = 128,
  [double]$WeightSpeed = 0.70,
  [double]$WeightFree  = 0.30,
  [string]$WatchPath = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Downloads"),
  [string]$DestinationFolderName = "Downloads_Routed",
  [switch]$ReportOnly,
  [int]$StabilitySeconds = 6,
  [int]$MaxWaitSeconds = 900
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

# ---------------- Helpers ----------------
function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 70)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 70)
}

function Get-DriveInfo([string]$Letter) {
  $root = "$Letter`:\"
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $root)) { return $null }

  try {
    $vol = Get-Volume -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($vol.DriveType -ne 'Fixed') { return $null }

    [pscustomobject]@{
      DriveLetter = $Letter
      Root        = $root
      FileSystem  = $vol.FileSystem
      Label       = $vol.FileSystemLabel
      SizeGB      = [math]::Round($vol.Size/1GB, 2)
      FreeGB      = [math]::Round($vol.SizeRemaining/1GB, 2)
      UsedGB      = [math]::Round(($vol.Size - $vol.SizeRemaining)/1GB, 2)
      FreePct     = if ($vol.Size -gt 0) { [math]::Round(($vol.SizeRemaining / $vol.Size) * 100, 2) } else { 0 }
    }
  } catch {
    return $null
  }
}

function Measure-DriveSpeedMBps([string]$Root, [int]$TestMB) {
  $testDir = Join-Path $Root ".nh_speedtest"
  $testFile = Join-Path $testDir ("test_{0}.bin" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")))
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testDir -Force | Out-Null

  $bytesToWrite = $TestMB * 1MB
  $buffer = New-Object byte[](4MB)  # chunk buffer
  $rng = [System.Random]::new()
  $rng.NextBytes($buffer)

  $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $written = 0L

  # WRITE test
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($testFile, [System.IO.FileMode]::CreateNew, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
  try {
    while ($written -lt $bytesToWrite) {
      $toWrite = [math]::Min($buffer.Length, $bytesToWrite - $written)
      $fs.Write($buffer, 0, $toWrite)
      $written += $toWrite
    }
    $fs.Flush($true)
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $writeSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $writeMBps = [math]::Round($TestMB / $writeSec, 2)

  # READ test
  $sw.Restart()
  $read = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($testFile, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read, [System.IO.FileShare]::Read)
  try {
    while ($true) {
      $n = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)
      if ($n -le 0) { break }
      $read += $n
    }
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $readSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $readMBps = [math]::Round(($read / 1MB) / $readSec, 2)

  # Cleanup
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  # Try to remove dir if empty
  try { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}

  [pscustomobject]@{
    WriteMBps = $writeMBps
    ReadMBps  = $readMBps
    AvgMBps   = [math]::Round((($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2), 2)
  }
}

function Choose-BestDrive {
  Write-Section "Drive assessment (speed + free space)"
  $results = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  foreach ($d in $Candidates) {
    $d = $d.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")

    $info = Get-DriveInfo $d
    if (-not $info) {
      Write-Host ("{0}: not available / not fixed / access denied" -f $d)
      continue
    }

    if ($info.FreeGB -lt $MinFreeGB) {
      Write-Host ("{0}: available but too low on space ({1} GB free < {2} GB min)" -f $d, $info.FreeGB, $MinFreeGB)
      continue
    }

    Write-Host ("Testing {0}:  Free {1} GB ({2}%), FS {3}, Label '{4}'" -f $info.DriveLetter, $info.FreeGB, $info.FreePct, $info.FileSystem, $info.Label)

    $speed = $null
    try {
      $speed = Measure-DriveSpeedMBps -Root $info.Root -TestMB $SpeedTestMB
    } catch {
      Write-Host ("{0}: speed test failed: {1}" -f $info.DriveLetter, $_.Exception.Message)
      continue
    }

    $obj = [pscustomobject]@{
      Drive      = $info.DriveLetter
      Root       = $info.Root
      SizeGB     = $info.SizeGB
      FreeGB     = $info.FreeGB
      FreePct    = $info.FreePct
      WriteMBps  = $speed.WriteMBps
      ReadMBps   = $speed.ReadMBps
      AvgMBps    = $speed.AvgMBps
      Score      = 0.0
    }

    $results.Add($obj) | Out-Null
  }

  if ($results.Count -eq 0) {
    throw "No eligible drives found among: $($Candidates -join ', '). (Either missing, not fixed, or below MinFreeGB.)"
  }

  # Normalize and score: speed + free%
  $maxSpeed = ($results | Measure-Object -Property AvgMBps -Maximum).Maximum
  if ($maxSpeed -le 0) { $maxSpeed = 1 }

  foreach ($r in $results) {
    $speedNorm = $r.AvgMBps / $maxSpeed
    $freeNorm  = $r.FreePct / 100.0
    $r.Score   = [math]::Round(($speedNorm * $WeightSpeed) + ($freeNorm * $WeightFree), 4)
  }

  $results | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host

  $best = $results | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  Write-Host ("Chosen drive: {0}  (Score {1})" -f $best.Drive, $best.Score)
  return [pscustomobject]@{
    Best    = $best
    Results = $results
  }
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Get-UniquePath([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $Path }
  $dir = Split-Path -Parent $Path
  $name = Split-Path -Leaf $Path
  $base = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($name)
  $ext  = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($name)

  for ($i=1; $i -le 999; $i++) {
    $candidate = Join-Path $dir ("{0} ({1}){2}" -f $base, $i, $ext)
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $candidate)) { return $candidate }
  }
  throw "Could not generate a unique filename for: $Path"
}

function Test-FileUnlocked([string]$Path) {
  try {
    $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($Path, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::ReadWrite, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
    $fs.Dispose()
    return $true
  } catch {
    return $false
  }
}

function Wait-FileReady([string]$Path) {
  $ignoreExt = @(".crdownload",".part",".partial",".tmp",".download",".aria2")
  $ext = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($Path).ToLowerInvariant()
  if ($ignoreExt -contains $ext) { return $false }

  $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($MaxWaitSeconds)
  $stableCountNeeded = [math]::Ceiling($StabilitySeconds / 2)
  $stableCount = 0
  $lastLen = -1L

  while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $false }

    try {
      $len = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path).Length
    } catch {
      Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
      continue
    }

    if ($len -eq $lastLen -and $len -gt 0) { $stableCount++ } else { $stableCount = 0 }
    $lastLen = $len

    if ($stableCount -ge $stableCountNeeded -and (Test-FileUnlocked $Path)) {
      return $true
    }

    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
  }

  return $false
}

# ---------------- Main ----------------
Write-Section "AutoRoute Downloads"
Write-Host ("WatchPath: {0}" -f $WatchPath)

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $WatchPath)) {
  throw "Downloads folder not found: $WatchPath"
}

$choice = Choose-BestDrive
$best = $choice.Best

$destRoot = Join-Path $best.Root $DestinationFolderName
Ensure-Dir $destRoot

Write-Section "Routing decision report (printed in console)"
Write-Host ("Destination root: {0}" -f $destRoot)
Write-Host ("Scoring weights: Speed={0} FreeSpace={1}  |  MinFreeGB={2}  |  SpeedTestMB={3}" -f $WeightSpeed, $WeightFree, $MinFreeGB, $SpeedTestMB)

if ($ReportOnly) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "ReportOnly enabled. Exiting without watching/moving files."
  return
}

Write-Section "Watcher started (Ctrl+C to stop)"
Write-Host "Ignoring temp extensions: .crdownload .part .partial .tmp .download .aria2"
Write-Host "Moves files only when stable + unlocked."

$moved = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
$watcher = New-Object System.IO.FileSystemWatcher
$watcher.Path = $WatchPath
$watcher.Filter = "*.*"
$watcher.IncludeSubdirectories = $false
$watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = $true

$handler = {
  param($sender, $eventArgs)

  $src = $eventArgs.FullPath

  # Skip directories
  try {
    if ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $src -ErrorAction Stop).PSIsContainer) { return }
  } catch { return }

  # Wait for download completion / unlock
  if (-not (Wait-FileReady -Path $src)) { return }

  $dest = Join-Path $using:destRoot (Split-Path -Leaf $src)
  $dest = Get-UniquePath -Path $dest

  try {
    Move-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination $dest -Force
    $entry = [pscustomobject]@{
      Time = (Get-Date)
      From = $src
      To   = $dest
      SizeMB = [math]::Round(((Get-Item -LiteralPath $dest).Length / 1MB), 2)
    }
    $using:moved.Add($entry) | Out-Null
    Write-Host ("MOVED [{0} MB]  {1}  ->  {2}" -f $entry.SizeMB, $entry.From, $entry.To)
  } catch {
    Write-Host ("FAILED MOVE: {0}`n{1}" -f $src, $_.Exception.Message)
  }
}

# Subscribe to events (Created + Renamed catches most browsers)
$sub1 = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $watcher -EventName Created -Action $handler
$sub2 = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $watcher -EventName Renamed -Action $handler

try {
  while ($true) { Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }
}
finally {
  # Cleanup
  Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier $sub1.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier $sub2.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  $watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = $false
  $watcher.Dispose()

  Write-Section "Session summary (printed in console)"
  if ($moved.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "No files moved this session."
  } else {
    $moved |
      Select-Object Time, SizeMB, From, To |
      Sort-Object Time |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }
}
What this does (in plain English)
Leaves downloads landing on C: (normal behavior).

Benchmarks D, G, H (quick write + read test) and checks free space.

Picks the best drive using a score:

70% speed

30% free space

Watches C:\Users\FRANK\Downloads

Moves completed downloads to:

X:\Downloads_Routed\... (X is the chosen drive)

Prints:

the benchmark table

the chosen drive

every moved file

a session summary table when you stop it

Two quick notes so you don’t trip over Windows again
This can’t magically reroute Microsoft Store app installs or game launchers. It’s for files downloaded into Downloads (browsers, Discord, etc.).

If you want it to run automatically at startup, that’s a scheduled task. I can give you the installer block for that too, but this already does the core job.

Now go run your PC inventory script, and when it’s done we can use that report to tell whether D/G/H are SSD/HDD and adjust weights so it stops making dumb choices.

Thought for 27s

Lee Gier, you want an “extremely detailed list of everything in the entire PC.” Reasonable human request, totally not how forensic tools are born.

Here’s a PowerShell inventory script that dumps a full hardware + OS + drivers + apps + services + tasks + network + storage + security report into a timestamped folder on your D: (or wherever you tell it). It also generates an HTML report so you can read it without living in CSV hell.

It does not dump passwords, Wi-Fi keys, or other “oops I leaked my life” stuff. It will also not attempt to list every file on every drive unless you explicitly enable it, because that’s how you create a 40GB text file and regret.

<#
PC_DeepInventory.ps1
Creates a deep inventory of this PC (hardware, OS, drivers, apps, storage, network, security, tasks, services).
Outputs: JSON/CSV/TXT + a readable HTML report.

USAGE:
  # Dry run style (safe): just run it
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1

  # Put output somewhere else
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -OutRoot "D:\PC_Audit"

  # Add a light file/folder size index (recommended if you want "what's eating my drive")
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -IncludeFileIndex

  # WARNING: Deep file path index (can be huge/slow)
  .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -DeepFileIndex

NOTES:
- Best run as Administrator for the most complete output.
- Does NOT extract secrets or passwords.
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$OutRoot = "D:\PC_Audit",
  [switch]$IncludeFileIndex,
  [switch]$DeepFileIndex
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Test-Admin {
  $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
  $p  = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
  return $p.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Write-Step([string]$Msg) {
  $ts = (Get-Date).ToString("HH:mm:ss")
  Write-Host "[$ts] $Msg"
}

function Save-Json($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Csv($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $Path -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Txt([string]$Text, [string]$Path) {
  $Text | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Try-Capture([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Block) {
  try {
    Write-Step "Collecting: $Name"
    & $Block
  } catch {
    $err = $_ | Out-String
    Write-Warning "Failed: $Name"
    return [pscustomobject]@{
      Name = $Name
      Error = $err.Trim()
    }
  }
  return $null
}

function Run-External([string]$Name, [string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args, [string]$OutFile) {
  Write-Step "Running: $Name"
  try {
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Exe -ArgumentList $Args -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru 
      -RedirectStandardOutput $OutFile -RedirectStandardError ($OutFile + ".err.txt")
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; OutFile=$OutFile }
  } catch {
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; Error=($_ | Out-String).Trim(); OutFile=$OutFile }
  }
}

# -------------------- Setup output --------------------
$stamp   = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
$outDir  = Join-Path $OutRoot "PC_Inventory_$stamp"

Ensure-Dir $csvDir

# Collect errors without killing the whole run
$errors = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  Save-Json $ci (Join-Path $jsonDir "ComputerInfo.json")

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "systeminfo" {
  $path = Join-Path $txtDir "systeminfo.txt"

})) | Out-Null

  $path = Join-Path $txtDir "msinfo32_report.txt"
  # msinfo32 /report can take a bit, but it's one of the best built-in inventories.
  Run-External -Name "msinfo32 /report" -Exe "msinfo32.exe" -Args @("/report",""$path"") -OutFile (Join-Path $rawDir "msinfo32_stdout.txt") | Out-Null
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Hardware (CIM / Win32_*) --------------------
$hwClasses = @(
  "Win32_ComputerSystem",

  })) | Out-Null

})) | Out-Null

})) | Out-Null

# SMART status (basic)

  }
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Drivers / Devices --------------------
$errors.Add((Try-Capture "PnP devices" {

  if ($pnp) {

  }
})) | Out-Null

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Installed drivers (pnputil)" {
  $path = Join-Path $txtDir "pnputil_enum-drivers.txt"
  Run-External -Name "pnputil /enum-drivers" -Exe "pnputil.exe" -Args @("/enum-drivers") -OutFile $path | Out-Null
})) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Software inventory --------------------
function Get-InstalledPrograms {
  $paths = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
  )
  $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
      Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
  }
  $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
}

$errors.Add((Try-Capture "Startup locations" {
  $startup = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  $runKeys = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
  )
  foreach ($rk in $runKeys) {
    $vals = Get-ItemProperty -Path $rk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($vals) {
      $vals.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^PS" } | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$rk; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.Value })
      }
    }
  }

  $startupFolders = @(
    "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup",
    "$env:AppData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
  )
  foreach ($sf in $startupFolders) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sf) {
      Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sf -Force | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$sf; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.FullName })
      }
    }
  }

  Save-Csv $startup (Join-Path $csvDir "StartupItems.csv")
  Save-Json $startup (Join-Path $jsonDir "StartupItems.json")
})) | Out-Null

  $events = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  foreach ($log in @("System","Application")) {
    $e = Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName=$log; Level=2 } -MaxEvents 200 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, LevelDisplayName, ProviderName, Message
    foreach ($x in $e) {
      $events.Add([pscustomobject]@{
        Log=$log
        TimeCreated=$x.TimeCreated
        Id=$x.Id
        Provider=$x.ProviderName
        Message=$x.Message
      })
    }
  }
  Save-Csv $events (Join-Path $csvDir "RecentErrors_System_Application.csv")
  Save-Json $events (Join-Path $jsonDir "RecentErrors_System_Application.json")

# -------------------- Optional: file/folder index --------------------
function Get-FolderSizeBytes([string]$Path) {
  try {
    $sum = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum
    if ($null -eq $sum) { return 0 }
    return [int64]$sum
  } catch {
    return -1
  }
}

if ($IncludeFileIndex -or $DeepFileIndex) {
  $errors.Add((Try-Capture "File index (WARNING: can be slow)" {
    $drives = Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Where-Object { Test-Path $_.Root }
    $index = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

    foreach ($d in $drives) {
      $root = $d.Root
      Write-Step "Indexing drive root: $root"
      $top = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

      foreach ($item in $top) {
        if ($item.PSIsContainer) {
          $bytes = Get-FolderSizeBytes $item.FullName
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "Directory"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $bytes
          })
        } else {
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "File"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $item.Length
          })
        }
      }

      if ($DeepFileIndex) {
        # This can become MASSIVE.
        $deepPath = Join-Path $csvDir ("DeepFileIndex_" + ($root.TrimEnd("\").Replace(":","")) + ".csv")
        Write-Step "Deep indexing ALL paths under: $root (this can take ages and create huge files)"
        Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
          Select-Object FullName, Length, LastWriteTime, Attributes |
          Export-Csv -LiteralPath $deepPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
      }
    }

    Save-Csv $index (Join-Path $csvDir "DriveRootIndex.csv")
    Save-Json $index (Join-Path $jsonDir "DriveRootIndex.json")
  })) | Out-Null
}

if ($errorsClean.Count -gt 0) {
  Save-Csv $errorsClean (Join-Path $csvDir "CollectionErrors.csv")
  Save-Json $errorsClean (Join-Path $jsonDir "CollectionErrors.json")
}

$report += "</head><body>"

} else {

$report += "<h2>Privacy</h2><p>No passwords or Wi-Fi keys were collected. This is inventory only.</p>"

Notes (because Windows is… Windows)

Run as Administrator if you want the most complete device/service/task info.

If your D: drive doesn’t exist, change -OutRoot to something real like C:\Temp\PC_Audit.

If you actually meant “list every single file and byte on the machine,” enable -DeepFileIndex and prepare for consequences.

>>     # /MOVE moves files+dirs (deletes from source after copy)

>>

>>         Write-Host "[DRY] robocopy $($args -join ' ')"
>>         return 0
>>     }
>>
>>     $p = Start-Process -FilePath "robocopy.exe" -ArgumentList $args -Wait -PassThru
>>     return $p.ExitCode
>> }

>>
>>     # If something still exists at LinkPath, don't overwrite.

>>         return
>>     }
>>

>>         return
>>     }
>>
