Thought for 36s

Lee Gier, what you want is basically a traffic cop for your Downloads folder: let everything download to C:\Users\FRANK\Downloads like normal, then the script benchmarks D/G/H, checks which one is fastest and least full, and moves completed downloads there. And you want it to print the full decision report right in the PowerShell window because staring at silent scripts is a human pastime.

Also: the reason you saw else: The term 'else' is not recognized... earlier is because you were pasting scripts line-by-line into the console. PowerShell doesn’t “remember” an if block across separate pastes. Save it as a .ps1 and run it.

PowerShell script: Auto-route Downloads from C: to best of D/G/H (fast + free), and print report

Save as: AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1

<#
AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1

Goal:
- Leave browser/app download location alone (C:\Users\<you>\Downloads).
- Automatically move completed downloads to the "best" drive among D/G/H,
  based on a quick speed test + how full the drive is.
- Print a detailed report in the PowerShell window.

Usage:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1 -Candidates D,G,H -MinFreeGB 30
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\AutoRoute-Downloads.ps1 -ReportOnly

Stop:
  Ctrl + C

Notes:
- Does NOT change Windows settings, browser settings, or registry.
- It watches your Downloads folder and moves files *after* they are stable/unlocked.
- Some downloads create temp extensions (.crdownload, .part, .tmp). Those are ignored until final file appears.

#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string[]]$Candidates = @("D","G","H"),
  [int]$MinFreeGB = 20,
  [int]$SpeedTestMB = 128,
  [double]$WeightSpeed = 0.70,
  [double]$WeightFree  = 0.30,
  [string]$WatchPath = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Downloads"),
  [string]$DestinationFolderName = "Downloads_Routed",
  [switch]$ReportOnly,
  [int]$StabilitySeconds = 6,
  [int]$MaxWaitSeconds = 900
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

# ---------------- Helpers ----------------
function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 70)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 70)
}

function Get-DriveInfo([string]$Letter) {
  $root = "$Letter:\"
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $root)) { return $null }

  try {
    $vol = Get-Volume -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($vol.DriveType -ne 'Fixed') { return $null }

    [pscustomobject]@{
      DriveLetter = $Letter
      Root        = $root
      FileSystem  = $vol.FileSystem
      Label       = $vol.FileSystemLabel
      SizeGB      = [math]::Round($vol.Size/1GB, 2)
      FreeGB      = [math]::Round($vol.SizeRemaining/1GB, 2)
      UsedGB      = [math]::Round(($vol.Size - $vol.SizeRemaining)/1GB, 2)
      FreePct     = if ($vol.Size -gt 0) { [math]::Round(($vol.SizeRemaining / $vol.Size) * 100, 2) } else { 0 }
    }
  } catch {
    return $null
  }
}

function Measure-DriveSpeedMBps([string]$Root, [int]$TestMB) {
  $testDir = Join-Path $Root ".nh_speedtest"
  $testFile = Join-Path $testDir ("test_{0}.bin" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")))
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testDir -Force | Out-Null

  $bytesToWrite = $TestMB * 1MB
  $buffer = New-Object byte[](4MB)  # chunk buffer
  $rng = [System.Random]::new()
  $rng.NextBytes($buffer)

  $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $written = 0L

  # WRITE test
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($testFile, [System.IO.FileMode]::CreateNew, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
  try {
    while ($written -lt $bytesToWrite) {
      $toWrite = [math]::Min($buffer.Length, $bytesToWrite - $written)
      $fs.Write($buffer, 0, $toWrite)
      $written += $toWrite
    }
    $fs.Flush($true)
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $writeSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $writeMBps = [math]::Round($TestMB / $writeSec, 2)

  # READ test
  $sw.Restart()
  $read = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($testFile, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read, [System.IO.FileShare]::Read)
  try {
    while ($true) {
      $n = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)
      if ($n -le 0) { break }
      $read += $n
    }
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $readSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $readMBps = [math]::Round(($read / 1MB) / $readSec, 2)

  # Cleanup
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  # Try to remove dir if empty
  try { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}

  [pscustomobject]@{
    WriteMBps = $writeMBps
    ReadMBps  = $readMBps
    AvgMBps   = [math]::Round((($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2), 2)
  }
}

function Choose-BestDrive {
  Write-Section "Drive assessment (speed + free space)"
  $results = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  foreach ($d in $Candidates) {
    $d = $d.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")

    $info = Get-DriveInfo $d
    if (-not $info) {
      Write-Host ("{0}: not available / not fixed / access denied" -f $d)
      continue
    }

    if ($info.FreeGB -lt $MinFreeGB) {
      Write-Host ("{0}: available but too low on space ({1} GB free < {2} GB min)" -f $d, $info.FreeGB, $MinFreeGB)
      continue
    }

    Write-Host ("Testing {0}:  Free {1} GB ({2}%), FS {3}, Label '{4}'" -f $info.DriveLetter, $info.FreeGB, $info.FreePct, $info.FileSystem, $info.Label)

    $speed = $null
    try {
      $speed = Measure-DriveSpeedMBps -Root $info.Root -TestMB $SpeedTestMB
    } catch {
      Write-Host ("{0}: speed test failed: {1}" -f $info.DriveLetter, $_.Exception.Message)
      continue
    }

    $obj = [pscustomobject]@{
      Drive      = $info.DriveLetter
      Root       = $info.Root
      SizeGB     = $info.SizeGB
      FreeGB     = $info.FreeGB
      FreePct    = $info.FreePct
      WriteMBps  = $speed.WriteMBps
      ReadMBps   = $speed.ReadMBps
      AvgMBps    = $speed.AvgMBps
      Score      = 0.0
    }

    $results.Add($obj) | Out-Null
  }

  if ($results.Count -eq 0) {
    throw "No eligible drives found among: $($Candidates -join ', '). (Either missing, not fixed, or below MinFreeGB.)"
  }

  # Normalize and score: speed + free%
  $maxSpeed = ($results | Measure-Object -Property AvgMBps -Maximum).Maximum
  if ($maxSpeed -le 0) { $maxSpeed = 1 }

  foreach ($r in $results) {
    $speedNorm = $r.AvgMBps / $maxSpeed
    $freeNorm  = $r.FreePct / 100.0
    $r.Score   = [math]::Round(($speedNorm * $WeightSpeed) + ($freeNorm * $WeightFree), 4)
  }

  $results | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host

  $best = $results | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  Write-Host ("Chosen drive: {0}  (Score {1})" -f $best.Drive, $best.Score)
  return [pscustomobject]@{
    Best    = $best
    Results = $results
  }
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Get-UniquePath([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $Path }
  $dir = Split-Path -Parent $Path
  $name = Split-Path -Leaf $Path
  $base = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($name)
  $ext  = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($name)

  for ($i=1; $i -le 999; $i++) {
    $candidate = Join-Path $dir ("{0} ({1}){2}" -f $base, $i, $ext)
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $candidate)) { return $candidate }
  }
  throw "Could not generate a unique filename for: $Path"
}

function Test-FileUnlocked([string]$Path) {
  try {
    $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($Path, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::ReadWrite, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
    $fs.Dispose()
    return $true
  } catch {
    return $false
  }
}

function Wait-FileReady([string]$Path) {
  $ignoreExt = @(".crdownload",".part",".partial",".tmp",".download",".aria2")
  $ext = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($Path).ToLowerInvariant()
  if ($ignoreExt -contains $ext) { return $false }

  $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($MaxWaitSeconds)
  $stableCountNeeded = [math]::Ceiling($StabilitySeconds / 2)
  $stableCount = 0
  $lastLen = -1L

  while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $false }

    try {
      $len = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $Path).Length
    } catch {
      Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
      continue
    }

    if ($len -eq $lastLen -and $len -gt 0) { $stableCount++ } else { $stableCount = 0 }
    $lastLen = $len

    if ($stableCount -ge $stableCountNeeded -and (Test-FileUnlocked $Path)) {
      return $true
    }

    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
  }

  return $false
}

# ---------------- Main ----------------
Write-Section "AutoRoute Downloads"
Write-Host ("WatchPath: {0}" -f $WatchPath)

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $WatchPath)) {
  throw "Downloads folder not found: $WatchPath"
}

$choice = Choose-BestDrive
$best = $choice.Best

$destRoot = Join-Path $best.Root $DestinationFolderName
Ensure-Dir $destRoot

Write-Section "Routing decision report (printed in console)"
Write-Host ("Destination root: {0}" -f $destRoot)
Write-Host ("Scoring weights: Speed={0} FreeSpace={1}  |  MinFreeGB={2}  |  SpeedTestMB={3}" -f $WeightSpeed, $WeightFree, $MinFreeGB, $SpeedTestMB)

if ($ReportOnly) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "ReportOnly enabled. Exiting without watching/moving files."
  return
}

Write-Section "Watcher started (Ctrl+C to stop)"
Write-Host "Ignoring temp extensions: .crdownload .part .partial .tmp .download .aria2"
Write-Host "Moves files only when stable + unlocked."

$moved = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
$watcher = New-Object System.IO.FileSystemWatcher
$watcher.Path = $WatchPath
$watcher.Filter = "*.*"
$watcher.IncludeSubdirectories = $false
$watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = $true

$handler = {
  param($sender, $eventArgs)

  $src = $eventArgs.FullPath

  # Skip directories
  try {
    if ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $src -ErrorAction Stop).PSIsContainer) { return }
  } catch { return }

  # Wait for download completion / unlock
  if (-not (Wait-FileReady -Path $src)) { return }

  $dest = Join-Path $using:destRoot (Split-Path -Leaf $src)
  $dest = Get-UniquePath -Path $dest

  try {
    Move-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination $dest -Force
    $entry = [pscustomobject]@{
      Time = (Get-Date)
      From = $src
      To   = $dest
      SizeMB = [math]::Round(((Get-Item -LiteralPath $dest).Length / 1MB), 2)
    }
    $using:moved.Add($entry) | Out-Null
    Write-Host ("MOVED [{0} MB]  {1}  ->  {2}" -f $entry.SizeMB, $entry.From, $entry.To)
  } catch {
    Write-Host ("FAILED MOVE: {0}n{1}" -f $src, $_.Exception.Message)
  }
}

# Subscribe to events (Created + Renamed catches most browsers)
$sub1 = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $watcher -EventName Created -Action $handler
$sub2 = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $watcher -EventName Renamed -Action $handler

try {
  while ($true) { Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }
}
finally {
  # Cleanup
  Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier $sub1.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Unregister-Event -SourceIdentifier $sub2.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  $watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = $false
  $watcher.Dispose()

  Write-Section "Session summary (printed in console)"
  if ($moved.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "No files moved this session."
  } else {
    $moved |
      Select-Object Time, SizeMB, From, To |
      Sort-Object Time |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }
}

What this does (in plain English)

Leaves downloads landing on C: (normal behavior).

Benchmarks D, G, H (quick write + read test) and checks free space.

Picks the best drive using a score:

70% speed

30% free space

Watches C:\Users\FRANK\Downloads

Moves completed downloads to:

X:\Downloads_Routed\... (X is the chosen drive)

Prints:

the benchmark table

the chosen drive

every moved file

a session summary table when you stop it

Two quick notes so you don’t trip over Windows again

This can’t magically reroute Microsoft Store app installs or game launchers. It’s for files downloaded into Downloads (browsers, Discord, etc.).

If you want it to run automatically at startup, that’s a scheduled task. I can give you the installer block for that too, but this already does the core job.

Now go run your PC inventory script, and when it’s done we can use that report to tell whether D/G/H are SSD/HDD and adjust weights so it stops making dumb choices.

<#
PC_DeepInventory.ps1
Deep inventory of this PC (hardware, OS, drivers, apps, services, tasks, network, storage, security).
Outputs: JSON/CSV/TXT + a readable HTML report.
ALSO prints a console summary report automatically.

USAGE:

  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -OutRoot "D:\PC_Audit"

  # Print more to the console:

- Best run as Administrator for the most complete output.
- Does NOT extract secrets or passwords.
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$OutRoot = "D:\PC_Audit",
  [switch]$IncludeFileIndex,
  [switch]$DeepFileIndex,

  # Console reporting controls
  [switch]$PrintConsoleReport = $true,
  [int]$PrintMsinfoHeadLines = 120
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Test-Admin {
  $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
  $p  = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
  return $p.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Write-Step([string]$Msg) {
  $ts = (Get-Date).ToString("HH:mm:ss")
  Write-Host "[$ts] $Msg"
}

function Save-Json($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Csv($Obj, [string]$Path) {
  $Obj | Export-Csv -LiteralPath $Path -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
}

function Save-Txt([string]$Text, [string]$Path) {
  $Text | Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Encoding UTF8
}

function Try-Capture([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Block, [ref]$OutVar) {
  try {
    Write-Step "Collecting: $Name"
    $result = & $Block
    $OutVar.Value = $result
    return $null
  } catch {
    $err = $_ | Out-String
    Write-Warning "Failed: $Name"
    $OutVar.Value = $null
    return [pscustomobject]@{
      Name  = $Name
      Error = $err.Trim()
    }
  }
}

function Run-External([string]$Name, [string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args, [string]$OutFile) {
  Write-Step "Running: $Name"
  try {
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Exe -ArgumentList $Args -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru `
      -RedirectStandardOutput $OutFile -RedirectStandardError ($OutFile + ".err.txt")
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; OutFile=$OutFile }
  } catch {
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Name=$Name; Error=($_ | Out-String).Trim(); OutFile=$OutFile }
  }
}

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 80)

# -------------------- Software inventory --------------------
function Get-InstalledPrograms {
  $paths = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
  )
  $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
      Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
  }
  $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
}

        TimeCreated=$x.TimeCreated

        Provider=$x.ProviderName

      })
    }
  }
  $events
} ([ref]$tmpEvents))) | Out-Null

# -------------------- Optional: file/folder index --------------------
function Get-FolderSizeBytes([string]$Path) {
  try {
    $sum = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum
    if ($null -eq $sum) { return 0 }
    return [int64]$sum
  } catch {
    return -1
  }
}

if ($IncludeFileIndex -or $DeepFileIndex) {
  $tmpIndex = $null
  $errors.Add((Try-Capture "File index (WARNING: can be slow)" {
    $drives = Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Where-Object { Test-Path $_.Root }
    $index = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

    foreach ($d in $drives) {
      $root = $d.Root
      Write-Step "Indexing drive root: $root"
      $top = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

      foreach ($item in $top) {
        if ($item.PSIsContainer) {
          $bytes = Get-FolderSizeBytes $item.FullName
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "Directory"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $bytes
          })
        } else {
          $index.Add([pscustomobject]@{
            Drive = $root
            Type  = "File"
            Path  = $item.FullName
            SizeBytes = $item.Length
          })
        }
      }

      if ($DeepFileIndex) {
        $deepPath = Join-Path $csvDir ("DeepFileIndex_" + ($root.TrimEnd("\").Replace(":","")) + ".csv")
        Write-Step "Deep indexing ALL paths under: $root (this can take ages and create huge files)"
        Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
          Select-Object FullName, Length, LastWriteTime, Attributes |
          Export-Csv -LiteralPath $deepPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
      }
    }

    $index
  } ([ref]$tmpIndex))) | Out-Null

  if ($tmpIndex) {
    Save-Csv $tmpIndex (Join-Path $csvDir "DriveRootIndex.csv")
    Save-Json $tmpIndex (Join-Path $jsonDir "DriveRootIndex.json")
  }
}

# -------------------- PRINT CONSOLE REPORT --------------------
if ($PrintConsoleReport) {
  Write-Section "CONSOLE REPORT (what you asked for)"

  # OS summary
  if ($os) {
    $osSummary = [pscustomobject]@{
      ComputerName = $env:COMPUTERNAME
      OS          = $os.Caption
      Version     = $os.Version
      Build       = $os.BuildNumber
      InstallDate = $os.InstallDate
      BootTime    = $os.LastBootUpTime
    }
    Write-Host "`n--- OS ---"
    $osSummary | Format-List | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  # CPU/RAM/GPU summary
  if ($cpu) {
    Write-Host "--- CPU ---"
    $cpu | Select-Object Name, Manufacturer, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors, MaxClockSpeed |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  if ($ram) {
    $totalGB = [math]::Round((($ram | Measure-Object -Property Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1GB), 2)
    Write-Host "--- RAM ---"
    Write-Host ("Total Installed RAM (GB): {0}" -f $totalGB)
    $ram | Select-Object Manufacturer, PartNumber, Speed, Capacity |
      ForEach-Object {
        $_.Capacity = [math]::Round(($_.Capacity / 1GB), 2)
        $_
      } | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  if ($gpu) {
    Write-Host "--- GPU ---"
    $gpu | Select-Object Name, DriverVersion, VideoProcessor, AdapterRAM |
      ForEach-Object {
        $_.AdapterRAM = if ($_.AdapterRAM) { [math]::Round(($_.AdapterRAM / 1GB), 2) } else { $null }
        $_
      } | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  # BIOS / board
  if ($bios) {
    Write-Host "--- BIOS ---"
    $bios | Select-Object Manufacturer, SMBIOSBIOSVersion, SerialNumber, ReleaseDate |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }
  if ($baseboard) {
    Write-Host "--- Motherboard ---"
    $baseboard | Select-Object Manufacturer, Product, SerialNumber, Version |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  # Storage
  if ($disks) {
    Write-Host "--- Disks ---"
    $disks | Select-Object Number, FriendlyName, BusType, MediaType, Size, PartitionStyle, HealthStatus |
      ForEach-Object {
        $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size / 1GB), 2)
        $_
      } | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  if ($vols) {
    Write-Host "--- Volumes ---"
    $vols | Select-Object DriveLetter, FileSystemLabel, FileSystem, Size, SizeRemaining, HealthStatus |
      ForEach-Object {
        $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size / 1GB), 2)
        $_.SizeRemaining = [math]::Round(($_.SizeRemaining / 1GB), 2)
        $_
      } | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  # Network quick view
  if ($netAdapters) {
    Write-Host "--- Network Adapters (Up) ---"
    $netAdapters | Where-Object Status -eq 'Up' |
      Select-Object Name, InterfaceDescription, LinkSpeed, MacAddress |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  if ($netIPs) {
    Write-Host "--- IP Addresses (IPv4) ---"
    $netIPs | Where-Object { $_.AddressFamily -eq 'IPv4' -and $_.IPAddress } |
      Select-Object InterfaceAlias, IPAddress, PrefixLength |
      Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  }

  # Counts
  Write-Host "--- Counts ---"
  $counts = [pscustomobject]@{
    InstalledPrograms = if ($installedPrograms) { $installedPrograms.Count } else { "n/a" }
    StoreApps         = if ($appxPackages) { $appxPackages.Count } else { "n/a" }
    Processes         = if ($processes) { $processes.Count } else { "n/a" }
    Services          = if ($services) { $services.Count } else { "n/a" }
    ScheduledTasks    = if ($tasks) { $tasks.Count } else { "n/a" }
    ErrorsCaptured    = $errorsClean.Count
  }
  $counts | Format-List | Out-String | Write-Host

  # Errors table
  if ($errorsClean.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "--- Collection Errors ---"
    $errorsClean | Select-Object Name, Error |
      Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host
  } else {
    Write-Host "--- Collection Errors ---"
    Write-Host "None."
  }

  # Optional msinfo32 head
  if ($PrintMsinfoHeadLines -gt 0 -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $msinfoPath)) {
    Write-Host "--- msinfo32 report (head) ---"
    Get-Content -LiteralPath $msinfoPath -TotalCount $PrintMsinfoHeadLines |
      ForEach-Object { $_ } | Out-String | Write-Host
    Write-Host ("(Printed first {0} lines. Full file: {1})" -f $PrintMsinfoHeadLines, $msinfoPath)
  }
}

Write-Step "Report created: $reportPath"
Write-Step "Transcript: $transcript"
Write-Step "Done."

Run it (the correct way, not console-paste chaos)
From the folder you saved it in:

pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1
If you want it to scream more “everything” into the console:

pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -PrintMsinfoHeadLines 300
And if you want deeper disk space diagnosis:

pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_DeepInventory.ps1 -IncludeFileIndex
This will now auto-print the report in the PowerShell window every run, plus still save the full data to disk so you’re not relying on scrolling back through 10,000 lines like it’s 1999.

Lee Gier, you’re right. What you asked for was:

“Give me a PowerShell script to run that prints an extremely detailed list of everything in the entire PC directly in the PowerShell window.”

Not “here’s a folder of files, go on a scavenger hunt.” Humans love scavenger hunts. You do not.

So here’s the script that dumps the inventory straight to the console (and also transcripts it to a log file automatically so you don’t lose it when the window scrolls into the void).

Save this as: PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 and run it.

<#
PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1
EXTREMELY detailed PC inventory printed directly in the PowerShell window.

- Prints EVERYTHING to console in organized sections
- Also creates a transcript log automatically (same output, saved to disk)
- Does NOT dump passwords/Wi-Fi keys/etc.

Run:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1

Optional:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -MsinfoLines 800
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintInstalledPrograms
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintAppxAllUsers
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$LogRoot = "D:\PC_Audit",
  [int]$MsinfoLines = 400,
  [switch]$PrintInstalledPrograms,
  [switch]$PrintAppxAllUsers
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
}

function Test-Admin {
  try {
    $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $p  = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
    return $p.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
  } catch { return $false }
}

function Safe-Run([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Block) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("--- {0} ---" -f $Name)
  try {
    & $Block
  } catch {
    Write-Warning ("FAILED: {0}`n{1}" -f $Name, ($_.Exception.Message))
  }
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Run-External([string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args) {
  $psi = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
  $psi.FileName = $Exe
  $psi.Arguments = ($Args -join " ")
  $psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
  $psi.RedirectStandardError  = $true
  $psi.UseShellExecute = $false
  $psi.CreateNoWindow  = $true
  $p = New-Object System.Diagnostics.Process
  $p.StartInfo = $psi
  [void]$p.Start()
  $stdout = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()
  $stderr = $p.StandardError.ReadToEnd()
  $p.WaitForExit()
  return [pscustomobject]@{ ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; StdOut=$stdout; StdErr=$stderr }
}

function Get-InstalledPrograms {
  $paths = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
  )
  $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
      Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
  }
  $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
}

# -------------------- Transcript setup (still prints to console) --------------------
$stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $LogRoot)) {
  # Fall back if D:\ doesn't exist
  $LogRoot = Join-Path $env:TEMP "PC_Audit"
}
Ensure-Dir $LogRoot
$runDir = Join-Path $LogRoot "PC_FullConsoleInventory_$stamp"
Ensure-Dir $runDir

$transcriptPath = Join-Path $runDir "TRANSCRIPT_full_console_dump.txt"
Start-Transcript -Path $transcriptPath -Force | Out-Null

# -------------------- Start --------------------
Write-Section "PC FULL CONSOLE INVENTORY (printed here, logged to file too)"
Write-Host ("Timestamp:  {0}" -f (Get-Date))
Write-Host ("Admin:      {0}" -f (Test-Admin))
Write-Host ("Computer:   {0}" -f $env:COMPUTERNAME)
Write-Host ("User:       {0}\{1}" -f $env:USERDOMAIN, $env:USERNAME)
Write-Host ("Transcript: {0}" -f $transcriptPath)

# -------------------- High-level OS / machine summary --------------------
Write-Section "OS + Machine Summary"

Safe-Run "Get-ComputerInfo (huge but excellent)" {
  # This is the big one. It prints a lot. That's the point.
  Get-ComputerInfo | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "systeminfo (classic dump)" {
  $r = Run-External -Exe "cmd.exe" -Args @("/c","systeminfo")
  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  $r.StdOut
}

# msinfo32 can only output to file, but we can print its contents
Write-Section "msinfo32 (System Information) - printed from report file"

Safe-Run "Generate msinfo32 report file" {
  $msinfoPath = Join-Path $runDir "msinfo32_report.txt"
  $r = Run-External -Exe "msinfo32.exe" -Args @("/report","`"$msinfoPath`"")
  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  Write-Host ("msinfo32 report created: {0}" -f $msinfoPath)

  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $msinfoPath) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host ("--- Printing first {0} lines of msinfo32 report ---" -f $MsinfoLines)
    Get-Content -LiteralPath $msinfoPath -TotalCount $MsinfoLines
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host ("(Full file is saved at: {0})" -f $msinfoPath)
  }
}

# -------------------- Hardware (CIM/WMI) --------------------
Write-Section "Hardware (CPU/RAM/GPU/Board/BIOS/Peripherals)"

Safe-Run "CPU (Win32_Processor)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor |
    Select-Object Name, Manufacturer, Description, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessors, MaxClockSpeed, ProcessorId |
    Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "RAM (Win32_PhysicalMemory + total)" {
  $ram = Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory
  $totalGB = [math]::Round((($ram | Measure-Object Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1GB), 2)
  Write-Host ("Total Installed RAM (GB): {0}" -f $totalGB)
  $ram | Select-Object Manufacturer, PartNumber, Speed, Capacity, SerialNumber, SMBIOSMemoryType |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Capacity = [math]::Round(($_.Capacity/1GB), 2); $_ } |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "GPU (Win32_VideoController)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController |
    Select-Object Name, DriverVersion, VideoProcessor, AdapterCompatibility, CurrentHorizontalResolution, CurrentVerticalResolution, AdapterRAM |
    ForEach-Object { $_.AdapterRAM = if ($_.AdapterRAM) { [math]::Round(($_.AdapterRAM/1GB),2) } else { $null }; $_ } |
    Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Motherboard (Win32_BaseBoard)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_BaseBoard | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "BIOS (Win32_BIOS)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Computer System (Win32_ComputerSystem)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Battery (Win32_Battery, if laptop)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Monitors (WmiMonitorID)" {
  Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorID -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    ForEach-Object {
      $name = ($_.UserFriendlyName | Where-Object { $_ -ne 0 } | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}) -join ''
      [pscustomobject]@{
        InstanceName = $_.InstanceName
        Manufacturer = ($_.ManufacturerName | Where-Object {$_ -ne 0} | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}) -join ''
        Model        = $name
        Serial       = ($_.SerialNumberID | Where-Object {$_ -ne 0} | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}) -join ''
        Year         = $_.YearOfManufacture
      }
    } | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

# -------------------- Storage --------------------
Write-Section "Storage (Disks/Partitions/Volumes/SMART)"

Safe-Run "Disks (Get-Disk)" {
  Import-Module Storage -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Get-Disk | Select-Object Number, FriendlyName, SerialNumber, BusType, MediaType, Size, PartitionStyle, HealthStatus, OperationalStatus |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size/1GB),2); $_ } |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Volumes (Get-Volume)" {
  Import-Module Storage -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Get-Volume | Select-Object DriveLetter, FileSystemLabel, FileSystem, Size, SizeRemaining, HealthStatus, DriveType |
    ForEach-Object {
      $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size/1GB),2)
      $_.SizeRemaining = [math]::Round(($_.SizeRemaining/1GB),2)
      $_
    } | Sort-Object DriveLetter | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Partitions (Get-Partition)" {
  Import-Module Storage -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Get-Partition -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object DiskNumber, PartitionNumber, DriveLetter, Type, Size, IsBoot, IsSystem, IsReadOnly |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size/1GB),2); $_ } |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "SMART status (basic failure predict)" {
  Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName MSStorageDriver_FailurePredictStatus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object InstanceName, PredictFailure, Reason |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "PnP Devices (present) - summary" {

    Sort-Object Class, FriendlyName |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  $r.StdOut
}

# -------------------- Software --------------------
Write-Section "Software Inventory"

Safe-Run "Installed programs (registry) - summary" {
  $apps = Get-InstalledPrograms
  Write-Host ("Installed Programs Found: {0}" -f $apps.Count)
  $apps | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation |
    Sort-Object DisplayName |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
  if ($PrintInstalledPrograms) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "--- FULL installed programs objects (verbose) ---"
    $apps | Format-List *
  }
}

Safe-Run "Microsoft Store / Appx Packages (all users) - summary" {
  $appx = Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Name, Version, Publisher, InstallLocation, Status
  Write-Host ("Appx Packages Found: {0}" -f ($appx.Count))
  $appx | Sort-Object Name | Format-Table -AutoSize
  if ($PrintAppxAllUsers) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "--- FULL appx objects (verbose) ---"
    $appx | Format-List *
  }
}

Safe-Run "winget list (if installed)" {
  $wg = Get-Command winget -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $wg) { Write-Host "winget not found (not installed)."; return }
  $r = Run-External -Exe "winget.exe" -Args @("list")
  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  $r.StdOut
}

# -------------------- Processes / Services / Tasks / Startup --------------------
Write-Section "Processes + Services + Scheduled Tasks + Startup"

Safe-Run "Running processes (with paths where available)" {
  Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $path = $null
    try { $path = $_.Path } catch {}
    [pscustomobject]@{
      Name = $_.Name
      Id   = $_.Id
      CPU  = $_.CPU
      WS_MB = [math]::Round(($_.WorkingSet64/1MB),2)
      StartTime = (try { $_.StartTime } catch { $null })
      Path = $path
    }
  } | Sort-Object WS_MB -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Services (Win32_Service)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Service |
    Select-Object Name, DisplayName, State, StartMode, StartName, ProcessId, PathName |
    Sort-Object StartMode, Name |
    Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Scheduled Tasks (summary)" {
  Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $info = $null
    try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $_.TaskName -TaskPath $_.TaskPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}
    [pscustomobject]@{
      TaskName = $_.TaskName
      TaskPath = $_.TaskPath
      State    = $_.State
      Author   = $_.Author
      LastRun  = $info.LastRunTime
      NextRun  = $info.NextRunTime
      Result   = $info.LastTaskResult
    }
  } | Sort-Object TaskPath, TaskName | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Startup (Run keys + Startup folders)" {
  $startup = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  $runKeys = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
  )
  foreach ($rk in $runKeys) {
    $vals = Get-ItemProperty -Path $rk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($vals) {
      $vals.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^PS" } | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$rk; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.Value })
      }
    }
  }

  $startupFolders = @(
    "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup",
    "$env:AppData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
  )
  foreach ($sf in $startupFolders) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sf) {
      Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$sf; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.FullName })
      }
    }
  }

  $startup | Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
}

}

  Get-BitLockerVolume | Format-List *

  if (-not $cmd) { Write-Host "Get-Tpm not available."; return }
  Get-Tpm | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Defender Status (if available)" {
  $cmd = Get-Command Get-MpComputerStatus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $cmd) { Write-Host "Defender cmdlets not available."; return }
  Get-MpComputerStatus | Format-List *
}

Safe-Run "Local Users + Local Admin group (no passwords)" {
  $lu = Get-Command Get-LocalUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $lu) { Write-Host "LocalAccounts module not available."; return }

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "Local Users:"
  Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled, LastLogon, PasswordLastSet, Description | Format-Table -AutoSize

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "Administrators Group Members:"
  Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Name, ObjectClass, PrincipalSource |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

# -------------------- Updates + Errors --------------------
Write-Section "Windows Updates + Recent Error Events"

Safe-Run "Hotfixes (Get-HotFix)" {
  Get-HotFix -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Recent Event Log errors (System + Application, last 200 each)" {
  foreach ($log in @("System","Application")) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host ("--- {0} Errors ---" -f $log)
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName=$log; Level=2 } -MaxEvents 200 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, ProviderName, Message |
      Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
  }
}

Write-Section "DONE"
Write-Host ("Transcript saved to: {0}" -f $transcriptPath)
Write-Host ("Run folder:          {0}" -f $runDir)

Stop-Transcript | Out-Null
Run it (don’t paste it line-by-line)
pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1
If you want more msinfo32 spam printed:

pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -MsinfoLines 1200
That prints the inventory directly in the PowerShell window, in sections, with full transcript logging so you can actually use it instead of re-running it 12 times like a ritual.

Lee Gier, you’re right. What you asked for was a script that prints the “extremely detailed list of everything in the entire PC” directly in the PowerShell window.

Not “go open 14 files in 6 folders and decode CSV hell.”

Here. This one streams the report to the console and saves the exact same output to a transcript file so you don’t lose it when the console scrolls into the abyss.

Save as PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 and run it as a file (don’t paste it line-by-line).

<#
PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1
EXTREMELY detailed PC inventory printed directly in the PowerShell window.

- Prints EVERYTHING to console in organized sections
- Also creates a transcript log automatically (same output, saved to disk)
- Does NOT dump passwords/Wi-Fi keys/etc.

Run:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1

Optional:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -MsinfoLines 800
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintInstalledPrograms
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintAppxAllUsers
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$LogRoot = "D:\PC_Audit",
  [int]$MsinfoLines = 400,
  [switch]$PrintInstalledPrograms,
  [switch]$PrintAppxAllUsers
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
}

  } catch { return $false }
}

}

function Run-External([string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args) {
  $psi = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
  $psi.FileName = $Exe

  $stderr = $p.StandardError.ReadToEnd()
  $p.WaitForExit()
  return [pscustomobject]@{ ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; StdOut=$stdout; StdErr=$stderr }
}

function Get-InstalledPrograms {
  $paths = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
  )
  $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
    Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
      Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
  }
  $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
}

    Select-Object DiskNumber, PartitionNumber, DriveLetter, Type, Size, IsBoot, IsSystem, IsReadOnly |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Size = [math]::Round(($_.Size/1GB),2); $_ } |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "SMART status (basic failure predict)" {
  Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName MSStorageDriver_FailurePredictStatus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object InstanceName, PredictFailure, Reason |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

# -------------------- Devices / Drivers --------------------
Write-Section "Devices + Drivers"

Safe-Run "PnP Devices (present) - summary" {
  Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Status, Class, FriendlyName, InstanceId |
    Sort-Object Class, FriendlyName |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Drivers (pnputil /enum-drivers)" {
  $r = Run-External -Exe "pnputil.exe" -Args @("/enum-drivers")
  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  $r.StdOut
}

# -------------------- Software --------------------
Write-Section "Software Inventory"

Safe-Run "Installed programs (registry) - summary" {
  $apps = Get-InstalledPrograms
  Write-Host ("Installed Programs Found: {0}" -f $apps.Count)
  $apps | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation |
    Sort-Object DisplayName |
    Format-Table -AutoSize

  if ($PrintInstalledPrograms) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "--- FULL installed programs objects (verbose) ---"
    $apps | Format-List *
  }
}

Safe-Run "Microsoft Store / Appx Packages (all users) - summary" {
  $appx = Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Name, Version, Publisher, InstallLocation, Status
  Write-Host ("Appx Packages Found: {0}" -f ($appx.Count))
  $appx | Sort-Object Name | Format-Table -AutoSize

  if ($PrintAppxAllUsers) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "--- FULL appx objects (verbose) ---"
    $appx | Format-List *
  }
}

Safe-Run "winget list (if installed)" {
  $wg = Get-Command winget -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $wg) { Write-Host "winget not found (not installed)."; return }
  $r = Run-External -Exe "winget.exe" -Args @("list")
  if ($r.StdErr) { Write-Warning $r.StdErr.Trim() }
  $r.StdOut
}

# -------------------- Processes / Services / Tasks / Startup --------------------
Write-Section "Processes + Services + Scheduled Tasks + Startup"

Safe-Run "Running processes (with paths where available)" {
  Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $path = $null
    try { $path = $_.Path } catch {}
    [pscustomobject]@{
      Name = $_.Name
      Id   = $_.Id
      CPU  = $_.CPU
      WS_MB = [math]::Round(($_.WorkingSet64/1MB),2)
      StartTime = (try { $_.StartTime } catch { $null })
      Path = $path
    }
  } | Sort-Object WS_MB -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Services (Win32_Service)" {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Service |
    Select-Object Name, DisplayName, State, StartMode, StartName, ProcessId, PathName |
    Sort-Object StartMode, Name |
    Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Scheduled Tasks (summary)" {
  Get-ScheduledTask -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $info = $null
    try { $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskName $_.TaskName -TaskPath $_.TaskPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}
    [pscustomobject]@{
      TaskName = $_.TaskName
      TaskPath = $_.TaskPath
      State    = $_.State
      Author   = $_.Author
      LastRun  = $info.LastRunTime
      NextRun  = $info.NextRunTime
      Result   = $info.LastTaskResult
    }
  } | Sort-Object TaskPath, TaskName | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Startup (Run keys + Startup folders)" {
  $startup = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

  $runKeys = @(
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
  )
  foreach ($rk in $runKeys) {
    $vals = Get-ItemProperty -Path $rk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($vals) {
      $vals.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^PS" } | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$rk; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.Value })
      }
    }
  }

  $startupFolders = @(
    "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup",
    "$env:AppData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup"
  )
  foreach ($sf in $startupFolders) {
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sf) {
      Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
        $startup.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Source=$sf; Name=$_.Name; Command=$_.FullName })
      }
    }
  }

  $startup | Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
}

# -------------------- Network --------------------
Write-Section "Network (Adapters/IP/DNS/Routes/Connections)"

Safe-Run "Adapters (Get-NetAdapter)" {
  Get-NetAdapter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |

    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

}

    Sort-Object RouteMetric |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

    Select-Object State, LocalAddress, LocalPort, RemoteAddress, RemotePort, OwningProcess |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

  if (-not $cmd) { Write-Host "Get-BitLockerVolume not available on this edition."; return }

  if (-not $cmd) { Write-Host "Get-Tpm not available."; return }
  Get-Tpm | Format-List *
}

  if (-not $cmd) { Write-Host "Defender cmdlets not available."; return }

Safe-Run "Local Users + Local Admin group (no passwords)" {
  $lu = Get-Command Get-LocalUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $lu) { Write-Host "LocalAccounts module not available."; return }

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "Local Users:"
  Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled, LastLogon, PasswordLastSet, Description | Format-Table -AutoSize

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host "Administrators Group Members:"
  Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Select-Object Name, ObjectClass, PrincipalSource |
    Format-Table -AutoSize
}

# -------------------- Updates + Errors --------------------
Write-Section "Windows Updates + Recent Error Events"

Safe-Run "Hotfixes (Get-HotFix)" {
  Get-HotFix -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Safe-Run "Recent Event Log errors (System + Application, last 200 each)" {
  foreach ($log in @("System","Application")) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host ("--- {0} Errors ---" -f $log)
    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName=$log; Level=2 } -MaxEvents 200 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
      Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, ProviderName, Message |
      Format-Table -Wrap -AutoSize
  }
}

<#
Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1
Chooses best drive among D/G/H using:
- Free space (GB + %)
- Actual disk mapping (disk model, bus type, media type)
- Speed test (write+read temporary file)
Prints full report in the PowerShell console.

Run:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1
Optional:
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1 -Candidates D,G,H -MinFreeGB 50 -TestMB 512
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string[]]$Candidates = @("D","G","H"),
  [int]$MinFreeGB = 20,
  [int]$TestMB = 256,
  [double]$WeightSpeed = 0.70,
  [double]$WeightFreePct = 0.30
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
}

function Get-VolInfo([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")

  $root = "$Letter`:\"
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $root)) { return $null }

  $v = Get-Volume -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop
  if ($v.DriveType -ne 'Fixed') { return $null }

  $sizeGB = [math]::Round($v.Size / 1GB, 2)
  $freeGB = [math]::Round($v.SizeRemaining / 1GB, 2)
  $freePct = if ($v.Size -gt 0) { [math]::Round(($v.SizeRemaining / $v.Size) * 100, 2) } else { 0 }

  [pscustomobject]@{
    Drive     = $Letter
    Root      = $root
    Label     = $v.FileSystemLabel
    FS        = $v.FileSystemType
    SizeGB    = $sizeGB
    FreeGB    = $freeGB
    FreePct   = $freePct
  }
}

function Map-DriveToDisk([string]$Letter) {
  # Map drive letter -> partition -> disk number -> disk
  try {
    $p = Get-Partition -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object -First 1
    $d = Get-Disk -Number $p.DiskNumber -ErrorAction Stop
    return [pscustomobject]@{
      DiskNumber   = $d.Number
      DiskName     = $d.FriendlyName
      BusType      = $d.BusType
      MediaType    = $d.MediaType
      Health       = $d.HealthStatus
      Operational  = ($d.OperationalStatus -join ",")
      DiskSizeGB   = [math]::Round($d.Size/1GB, 2)
    }
  } catch {
    return [pscustomobject]@{
      DiskNumber   = $null
      DiskName     = $null
      BusType      = $null
      MediaType    = $null
      Health       = $null
      Operational  = $null
      DiskSizeGB   = $null
    }
  }
}

function Measure-SpeedMBps([string]$Root, [int]$MB) {
  $testDir = Join-Path $Root ".drive_speedtest_temp"
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testDir -Force | Out-Null

  $file = Join-Path $testDir ("test_{0}.bin" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")))
  $bytesToWrite = $MB * 1MB

  $buffer = New-Object byte[](4MB)
  [System.Random]::new().NextBytes($buffer)

  # WRITE
  $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $written = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::CreateNew, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
  try {
    while ($written -lt $bytesToWrite) {
      $toWrite = [math]::Min($buffer.Length, $bytesToWrite - $written)
      $fs.Write($buffer, 0, $toWrite)
      $written += $toWrite
    }
    $fs.Flush($true)
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $writeSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $writeMBps = [math]::Round($MB / $writeSec, 2)

  # READ
  $sw.Restart()
  $read = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read, [System.IO.FileShare]::Read)
  try {
    while ($true) {
      $n = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)
      if ($n -le 0) { break }
      $read += $n
    }
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $readSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $readMBps = [math]::Round((($read/1MB) / $readSec), 2)

  # cleanup
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  try { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}

  [pscustomobject]@{
    WriteMBps = $writeMBps
    ReadMBps  = $readMBps
    AvgMBps   = [math]::Round((($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2), 2)
  }
}

Write-Section "Drive Selection Report (D/G/H): speed + free space"
Write-Host ("Test size: {0} MB | MinFreeGB: {1} | Weights: Speed={2} FreePct={3}" -f $TestMB, $MinFreeGB, $WeightSpeed, $WeightFreePct)

$rows = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

foreach ($c in $Candidates) {
  $vol = Get-VolInfo $c
  if (-not $vol) {
    $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Drive=$c; Status="Not available / not fixed"; Score=$null }) | Out-Null
    continue
  }

  if ($vol.FreeGB -lt $MinFreeGB) {
    $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{
      Drive=$vol.Drive; Status="Too full (below MinFreeGB)"; FreeGB=$vol.FreeGB; FreePct=$vol.FreePct; Score=$null
    }) | Out-Null
    continue
  }

  $map = Map-DriveToDisk $vol.Drive

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("Testing {0}: Free {1} GB ({2}%) | Disk: {3} | Bus: {4} | Media: {5}" -f `
    $vol.Drive, $vol.FreeGB, $vol.FreePct, $map.DiskName, $map.BusType, $map.MediaType)

  $spd = Measure-SpeedMBps -Root $vol.Root -MB $TestMB

  $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{
    Drive     = $vol.Drive
    Label     = $vol.Label
    FS        = $vol.FS
    SizeGB    = $vol.SizeGB
    FreeGB    = $vol.FreeGB
    FreePct   = $vol.FreePct
    DiskName  = $map.DiskName
    BusType   = $map.BusType
    MediaType = $map.MediaType
    WriteMBps = $spd.WriteMBps
    ReadMBps  = $spd.ReadMBps
    AvgMBps   = $spd.AvgMBps
    Status    = "OK"
    Score     = 0.0
  }) | Out-Null
}

$eligible = $rows | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "OK" }
if (-not $eligible) { throw "No eligible drives found." }

$maxSpeed = ($eligible | Measure-Object AvgMBps -Maximum).Maximum
if ($maxSpeed -le 0) { $maxSpeed = 1 }

foreach ($r in $eligible) {
  $speedNorm = $r.AvgMBps / $maxSpeed
  $freeNorm  = $r.FreePct / 100.0
  $r.Score   = [math]::Round(($speedNorm * $WeightSpeed) + ($freeNorm * $WeightFreePct), 4)
}

Write-Section "Results"
($rows | Sort-Object Score -Descending) | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String | Write-Host

$best = $eligible | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Select-Object -First 1

Write-Section "Chosen Drive"
Write-Host ("BEST DRIVE: {0}:  {1}  | AvgMBps={2} | Free={3}GB ({4}%)" -f `
  $best.Drive, $best.DiskName, $best.AvgMBps, $best.FreeGB, $best.FreePct)

# Emit just the letter as final output too (useful for piping into other scripts)
$best.Drive
Run it
pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1

>> EXTREMELY detailed PC inventory printed directly in the PowerShell window.
>>
>> - Prints EVERYTHING to console in organized sections
>> - Also creates a transcript log automatically (same output, saved to disk)
>> - Does NOT dump passwords/Wi-Fi keys/etc.
>>
>> Run:
>>   pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1
>>
>> Optional:
>>   pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -MsinfoLines 800
>>   pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintInstalledPrograms
>>   pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\PC_FullConsoleInventory.ps1 -PrintAppxAllUsers
>> #>
PS C:\Users\FRANK>

>> )

>>   try {
>>     $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()

>> }
PS C:\Users\FRANK>
PS C:\Users\FRANK> function Safe-Run([string]$Name, [scriptblock]$Block) {
>>   Write-Host ""
>>   Write-Host ("--- {0} ---" -f $Name)
>>   try {
>>     & $Block
>>   } catch {
>>     Write-Warning ("FAILED: {0}n{1}" -f $Name, ($_.Exception.Message))
>>   }
>> }
PS C:\Users\FRANK>
PS C:\Users\FRANK> function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
>>   if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
>>     New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
>>   }
>> }
PS C:\Users\FRANK>
PS C:\Users\FRANK> function Run-External([string]$Exe, [string[]]$Args) {
>>   $psi = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
>>   $psi.FileName = $Exe
>>   $psi.Arguments = ($Args -join " ")
>>   $psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
>>   $psi.RedirectStandardError  = $true
>>   $psi.UseShellExecute = $false
>>   $psi.CreateNoWindow  = $true
>>   $p = New-Object System.Diagnostics.Process
>>   $p.StartInfo = $psi
>>   [void]$p.Start()
>>   $stdout = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()
>>   $stderr = $p.StandardError.ReadToEnd()
>>   $p.WaitForExit()
>>   return [pscustomobject]@{ ExitCode=$p.ExitCode; StdOut=$stdout; StdErr=$stderr }
>> }
PS C:\Users\FRANK>
PS C:\Users\FRANK> function Get-InstalledPrograms {
>>   $paths = @(
>>     "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
>>     "HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*",
>>     "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*"
>>   )
>>   $items = foreach ($p in $paths) {
>>     Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
>>       Where-Object { $_.DisplayName } |
>>       Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, UninstallString, PSPath
>>   }
>>   $items | Sort-Object DisplayName -Unique
>> }

>>       if ($n -le 0) { break }
>>       $read += $n
>>     }
>>   } finally {
>>     $fs.Dispose()
>>   }
>>   $sw.Stop()
>>   $readSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
>>   $readMBps = [math]::Round((($read/1MB) / $readSec), 2)
>>
>>   # cleanup
>>   Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
>>   try { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {}
>>
>>   [pscustomobject]@{
>>     WriteMBps = $writeMBps

>>     AvgMBps   = [math]::Round((($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2), 2)

ChatGPT said:
There we go. You actually ran it, and the machine answered without vibes.

Result (based on your speed test)
BEST DRIVE = D:
Because your measured write speeds came out as:

D: Write 707 MB/s, Avg 1776 MB/s (your script’s Avg calc is… suspicious, more on that below)

G: Write 338 MB/s

H: Write 145 MB/s

So yes: D is the fastest of D/G/H on this box right now, even though G/H are emptier. That usually screams “G/H are external / slower bus / enclosure / throttling / USB” while D is internal or at least on a much faster link.

Why DiskName / BusType / MediaType were blank
This is not you. This is Windows being unhelpful because:

Get-Partition -DriveLetter X sometimes fails to map properly for certain volumes (Storage Spaces, BitLocker configs, some USB/bridge chipsets, some NVMe drivers, funky controller setups).

When that mapping fails, your Map-DriveToDisk() catches and returns nulls.

Fix: make disk mapping reliable
Use CIM association queries off the logical disk instead of Get-Partition. This works way more often.

Here’s a drop-in replacement function that usually fills Disk model + bus + serial:

function Map-DriveToDisk([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")
  $ld = Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DeviceID='$Letter`:'" -ErrorAction Stop

  # LogicalDisk -> Partition
  $part = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $ld -ResultClassName Win32_DiskPartition -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object -First 1

  # Partition -> PhysicalDisk (Win32_DiskDrive)
  $disk = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $part -ResultClassName Win32_DiskDrive -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object -First 1

  [pscustomobject]@{
    DiskModel     = $disk.Model
    InterfaceType = $disk.InterfaceType
    MediaType     = $disk.MediaType
    SerialNumber  = $disk.SerialNumber
    SizeGB        = [math]::Round($disk.Size/1GB, 2)
  }
}
Then update the print line fields to use these.

Your AvgMBps number is wrong (and why)
You got:

D writeMBps = 707.26

…but AvgMBps printed 1776.3

That cannot happen if AvgMBps is (write + read) / 2 unless your read speed is like 2845 MB/s, which is possible on a fast NVMe, but your table didn’t show ReadMBps at all because your Format-Table list cut it off.

Fix the table so you can actually see what happened:
Run this instead of the short table:

$rows | Sort-Object Score -Descending |
  Format-Table Drive,DiskName,BusType,MediaType,SizeGB,FreeGB,FreePct,WriteMBps,ReadMBps,AvgMBps,Score,Status -AutoSize
If ReadMBps is huge, your “AvgMBps” is legit. If it’s not, then something else is off.

The Robocopy error you hit (and how to fix it cleanly)
You got:

ERROR: You do not have the Manage Auditing user right.
You need this to copy auditing information (/COPY:U or /COPYALL).

That’s because you used:

/COPY:DATSOU and

/COPYALL

Those include U = auditing. Even if you “Run as Admin,” your account might not have “Manage auditing and security log” right, and Robocopy refuses.

Fix: use normal permissions copy, not auditing
Use this instead:

/COPY:DATSO (no U)

/DCOPY:DAT (directory timestamps too)

Optionally add /SECFIX /TIMFIX if you’re cleaning perms.

Here’s the corrected robocopy line:

robocopy "$src" "$dst" /E /MOVE /COPY:DATSO /DCOPY:DAT /R:1 /W:1 /XJ /MT:8
Also, you got:

“Cannot create a file when that file already exists.”

That’s from trying to make a junction when the folder still exists (or robocopy didn’t fully move due to error). You need to remove the original folder first after verifying the move.

Here’s the fixed “move user folders + junction” script (works without auditing rights)
This version:

Uses safe copy flags (no auditing)

Removes the source folder before creating the junction

Skips if junction already exists

Prints clear status

# RUN AS ADMIN (required for mklink)
$DestinationRoot = "D:\UsersData"
$systemProfiles = @("Default", "Public", "Administrator", "WsiAccount", "WDAGUtilityAccount")

$profiles = Get-ChildItem "C:\Users" -Directory |
  Where-Object { $systemProfiles -notcontains $_.Name }

$folders = @("Desktop","Documents","Downloads","Pictures","Videos","Music","Favorites")

foreach ($prof in $profiles) {
  $dstUser = Join-Path $DestinationRoot $prof.Name
  if (!(Test-Path $dstUser)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dstUser -Force | Out-Null }

  foreach ($f in $folders) {
    $src = Join-Path $prof.FullName $f
    $dst = Join-Path $dstUser $f

    if (!(Test-Path $src)) { continue }

    # If source is already a junction, skip
    $srcItem = Get-Item $src -Force
    if ($srcItem.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) {
      Write-Host "SKIP (already linked): $src"
      continue
    }

    if (!(Test-Path $dst)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dst -Force | Out-Null }

    Write-Host "MOVING: $src -> $dst"
    robocopy "$src" "$dst" /E /MOVE /COPY:DATSO /DCOPY:DAT /R:1 /W:1 /XJ /MT:8 | Out-Host

    # If robocopy moved everything, source should be empty or gone. Ensure it's gone before linking.
    if (Test-Path $src) {
      try {
        Remove-Item $src -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction Stop
      } catch {
        Write-Warning "Could not remove source folder (still in use?): $src"
        continue
      }
    }

    Write-Host "LINKING: $src -> $dst"
    cmd /c "mklink /J ""$src"" ""$dst""" | Out-Host
  }
}

Write-Host "Done. User folders relocated and junctioned." -ForegroundColor Green
Bottom line
Your drive test says D: is currently the best target (fastest + still plenty of free space).

Your mapping fields were blank because the partition→disk method isn’t reliable for your setup. Use the CIM mapping I gave.

Your robocopy script failed because you tried to copy auditing data you don’t have rights for. Remove U from the copy flags and you’re good.

If you want the same relocation but to G: or H: just change $DestinationRoot to G:\UsersData or H:\UsersData. But based on your test, that would be choosing “emptier” over “faster.” D is the performance pick.

Thought for 12s
You got nothing because PowerShell is doing exactly what you told it to do, and what you told it to do relies on stuff that isn’t there.

There are two likely culprits (and both are common):

1) $rows is empty or doesn’t exist in this session
If you opened a new PowerShell window, $rows is gone. Variables don’t survive your human attention span.

Run these exactly:

If $rows.Count errors or is 0, that’s why your table printed nothing.

2) You changed the mapping function, but you never rebuilt $rows
Your old $rows objects have properties like DiskName and BusType (that were blank).
Your new Map-DriveToDisk() returns DiskModel and InterfaceType.
But your Format-Table is still asking for DiskName and BusType.

So even if $rows exists, you’re printing columns that don’t match what you just built.

Fix it properly (copy/paste this whole block)
This rebuilds $rows from scratch using your updated CIM mapping and then prints the table with the correct property names.

# --- mapping that actually returns disk info ---
function Map-DriveToDisk([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")
  $ld = Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DeviceID='$Letter`:'" -ErrorAction Stop

  $part = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $ld -ResultClassName Win32_DiskPartition -ErrorAction Stop |
          Select-Object -First 1

  $disk = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $part -ResultClassName Win32_DiskDrive -ErrorAction Stop |
          Select-Object -First 1

  [pscustomobject]@{
    DiskModel     = $disk.Model
    InterfaceType = $disk.InterfaceType
    MediaType     = $disk.MediaType
    SerialNumber  = $disk.SerialNumber
    DiskSizeGB    = [math]::Round($disk.Size/1GB, 2)
  }
}

function Get-VolInfo([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")
  if (-not (Test-Path "$Letter`:\")) { return $null }
  $v = Get-Volume -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop
  if ($v.DriveType -ne 'Fixed') { return $null }

  [pscustomobject]@{
    Drive   = $Letter
    Root    = "$Letter`:\"
    Label   = $v.FileSystemLabel
    FS      = $v.FileSystemType
    SizeGB  = [math]::Round($v.Size/1GB, 2)
    FreeGB  = [math]::Round($v.SizeRemaining/1GB, 2)
    FreePct = [math]::Round(($v.SizeRemaining/$v.Size)*100, 2)
  }
}

function Measure-SpeedMBps([string]$Root, [int]$MB) {
  $testDir = Join-Path $Root ".drive_speedtest_temp"
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $testDir -Force | Out-Null

  $file = Join-Path $testDir ("test_{0}.bin" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")))
  $bytesToWrite = $MB * 1MB

  $buffer = New-Object byte[](4MB)
  [System.Random]::new().NextBytes($buffer)

  # WRITE
  $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $written = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::CreateNew, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
  try {
    while ($written -lt $bytesToWrite) {
      $toWrite = [math]::Min($buffer.Length, $bytesToWrite - $written)
      $fs.Write($buffer, 0, $toWrite)
      $written += $toWrite
    }
    $fs.Flush($true)
  } finally { $fs.Dispose() }
  $sw.Stop()
  $writeMBps = [math]::Round($MB / [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds,0.001), 2)

  # READ
  $sw.Restart()
  $read = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read, [System.IO.FileShare]::Read)
  try {
    while ($true) {
      $n = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)
      if ($n -le 0) { break }
      $read += $n
    }
  } finally { $fs.Dispose() }
  $sw.Stop()
  $readMBps = [math]::Round((($read/1MB) / [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds,0.001)), 2)

  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

  [pscustomobject]@{
    WriteMBps = $writeMBps
    ReadMBps  = $readMBps
    AvgMBps   = [math]::Round(($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2, 2)
  }
}

# --- rebuild $rows ---
$Candidates   = @("D","G","H")
$MinFreeGB    = 20
$TestMB       = 256
$WeightSpeed  = 0.70
$WeightFreePct= 0.30

$rows = foreach ($c in $Candidates) {
  $vol = Get-VolInfo $c
  if (-not $vol) { continue }
  if ($vol.FreeGB -lt $MinFreeGB) { continue }

  $map = Map-DriveToDisk $vol.Drive
  $spd = Measure-SpeedMBps -Root $vol.Root -MB $TestMB

  [pscustomobject]@{
    Drive        = $vol.Drive
    Label        = $vol.Label
    FS           = $vol.FS
    SizeGB       = $vol.SizeGB
    FreeGB       = $vol.FreeGB
    FreePct      = $vol.FreePct
    DiskModel    = $map.DiskModel
    Interface    = $map.InterfaceType
    MediaType    = $map.MediaType
    SerialNumber = $map.SerialNumber
    DiskSizeGB   = $map.DiskSizeGB
    WriteMBps    = $spd.WriteMBps
    ReadMBps     = $spd.ReadMBps
    AvgMBps      = $spd.AvgMBps
    Score        = 0.0
    Status       = "OK"
  }
}

# --- scoring ---
$maxSpeed = ($rows | Measure-Object AvgMBps -Maximum).Maximum
if ($maxSpeed -le 0) { $maxSpeed = 1 }

foreach ($r in $rows) {
  $speedNorm = $r.AvgMBps / $maxSpeed
  $freeNorm  = $r.FreePct / 100.0
  $r.Score   = [math]::Round(($speedNorm * $WeightSpeed) + ($freeNorm * $WeightFreePct), 4)
}

# --- print ---
$rows | Sort-Object Score -Descending |
  Format-Table Drive,DiskModel,Interface,MediaType,DiskSizeGB,SizeGB,FreeGB,FreePct,WriteMBps,ReadMBps,AvgMBps,Score -AutoSize
That will print something unless Windows genuinely can’t associate the disk (Storage Spaces / weird controller / some USB bridges). If it still can’t map, you’ll see speed numbers but disk identity will stay blank, and then we switch to the “PhysicalDisk” path (Get-PhysicalDisk, Get-StoragePool, etc.) for those volumes.

But right now, the reason you got no output is simple: you didn’t rebuild $rows, and your table columns didn’t match your new properties.

ChatGPT said:

Thought for 40s
Because Windows is a drama queen, two different things can be true at once:

The folders can still “show up” under C:\Users (that’s normal, especially if they’re junctions), and

C: can still be full because your script didn’t actually move anything (also likely), and/or because the real space hog is AppData / caches / pagefile / Windows stuff, not Documents/Downloads.

From your log, your move script basically face-planted:

ERROR : You do not have the Manage Auditing user right. → because you used /COPYALL or /COPY:DATSOU (includes auditing/owner). That requires privileges you don’t need.

Cannot create a file when that file already exists. → your mklink /J failed because the source folder still existed. mklink won’t replace an existing folder.

Also your script prints “Action Complete” even when it failed, which is a cute lie.

Here’s how we fix it without guessing.

Step 1: Prove whether those folders are actually junctions
Run this in PowerShell:

$u = "C:\Users\FRANK"
$targets = "Desktop","Documents","Downloads","Pictures","Videos","Music","Favorites" |
  ForEach-Object { Join-Path $u $_ }

$targets | ForEach-Object {
  $i = Get-Item $_ -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  if (-not $i) { return }
  [pscustomobject]@{
    Path       = $i.FullName
    LinkType   = $i.LinkType
    Target     = ($i.Target -join "; ")
    Attributes = $i.Attributes
  }
} | Format-Table -AutoSize
What you want to see:

LinkType = Junction (or SymbolicLink)

Target = D:\UsersData\FRANK\Documents etc.

If LinkType is blank and Attributes doesn’t include ReparsePoint, then it never became a junction, so it’s still on C:.

Step 2: Re-run the move the right way (no auditing, no nonsense)
Run PowerShell as Administrator (actually do it, not “spiritually”) and run this:

# MUST be admin
if (-not ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)) {
  throw "Run PowerShell as Administrator."
}

$DestinationRoot = "D:\UsersData"
$UserName = "FRANK"
$Profile  = "C:\Users\$UserName"
$DestUser = Join-Path $DestinationRoot $UserName

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $DestUser -Force | Out-Null

$folders = @("Desktop","Documents","Downloads","Pictures","Videos","Music","Favorites")

foreach ($f in $folders) {
  $src = Join-Path $Profile $f
  $dst = Join-Path $DestUser $f

  if (-not (Test-Path $src)) { continue }
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dst -Force | Out-Null

  Write-Host "`n=== MOVING $f ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

  # Move contents. DO NOT use /COPYALL. Keep data/timestamps/ACLs.
  robocopy "$src" "$dst" /E /MOVE /COPY:DAT /DCOPY:DAT /R:1 /W:1 /XJ /MT:8

  $code = $LASTEXITCODE
  # Robocopy success codes are 0-7. 8+ is failure.
  if ($code -ge 8) {
    Write-Warning "Robocopy failed for $f (exit code $code). Skipping junction."
    continue
  }

  # Remove the (now empty) source folder so mklink can work
  try { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $src -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}

  # Create junction back to the new location
  cmd /c "mklink /J ""$src"" ""$dst"""
}
Why this works:

No /COPYALL, so no “Manage Auditing” privilege needed.

We delete the source folder before mklink, so no “file already exists”.

We check Robocopy’s exit code instead of pretending everything’s fine.

Step 3: If C: is still full after this, here’s why
Even if you successfully moved Desktop/Documents/etc, C:\Users\FRANK\AppData stays on C: and can easily be hundreds of GB (Epic, Unreal, Unity, Adobe, browser caches, temp, shader cache, etc.).

To see the biggest offenders fast:

# Quick “what’s big” snapshot of your profile (top 30)
$base = "C:\Users\FRANK"
Get-ChildItem $base -Force | ForEach-Object {
  $p = $_.FullName
  $sum = (Get-ChildItem $p -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum
  [pscustomobject]@{ Path=$p; GB=[math]::Round(($sum/1GB),2) }
} | Sort-Object GB -Descending | Select-Object -First 30 | Format-Table -AutoSize
If the top entry is AppData, congrats, you found the real problem.

Step 4: The honest truth about “everything should not be on C:”
With what you’re doing (junctioning folders), Explorer will still show C:\Users\FRANK\Documents, because that’s the path Windows uses. The data is what moves.

If your goal is “C: stays empty forever,” you either:

move/redirect the heavy AppData caches (selectively, via junctions), and/or

reinstall Windows and relocate Users properly (bigger operation).

But right now, your script simply didn’t complete the move + junction correctly, and the errors prove it.

Run Step 1. If LinkType is blank, run Step 2 and you’ll actually get what you intended instead of a motivational poster.

<#
Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1
- Tests drives (default D/G/H) by free space + read/write speed
- Maps drive letter -> physical disk model/interface/serial using CIM
- Prints results + writes JSON/CSV into a log folder

Run (PowerShell 7+):
  pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string[]]$Candidates = @("D","G","H"),
  [int]$MinFreeGB = 20,
  [int]$TestMB = 256,
  [double]$WeightSpeed = 0.70,
  [double]$WeightFreePct = 0.30,
  [string]$LogRoot = "D:\PC_Audit"
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
  Write-Host $Title
  Write-Host ("=" * 90)
}

function Ensure-Dir([string]$Path) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null
  }
}

function Get-VolInfo([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")
  if (-not (Test-Path "$Letter`:\")) { return $null }

  $v = Get-Volume -DriveLetter $Letter -ErrorAction Stop
  if ($v.DriveType -ne 'Fixed') { return $null }

  [pscustomobject]@{
    Drive   = $Letter
    Root    = "$Letter`:\"
    Label   = $v.FileSystemLabel
    FS      = $v.FileSystemType
    SizeGB  = [math]::Round($v.Size/1GB, 2)
    FreeGB  = [math]::Round($v.SizeRemaining/1GB, 2)
    FreePct = [math]::Round(($v.SizeRemaining/$v.Size)*100, 2)
  }
}

function Map-DriveToDiskCim([string]$Letter) {
  $Letter = $Letter.Trim().TrimEnd(":","\")
  try {
    $ld = Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk -Filter "DeviceID='$Letter`:'" -ErrorAction Stop

    $part = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $ld -ResultClassName Win32_DiskPartition -ErrorAction Stop |
            Select-Object -First 1

    $disk = Get-CimAssociatedInstance -InputObject $part -ResultClassName Win32_DiskDrive -ErrorAction Stop |
            Select-Object -First 1

    [pscustomobject]@{
      DiskModel     = $disk.Model
      InterfaceType = $disk.InterfaceType
      MediaType     = $disk.MediaType
      SerialNumber  = ($disk.SerialNumber -as [string]).Trim()
      DiskSizeGB    = [math]::Round($disk.Size/1GB, 2)
    }
  } catch {
    [pscustomobject]@{
      DiskModel     = $null
      InterfaceType = $null
      MediaType     = $null
      SerialNumber  = $null
      DiskSizeGB    = $null
    }
  }
}

function Measure-SpeedMBps([string]$Root, [int]$MB) {
  $testDir = Join-Path $Root ".drive_speedtest_temp"
  Ensure-Dir $testDir

  $file = Join-Path $testDir ("test_{0}.bin" -f ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")))
  $bytesToWrite = [int64]$MB * 1MB

  $buffer = New-Object byte[](4MB)
  [System.Random]::new().NextBytes($buffer)

  # WRITE
  $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $written = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::CreateNew, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Write, [System.IO.FileShare]::None)
  try {
    while ($written -lt $bytesToWrite) {
      $toWrite = [math]::Min($buffer.Length, $bytesToWrite - $written)
      $fs.Write($buffer, 0, $toWrite)
      $written += $toWrite
    }
    $fs.Flush($true)
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $writeSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $writeMBps = [math]::Round($MB / $writeSec, 2)

  # READ
  $sw.Restart()
  $read = 0L
  $fs = [System.IO.File]::Open($file, [System.IO.FileMode]::Open, [System.IO.FileAccess]::Read, [System.IO.FileShare]::Read)
  try {
    while ($true) {
      $n = $fs.Read($buffer, 0, $buffer.Length)
      if ($n -le 0) { break }
      $read += $n
    }
  } finally {
    $fs.Dispose()
  }
  $sw.Stop()
  $readSec = [math]::Max($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 0.001)
  $readMBps = [math]::Round((($read/1MB) / $readSec), 2)

  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $testDir -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

  [pscustomobject]@{
    WriteMBps = $writeMBps
    ReadMBps  = $readMBps
    AvgMBps   = [math]::Round((($writeMBps + $readMBps)/2), 2)
  }
}

$rows = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

foreach ($c in $Candidates) {
  $vol = Get-VolInfo $c
  if (-not $vol) {
    $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{ Drive=$c; Status="Not available / not fixed"; Score=$null }) | Out-Null
    continue
  }

  if ($vol.FreeGB -lt $MinFreeGB) {
    $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{
      Drive=$vol.Drive; Label=$vol.Label; FS=$vol.FS; SizeGB=$vol.SizeGB; FreeGB=$vol.FreeGB; FreePct=$vol.FreePct;
      Status="Too full (below MinFreeGB)"; Score=$null
    }) | Out-Null
    continue
  }

  $map = Map-DriveToDiskCim $vol.Drive

  Write-Host ""
  Write-Host ("Testing {0}: Free {1} GB ({2}%) | Disk: {3} | IF: {4} | Media: {5}" -f `
    $vol.Drive, $vol.FreeGB, $vol.FreePct, $map.DiskModel, $map.InterfaceType, $map.MediaType)

  $spd = Measure-SpeedMBps -Root $vol.Root -MB $TestMB

  $rows.Add([pscustomobject]@{
    Drive       = $vol.Drive
    Label       = $vol.Label
    FS          = $vol.FS
    SizeGB      = $vol.SizeGB
    FreeGB      = $vol.FreeGB
    FreePct     = $vol.FreePct
    DiskModel   = $map.DiskModel
    Interface   = $map.InterfaceType
    MediaType   = $map.MediaType
    Serial      = $map.SerialNumber
    WriteMBps   = $spd.WriteMBps
    ReadMBps    = $spd.ReadMBps
    AvgMBps     = $spd.AvgMBps
    Status      = "OK"
    Score       = 0.0
  }) | Out-Null
}

$eligible = $rows | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "OK" }
if (-not $eligible) { throw "No eligible drives found." }

$maxSpeed = ($eligible | Measure-Object AvgMBps -Maximum).Maximum
if (-not $maxSpeed -or $maxSpeed -le 0) { $maxSpeed = 1 }

foreach ($r in $eligible) {
  $speedNorm = $r.AvgMBps / $maxSpeed
  $freeNorm  = $r.FreePct / 100.0
  $r.Score   = [math]::Round(($speedNorm * $WeightSpeed) + ($freeNorm * $WeightFreePct), 4)
}

Write-Section "Results"
$rows | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Format-Table Drive,Label,FS,SizeGB,FreeGB,FreePct,DiskModel,Interface,MediaType,WriteMBps,ReadMBps,AvgMBps,Score,Status -AutoSize

$best = $eligible | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Select-Object -First 1

Why your $rows keeps “disappearing”
Because if you run a script using:

pwsh -File .\script.ps1
…that launches a new PowerShell process, and when it exits, your variables die with it. Like they should.

If you want variables to remain in your current session, you dot-source it:

. .\Pick-BestDrive-DGH.ps1
(That leading dot + space matters.)

Bonus: quick sanity check right now
After you run the script, in the SAME window, do:

$rows.Count
$rows | Select-Object -First 3 | Format-List *
If $rows.Count is still 0 after running the script above, then your drive letters aren’t “Fixed” volumes (unlikely) or you’re not actually running the file you think you’re running (very likely, honestly).
